items.title: Sahara occidental : les États-Unis et la France activent la marche forcée de la reconfiguration de l’Afrique du Nord
items.description: Le Conseil de Sécurité de l’ONU se réunira à la fin de ce mois d'octobre pour voter, comme tous les ans, une résolution sur le Sahara Occidental et le mandat de la Minurso que les États-Unis et la France voudraient déjà réduire à un instrument de simple validation du plan d’autonomie marocain. Créée en avril 1991 pour surveiller notamment un cessez-le-feu entre le Polisario et le Maroc et obtenue suite à la demande pressante des alliés de Rabat, à savoir les Occidentaux et les États du Golfe alertés par la supériorité militaire des Sahraouis sur le terrain. Pour leur part, les dirigeants sahraouis étaient sceptiques sur la volonté du Maroc de s’engager sur la voie du référendum qui était, faut-il le rappeler, un préalable à l’acceptation de ce cessez-le-feu. L’Algérie y était d’ailleurs favorable malgré les réserves émises par les Sahraouis. La Minurso avait été appelée plus tard, et sans succès par beaucoup d’États, dont l’Algérie, à élargir son mandat aux questions des droits de l’homme au Sahara occidental à l’instar d’autres forces de maintien de la paix des Nations Unies. Dépouiller la Minurso de ses missions initiales au Sahara occidental Aujourd’hui, il est question de la dépouiller même de ses missions initiales d’organisation du référendum, de la renommer Minuso et de mettre fin à sa mission de maintien de la paix avant mai 2027. Pour sa part, l’envoyé personnel du SG de l’ONU pour le Sahara occidental, Staffan de Mistura , qui a du mal à maintenir les critères de neutralité, d’objectivité et d’égalité entre le Polisario et le Maroc, se voit renforcé et son mandat élargi à la recherche d’autres interlocuteurs sahraouis plus accommodants au sein de la diaspora ou encore dans les camps de réfugiés ( ?) aux côtés du Polisario que l’ONU reconnaît pourtant comme représentant légitime du peuple sahraoui. Cette démarche n’est en fait ni nouvelle ni surprenante dans la mesure où l’opération d’influence et de propagande lancée par quelques sénateurs américains cherche encore de nos jours à présenter le Polisario comme un groupe terroriste. L’objectif est d’accréditer un second représentant sahraoui déjà désigné, identifié, encouragé et reçu en juin dernier par les Ambassadeurs, représentants américain et français à l’ONU. L’Algérie est indirectement visée L’Algérie est indirectement visée pour être présentée comme un État soutenant un « groupe terroriste », un proxy de l’Iran et un pays hostile à Israël. Notre pays est soumis à un marchandage destiné surtout à convertir ses élites au pragmatisme d’ambiance pour trouver des vertus à la diplomatie transactionnelle du président Trump, dont les véritables conséquences sur notre région n'apparaîtront qu’à l’issue de son mandat. C’est là que réside tout le paradoxe de cette situation qui veut que l’Algérie et le Polisario assument le coût diplomatique du deal du rétablissement des relations diplomatiques entre le Maroc et Israël contre la reconnaissance par les USA du fait accompli au Sahara occidental le 10 décembre 2020. Quant à l’avenir des réfugiés sahraouis accueillis par l’Algérie, ils sont les victimes de l’occupation de leur terre depuis cinquante ans et doivent jouir à ce titre du droit inaliénable au retour et à l’expression de leur choix pour l’autodétermination. Les puissances occidentales du Conseil de sécurité leur proposent un financement international orienté vers des solutions individuelles et volontaires destinées – comme pour les Gazaouis – à faire de ces exilés involontaires des apatrides forcés. Dans cette perspective, une bien maigre compensation est proposée par l’Espagne pour réintégrer dans la nationalité espagnole une partie de ses administrés abandonnés en 1975 par un franquisme à l’agonie. La Quatrième Commission vient pourtant d'adresser un message très fort de la communauté internationale sur le droit des Sahraouis à l’autodétermination, car le cadre de cet appel, l’Assemblée générale des Nations unies, reste la véritable expression de la représentation des Nations et de l’égalité souveraine entre les États. Le Conseil de sécurité reste comme l’expression figée du rapport des forces militaires au lendemain de la Deuxième Guerre mondiale. Aujourd’hui, seules la Russie et la Chine s’efforcent de préserver un précaire équilibre dans un Conseil qui ne sera ni réformé de sitôt ni conforme à la réalité du monde qui émerge. Les trois pays occidentaux membres permanents du Conseil considèrent que le plan d’autonomie marocain est la seule base de négociation d’une « solution mutuellement acceptable », reste « la seule solution viable à la question sahraouie et que toute proposition devrait s’inscrire dans ce cadre ». Cette seule condition contraignante par nature, irrecevable par principe et irréalisable dans une négociation internationale, est à elle seule suffisante pour enlever tout crédit à la poursuite du processus actuel. Les États-Unis, qui ont le privilège de proposer le draft sur la question sahraouie, n'excluraient de prendre de « nouvelles mesures » qu’ils ne s'identifient pas encore à ce stade, « si les parties ne s’engagent pas de manière constructive dans le processus politique », selon des termes qui relèvent moins de la diplomatie du compromis que de l’arrogance que confèrent la puissance et l’immunité. Les Sahraouis sacrifiés Tout au long de ces cinq décennies, dont la durée est présentée par les Occidentaux comme un motif pour l’accélération du processus en cours, les seules victimes restent les Sahraouis que l’on veut insérer, depuis quarante ans, dans une nébuleuse sémantique « d’indépendance dans l’interdépendance », comme si le Maroc était un modèle de démocratie et le Sahara occidental, une terra nullius sans peuple et sans histoire. À ce titre, le président Abdelmadjid Tebboune avait tout à fait raison, il y a peu, de remettre la question du libre destin du peuple sahraoui au centre de tout processus. Sahara occidental : ce dont les Américains doivent tenir compte Les Américains, puisque c’est d’eux qu’il s’agit dans ce dossier, doivent tenir compte du fait que les dirigeants sahraouis n’ont ni la capacité ni le droit de décider du destin de leur peuple sans procéder au préalable à sa consultation directe, sans contrainte et sans ingérence étrangère. Le processus de règlement peut être long et passera inévitablement par des négociations directes entre le Polisario et le Maroc et ne peut en aucun cas dépendre des seuls agendas internes du président Trump et de celui du Roi Mohammed VI. Il est à craindre que les conditions ne soient pas réunies pour des négociations sans contraintes de quelque nature que ce soit et que la solution à la question sahraouie ne trouve pas cette fois encore un début de règlement au drame d’un peuple qui n’est plus présenté comme une victime de la colonisation, mais comme un obstacle à la reconfiguration projetée de l’Afrique du Nord. *Ancien ministre, ancien ambassadeur L’article Sahara occidental : les États-Unis et la France activent la marche forcée de la reconfiguration de l’Afrique du Nord est apparu en premier sur TSA .

items.title: Clean house or face defeat in 2027 — Onoh tasks Tinubu over claims of multi-billion Naira ministerial slots
items.description: .. .Onoh challenges APC spokesman to prove sale of ministerial seats By Emma Nnadozie Former South-East spokesperson for President Bola Tinubu’s 2023 Presidential Campaign Council, Denge Josef Onoh, has challenged All Progressives Congress (APC) campaign council spokesperson Alwan Hassan to provide evidence for his claim that ministerial appointments in Nigeria are secured through payments running into billions of naira. Onoh, who is also chairman of the Forum of Former Members of the Enugu State House of Assembly, described the allegation as damaging to Nigeria’s democratic institutions and international reputation. In a statement made available to journalists in Lagos, Onoh faulted Hassan’s reported remarks during an interview on Arise Television, in which he allegedly claimed that ministerial positions were purchased and that appointees sought to recover their financial investments through the looting of public funds. Onoh argued that the allegation should not be generalised to previous administrations without verifiable evidence, insisting that claims of corruption must be supported by facts rather than used to justify alleged wrongdoing in the present government. He said Hassan should provide the names of former ministers who allegedly paid for their appointments, the intermediaries involved, the amounts paid and the dates of the transactions. According to Onoh, the absence of such evidence would undermine attempts to portray the alleged practice as a longstanding feature of Nigeria’s democratic history. Defending the administration of former President Olusegun Obasanjo, Onoh described it as a period when appointments to the Federal Executive Council were based on merit, character, intellectual capacity and administrative competence. He argued that Obasanjo assembled technocrats and experienced professionals who contributed to Nigeria’s economic and institutional reforms. Onoh cited the country’s external debt relief, banking sector consolidation, telecommunications expansion and the establishment of the Economic and Financial Crimes Commission (EFCC) and the Independent Corrupt Practices and Other Related Offences Commission (ICPC) as notable achievements associated with that period. He challenged former cabinet members who served between 1999 and 2023 to state whether they paid to secure their appointments, maintaining that allegations against previous administrations should not be accepted without evidence. The former campaign council spokesperson also criticised what he described as a departure from the discipline and institutional respect that characterised the campaign structure under the late former President Muhammadu Buhari. He said Hassan’s reported comments raised questions about cohesion and discipline within the current administration’s political communication structure. Onoh further warned that allegations portraying ministerial appointments as commercial transactions could damage Nigeria’s international standing, discourage foreign investment and weaken public confidence in government institutions. He described the reported remarks as an affront to Nigerians, arguing that appointments to public office should be determined by competence, patriotism and a commitment to public service rather than financial considerations. Onoh, who said he remained a supporter of democratic governance and the Tinubu administration, added that the allegations, if substantiated, would raise serious questions about the integrity of the government’s appointment process. He argued that the President should address the controversy and take steps to restore public confidence in the Federal Executive Council. Onoh also called for a comprehensive cabinet reshuffle, urging Tinubu to appoint people he described as competent, patriotic and morally upright. He warned that failure to address the concerns could have political consequences for the ruling party in the 2027 general elections. The allegations attributed to Hassan could not be independently verified from the statement provided. Hassan’s response to Onoh’s criticism was also not included in the statement. The post Clean house or face defeat in 2027 — Onoh tasks Tinubu over claims of multi-billion Naira ministerial slots appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: Samson’s Take: One country, different standards of justice?
items.description: Something is troubling about how our criminal justice system treats suspects and offenders. The law sometimes appears merciful to the powerful, merciless to the poor, and remarkably swift against those accused of offensive speech, especially in recent times. Consider the Obuasi school scandal. At least 19 girls, helpless girls, have reportedly alleged sexual abuse involving their headmaster. He denies wrongdoing and enjoys the presumption of innocence. I’m a lawyer, I should say that. But why has the police response appeared so restrained compared with the speed and force sometimes deployed against suspects accused of misdemeanor speech offences? Yes, just upon the suspicion and arrest, they get locked up. They spend weeks in custody. Must frightened schoolgirls formally report before the police vigorously investigate credible allegations of sexual abuse? Then consider the Northern Development Authority case. Three former executives and a businessman were convicted of corruption-related offences yesterday, but they received fines rather than imprisonment. Fines, GH¢4,000. The court considered mitigating circumstances, including the prevention of financial loss; that is legally permissible. But compare their treatment with that of poor offenders in prison for stealing food, sometimes because they cannot afford fines or legal representation. If it’s messy being administered equally in this country, I’m not demanding imprisonment for the NDA convicts or unlawful detention of the Obuasi suspects. I’m demanding consistency, fairness, and equal justice. The law must protect every suspect’s rights while ensuring that serious allegations receive serious attention. And judicial mercy must never appear to depend on wealth, status, or influence. Attorney General Dominic Ayini’s proposal to deploy lawyers to police stations is therefore important. But legal representation alone cannot cure inconsistent enforcement. People are watching. Dear police, people are watching. Dear executives, the wielders of power, people are watching. The schoolgirls are watching. The poor are watching. And when justice appears harsh against the weak, but accommodating towards the powerful, confidence in the law suffers. Justice must be fair without being cruel, merciful without being selective, and equal without regard to status. One country, one constitution, one standard of justice. That’s the title of my take. And that is my take.

items.title: Ziguinchor : du matériel remis aux femmes et des embarcations aux CLPA
items.description: La ministre des Pêches et de l’Économie maritime, Amy Mara Dièye, a procédé ce vendredi 23 octobre à la remise de matériel aux femmes transformatrices de poisson et des embarcations aux Comités locaux de pêche artisanale (Clpa). Cette dotation s’inscrit dans le cadre du projet « ANARÉ DIFAL » (les femmes de la mer), financé par le Japon et mis en œuvre par la FAO, pour un montant de plus d’un milliard de FCFA. ZIGUINCHOR – L’État du Sénégal et ses partenaires veulent soutenir davantage le secteur de la pêche artisanale. C'est dans cette perspective que des équipements ont été remis aux femmes transformatrices de poisson et aux Comités locaux de pêche artisanale (Clpa). La cérémonie s’est tenue au quai de pêche de Boudody, à Ziguinchor, en présence de Bintia Stephen-Tchicaya, coordonnatrice de la FAO pour l’Afrique de l’Ouest et représentante de l’organisation au Sénégal. Un appui qui vise l’amélioration des conditions de travail, la réduction des pertes après capture, le renforcement et la gestion durable des ressources halieutiques en Casamance. Selon la ministre Amy Mara Dièye, ces équipements doivent apporter des changements visibles dans le quotidien des bénéficiaires. « Votre savoir-faire mérite des équipements à la hauteur de la noblesse de votre travail », a-t-elle déclaré, estimant que cette dotation doit alléger les tâches, améliorer l’hygiène et la qualité des produits, réduire les pertes et accroître les revenus des transformatrices. A lire aussi : Filière halieutique : la construction de trois unités de transformation lancée à Ziguinchor La ministre des Pêches et de l’Économie maritime a également insisté sur la nécessité d’évaluer les résultats de cet appui à partir des améliorations réellement constatées sur le terrain. « La réussite du projet se mesurera à sa capacité à vous permettre de travailler plus facilement, de perdre moins de produits et de mieux vivre de vos activités », a indiqué Amy Mara Dièye. Les embarcations remises aux CLPA doivent, pour leur part, renforcer leurs moyens d’action dans la surveillance et la gestion des ressources halieutiques. Amy Mara Dièye les a invités à assurer un bon entretien du matériel, à définir des règles de gestion claires et à rendre compte de son utilisation. Elle a aussi appelé les services techniques à accompagner les bénéficiaires dans la durée. De son côté, Bintia Stephen-Tchicaya a salué la coopération entre le Sénégal, le Japon et la FAO. Elle a souligné le rôle central de la pêche artisanale dans l’économie bleue et la contribution des femmes à la création de valeur en Casamance, malgré le manque d’équipements et les difficultés de conservation des produits. « Au-delà du matériel, ce projet représente un investissement dans le potentiel humain, l’autonomisation économique des femmes et l’avenir des communautés de pêche de la Casamance », a-t-elle affirmé. Elle a exhorté les bénéficiaires à utiliser les équipements de manière optimale et à renforcer la solidarité entre leurs organisations. Gaustin DIATTA (Correspondant)

items.title: UAE diplomat vying for UN's top job
items.description: An Emirati official with Palestinian roots, Lana Nusseibeh has emerged as a late frontrunner in the race to lead the United Nations, campaigning on a reformist agenda and vowing to work for peace. Since her official nomination on Wednesday, she has already garnered the backing of Gulf states but also faced scrutiny over her country’s normalisation with Israel and Abu Dhabi’s alleged role in Sudan’s war. If she succeeds, she would be the first woman and the second Arab to snatch the job in what would be a tour de force for the United Arab Emirates (UAE), a Middle East power that was under Iranian attack earlier this year. United Arab Emirates’ Assistant Minister for Political Affairs and Foreign Minister’s Envoy Lana Nusseibeh addresses the United Nations General Assembly at UN headquarters in New York City on September 27, 2025. —AFP In a campaign video, she vows if elected to “bring greater urgency to the work for peace” and “defend human rights”, speaking in perfect English with a slight British accent. The long-haired brunette, 48, sporting a red suit, projects the image of a modern Arab woman, one that her country has long sought to portray. “Lana Nusseibeh has a thick CV,” said Emirati political science academic Abdulkhaleq Abdulla. “She brings in the best of the UAE’s diplomacy.” She stepped down from her post as state minister at the foreign ministry and as envoy to the UN and EU to campaign for the top UN job. A seasoned diplomat, she has also served as the UAE’s permanent representative to the UN, from 2013 to 2024, the first woman to hold the post. Nickolay Mladenov, the high representative for Gaza under a US-backed “Board of Peace”, said Nusseibeh “does not give up when the room gets difficult”. “She is relentless, but never in a way that overwhelms people,” he said. Palestinian roots Nusseibeh comes from a prominent Palestinian family of statesmen, uprooted by the creation of Israel in 1948. Her family traditionally held the keys to the Church of the Holy Sepulcher in the walled Old City of Jerusalem. Yet she has defended the Abraham Accords , under which the UAE normalised ties with Israel in 2020, drawing criticism from pro-Palestinian activists and commentators on social media. Her grandfather was defence minister in Jordan in the 1950s and one of the first Palestinians to be in contact with the Israelis, while her father Zaki Nusseibeh was an adviser and interpreter to the UAE’s late founding president Sheikh Zayed. He currently serves as cultural adviser to the UAE president and was also a state minister. Nusseibeh has two sons. She holds two master’s degrees, including one in Israeli and Jewish diaspora studies from the University of London. Minister of State at the Ministry of Foreign Affairs of the United Arab Emirates Lana Nusseibeh attends a meeting with foreign ministers of the Gulf Cooperation Council Member States (GCC) and the US Secretary of State, in Manama on June 25, 2026. —AFP ‘No candidate short of criticism’ Nusseibeh’s nomination has sparked some backlash over her country’s involvement in the Sudan war, where the UAE is accused of backing the paramilitary Rapid Support Forces (RSF) — accusations it denies. Since April 2023, Sudan has been engulfed in a war between the army and the RSF, triggering what the United Nations has described as one of the world’s worst humanitarian crises. “There is no candidate that is short of criticism… We’ll just have to deal with it, especially the Sudan file,” Abdulla told AFP. “The UAE has already stated time and again that all of these are media allegations, and we have already made it clear that… we deny all of them, and we do not send any arms or finance the RSF,” he added. It is tradition that the UN’s top job rotates between different regions. United Arab Emirates’ Assistant Minister for Political Affairs and Foreign Minister’s Envoy Lana Nusseibeh addresses the United Nations General Assembly at UN headquarters in New York City on September 27, 2025. —AFP Under that premise, the role should go to a candidate from Latin America this time. But US ambassador to the UN Mike Waltz recently said the focus should be on picking the “best candidate” instead of the region or gender. In the latest informal straw poll held last week to gauge which candidates have a shot of becoming the next UN secretary general, every contender received an effective veto. Five of the 15 members of the UN Security Council wield veto power and can shut down any candidate unacceptable to them, which happened Friday when all seven candidates received at least two vetoes.

items.title: Infrastructures : la Guinée ratifie un prêt de 300 millions d’euros pour la route Labé-Tougué
items.description: Dans un décret lu à la télévision nationale, le président de la République a ratifié l’accord de prêt conclu entre le gouvernement guinéen et plusieurs institutions financières internationales, pour le financement du projet de construction et de bitumage de la route nationale reliant Labé à Tougué, y compris la bretelle Banti-Koubia. Signé le 22 juillet 2026, cet accord porte sur un montant de 300 millions d’euros. La Bank of Africa United Kingdom PLC intervient en qualité d’arrangeur principal mandaté, aux côtés de plusieurs institutions financières, notamment l’Armée Bank of Kuwait KSCP, l’Africa Finance Corporation, France Abu Dhabi Bank, ABC Islamic Bank, Bank of Africa et Bank of China. Le projet prévoit la construction et le bitumage de 148,860 kilomètres de route sur les routes nationales n° 27 et 28, ainsi que l’aménagement de la bretelle Banti-Koubia, longue de 11,443 kilomètres sur la route nationale n° 34. Il comprend également la construction d’un pont de 200 mètres sur le fleuve Bafing, avec un revêtement en béton bitumineux.

items.title: Section 144 imposed in Upper, Lower South Waziristan over security concerns
items.description: SOUTH WAZIRISTAN: The district administrations of Lower and Upper South Waziristan imposed Section 144 restrictions for Saturday, restricting movement in several areas and closing markets and major routes amid security concerns and the movement of logistical supplies for security forces. Lower South Waziristan Deputy Commissioner Musarrat Zaman and Upper South Waziristan Deputy Commissioner Irfan Ali issued separate notifications on Friday evening, outlining restrictions on public movement, access to designated roads and other activities in the affected areas. According to the notification issued by the Lower South Waziristan administration, Section 144 was enforced in Wana Bazaar, the Wana Bypass and several other localities. The restrictions were imposed in view of security concerns and to facilitate the safe transportation of logistical supplies for security forces. The notification prohibited movement along several routes, including those passing through Wana, Tiarza Gate, Karab Kot, Tanai, Azizabad Chowk and Dargai Bridge. Entry onto the routes connecting Gul Kach with Toi Khullah and Tanai was also strictly prohibited. The district administration said travel along the affected routes would be permitted only in emergencies and with prior authorisation from the police or security forces. Residents were advised to avoid unnecessary movement and comply with the instructions issued by the authorities. The notification also directed motorists to stop their vehicles at least 50 metres away upon seeing security forces. Officials said the restrictions were intended to facilitate security arrangements during the movement of logistical supplies. The administration warned that individuals violating the restrictions would be held responsible for their actions under the applicable law. In Upper South Waziristan, the administration issued a separate notification imposing Section 144 in Servekai and Sararogha tehsils and several adjoining areas. The restrictions were introduced for similar security reasons, particularly in connection with the transportation of logistical supplies for security forces. The notification also ordered the closure of markets and commercial centres in the affected areas. According to the district administration, entry was prohibited on several routes, including those leading to Ladha, Makeen, Sararogha and Nazar Khel. Restrictions were also imposed on roads leading to Dargai Bridge, Madi Jan, Sheen Warsak and Jandola. Other routes affected by the order included those passing through Servekai, Moley Khan Sarai, Barwand, Asman Manza and Torwam. The administration directed residents to refrain from travelling through the restricted areas until permitted by the relevant authorities. However, the notification allowed travel in emergencies, subject to authorisation from the police or security forces and verification of identity documents. Special provisions were also made for polio workers and vaccination teams. According to the notification, members of these teams would be allowed to move through the affected areas after establishing their identities. The Upper South Waziristan administration also instructed motorists to stop their vehicles at least 50 metres away upon seeing security forces and directed all occupants to disembark. The measure was included among the security instructions issued for compliance during the enforcement of Section 144. Both administrations urged residents to cooperate with law enforcement agencies, follow official instructions and avoid unnecessary travel on restricted routes. People requiring movement for emergencies were advised to seek permission from the relevant authorities before proceeding. Section 144 empowers district administrations to impose restrictions on certain activities and public movement in specified circumstances. The latest orders in the two districts come amid heightened security concerns and efforts to facilitate the movement of supplies for security forces.

items.title: La Tunisie est-elle prête à renégocier l’accord d’association avec Bruxelles ?
items.description: Dans ses relations avec la Tunisie, l’Union européenne (UE) a continuellement privilégié, sous le discours de la «coopération», les intérêts agricoles, l’accès aux marchés et les impératifs de stabilité de l’Europe elle-même, a souligné Mohamed Sassi dans son ouvrage intitulé «Les relations Tunisie-Union européenne: six décennies d’histoire» paru en 2025 aux éditions Nirvana, à Tunis. Mais la Tunisie a-t-elle jamais fait preuve, vraiment de capacité de négociation pour la défense de ses intérêts vitaux ? Aujourd’hui, elle demande la révision des termes des accords passés avec l’UE, mais alors que Bruxelles se dit prêt à moderniser l’Accord d’association avec Tunis, Tunis s’est-il vraiment préparé à s’y engager avec des idées et des programmes clairs ? Latif Belhedi L’UE se dit prête à entamer un dialogue avec la Tunisie en vue de moderniser l’Accord d'association de 1995, afin de l’adapter aux nouveaux défis économiques, technologiques et énergétiques, tout en renforçant les investissements et l’intégration industrielle entre les deux rives de la Méditerranée. C’est ce qu’a déclaré l’ambassadeur de l’UE à Tunis, Giuseppe Perrone, lors d'une intervention aujourd’hui sur les ondes d’ Express FM , tout en soulignant que, trente ans après la signature de cet accord, il est devenu nécessaire de mettre à jour un cadre initialement conçu principalement pour les échanges commerciaux, en l’étendant à des domaines tels que l’intelligence artificielle, les services numériques, la transition énergétique et les nouvelles chaînes de valeur. Mettre à jour le cadre du partenariat Bruxelles a déjà noué des contacts préliminaires avec les autorités tunisiennes et confirme sa volonté d’engager des discussions, mais aucun calendrier de négociation ni aucune proposition formelle de révision n’ont encore été annoncés. La position européenne s’inscrit dans le débat initié par les autorités tunisiennes, qui réclament un rééquilibrage de l’accord. Elles souhaitent favoriser un meilleur accès des produits agricoles au marché européen, attirer des investissements à haute valeur ajoutée et permettre une participation accrue des entreprises locales aux chaînes de production internationales. En mai dernier, le ministre des Affaires étrangères, Mohamed Ali Nafti, avait réaffirmé la nécessité d’un partenariat plus équitable, respectueux des priorités économiques nationales. Perrone a rappelé que l’UE demeure le principal partenaire commercial de la Tunisie. En 2025, les exportations tunisiennes vers les pays européens ont atteint environ 44 milliards de dinars, contre 37 milliards d’importations, soit un excédent commercial d’environ 7 milliards de dinars (équivalent à 2,1 milliards d’euros). On dénombre quelque 3 400 entreprises européennes présentes dans le pays, lesquelles assurent plus de 400 000 emplois directs. Cap sur les énergies renouvelables L’énergie figure parmi les priorités du partenariat, avec un soutien européen au développement des énergies renouvelables, à la modernisation de la Société nationale d’électricité (Steg) et au projet Elmed, une interconnexion électrique sous-marine entre la Tunisie et l’Italie. Cette infrastructure, développée par Terna et la Steg, prévoit une liaison bidirectionnelle d’environ 220 kilomètres, dotée d’une capacité de 600 mégawatts. En juin dernier, un contrat d’environ 770 millions d’euros a été attribué à Hitachi Energy pour la réalisation des stations de conversion en Sicile et sur la péninsule tunisienne du cap Bon. Selon Perrone, ce projet permettra de renforcer la sécurité des approvisionnements et l’intégration des marchés électriques euro-méditerranéens, tout en facilitant le recours aux énergies renouvelables. Le diplomate a fait état d’avancées significatives dans la préparation financière et technique, laissant entrevoir un début des travaux, sans toutefois en préciser la date. L’amère leçon de 60 ans de relations tuniso-européennes En matière d’investissements, Bruxelles vise à renforcer la coopération dans les secteurs de l’automobile, du textile, de l’agroalimentaire, du numérique et des technologies environnementales. Perrone a toutefois souligné la nécessité d'une plus grande prévisibilité réglementaire et d'une amélioration du climat des affaires en Tunisie. L’ambassadeur a par ailleurs rappelé l'existence d'un soutien budgétaire européen de 80 millions d’euros, destiné aux mesures sociales en faveur des familles vulnérables, et a annoncé la préparation d’un forum euro-méditerranéen sur l’investissement et le développement durable, prévu au printemps 2027 dans le cadre du nouveau Pacte pour la Méditerranée. L’objectif affiché par Bruxelles est de transformer le partenariat avec Tunis en un levier d’intégration économique et industrielle accrue, dépassant ainsi une coopération fondée essentiellement sur les échanges commerciaux. Bref, l’UE sait ce qu’elle peut tirer de sa coopération avec la Tunisie. Elle sait aussi ce qu’elle peut y apporter et semble prête à un nouveau round de négociation. On attend de la Tunisie qu’elle montre le même degré de préparation et la même capacité de proposition avant le démarrage des négociations, et n’y vienne pas seulement, comme souvent, avec de grandes idées et des récriminations. A bon entendeur… L’article La Tunisie est-elle prête à renégocier l’accord d’association avec Bruxelles ? est apparu en premier sur Kapitalis .

items.title: Concerned Ho Zongo Youth demand permanent resolution to Volta Regional Chief Imam impasse
items.description: Concerned Ho Zongo Youth are demanding a lasting resolution to the Volta Regional Chief Imam impasse and objecting to the “knee-jerk” approach to resolving the issue. They raised concerns about alleged political interference, urging political players to stay out of the issue, which is fueling violent among members of the community. The Concerned Ho Zongo Youth spokesperson, Abdul Razak Abubakar, entreated the Volta Regional Minister, James Gunu, the Volta Regional Security Council and other relevant institutions to endeavour to bring closure to the Chief Imam impasse. He warned of the consequences should the governing National Democratic Congress pick sides in the impasse or fail to restore peace in the Ho Zongo community. “The youth reserve the right to express their political disappointment through peaceful and lawful democratic means, including at the ballot box. No political party should take the support of any community for granted while legitimate concerns remain unresolved”, said Mr Abubakar. Shooting incident unresolved He recounted how the impasse was marked by a violent incident in December 2025, which resulted in the injury of scores of believers who had gathered at the Central Mosque for Salat al-Jumu’ah prayers. He explained that the victims were yet to receive justice, as the culprits had not been prosecuted. He therefore entreated the Interior Ministry to relaunch investigations into the shooting incident and ensure that those found culpable were brought to book to appease grieving hearts. “We also call on the Minister for the Interior to take urgent interest in the reported shooting incident, ensure a thorough investigation and help prevent any further violence. The safety of worshippers and residents must be paramount”, he said. Closure of mosque Following the shooting incident, the mosque was closed to the public to avert further clashes, forcing believers to worship on the premises. It was, however, opened briefly for the National Chief Imam, His Eminence Sheikh Dr Osmanu Nuhu Sharubutu, accompanied by the Volta Regional Minister, James Gunu, to perform some prayers two weeks ago. The mosque has since been locked to worshippers. Mr Abubakar warned that the Zongo youth would launch a series of demonstrations until an amicable solution to the Volta Regional Chief Imam impasse was found and the Ho Central Mosque reopened for its intended purpose. “The reopening of the mosque must be pursued through lawful coordination with the relevant authorities, with the safety of worshippers and the wider community fully protected. We expect the Minister to act urgently and demonstrate genuine leadership before tensions escalate further”, he said.

items.title: North Korea’s Kim calls for training world’s ‘strongest’ military
items.description: North Korean leader Kim Jong Un urged his military to train to become the strongest in the world at a two-day meeting of company commanders in Pyongyang, state media said Saturday. Kim’s call for what he dubbed a “Korean-style military revolution” came the same week Seoul’s military proposed talks to clarify the border after an explosion inside the heavily fortified Demilitarised Zone (DMZ) further strained inter-Korean ties. Seoul and Pyongyang remain technically at war as the 1950-53 Korean War ended in a truce, not a peace treaty. The Pyongyang event, held Thursday and Friday, was aimed at developing a plan “to train the strongest armed forces in the world,” Kim said, according to the official Korea Central News Agency (KCNA). He also called for “all the companies” of the North’s army to be “turned into a strong elite unit in military and technical aspects and consolidated into perfect combat forces”. KCNA said it was the first gathering of “the entire army” since a February party congress where Kim had called for stronger conventional forces and reaffirmed plans to develop nuclear weapons and missiles. North Korea has also tested a slew of weapons recently, including a “new-type” precision-guided torpedo system and an intermediate-range hypersonic missile, both of which were said to use AI technology. Despite long-running UN sanctions, North Korea has enshrined its status as a nuclear-armed state in law, with its regime repeatedly declaring its atomic arsenal permanent and irreversible. The North has also become a key Russian ally since it launched its invasion of Ukraine in 2022, sending troops to support Moscow’s war effort in return for economic benefits and military technology. South Korea proposed on Friday military talks with North Korea to clarify their border and restore communication channels, after Seoul blamed the DMZ blast that injured South Korean soldiers on North Korean landmines, a claim Pyongyang strongly rejected. Pyongyang, which also previously rejected Seoul’s demand for an apology over the explosion, has not responded to Friday’s proposal. c The post North Korea’s Kim calls for training world’s ‘strongest’ military appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: Paiements numériques : le virement instantané grimpe de 78%
items.description: Virement instantané en hausse de 78 %, paiement mobile de 42 %, cartes bancaires de 20 % : le rapport annuel de Bank Al-Maghrib sur les infrastructures de marchés financiers et les moyens de paiement décrit une bascule rapide des usages. Les règlements chez les commerçants via portefeuille mobile restent toutefois marginaux, un point que la Banque centrale entend corriger par le plafonnement de l’interchange, un fonds dédié à l’acceptation et un schéma national de paiement. Les échanges scripturaux ont atteint 718 millions d’opérations en 2025, en hausse de 15 %, pour une valeur proche de 6 121 milliards de dirhams (+10 %). Le rapport de Bank Al-Maghrib couvrant l'exercice 2025 en déduit une moyenne de 19,4 transactions par habitant/an. Deux instruments tirent la dynamique : le virement instantané, dont le nombre d’opérations a augmenté d’environ 78 %, et le paiement mobile, en hausse d’environ 42 %. Dans la structure des échanges en nombre, le virement conserve la première place avec 47,6 % (48,9 % en 2024), devant la carte bancaire à 32 % (30,8 %) et le prélèvement à 7,8 %. Le virement instantané passe de 2,6 % à 4 % et devance désormais le chèque et le paiement mobile, qui pèsent chacun 3,9 %, tandis que la lettre de change normalisée plafonne à 0,8 %. En valeur, la hiérarchie diffère : le virement détient 62,3 % des montants (61,1 % en 2024), le chèque recule de 23,8 % à 21,9 %, la lettre de change normalisée pèse 6,6 % et le prélèvement 6,1 %. Le virement instantané et la carte atteignent respectivement 1,8 % et 1,2 % des montants, contre 1,1 % chacun un an plus tôt, alors que le M-Wallet reste à 0,1 %. Les échanges au sein d’un même établissement demeurent majoritaires, avec 66 % des opérations en nombre et 54 % en valeur. Le rapport l’explique principalement par la démocratisation des applications bancaires et par la gratuité des transferts en intra-établissement. Sur le circuit interbancaire du GSIMT, le nombre d’opérations atteint 165 millions, contre 151 millions en 2024, grâce aux virements (121 millions, contre 105 millions), dont 29 millions de virements instantanés. Les chèques et les prélèvements reculent chacun de 5 %. En nombre, le virement instantané représente 18 % des échanges interbancaires, quand le chèque tombe à 14 %, après 16 % en 2024 et 24 % en 2022. Le montant moyen d’un virement instantané ressort à 3,70 KDH, le plafond unitaire étant fixé à 20 000 dirhams, contre 13,30 KDH pour un virement standard. Du côté des cartes, 230,1 millions d’opérations ont été enregistrées pour 70,8 milliards de dirhams, soit 20 % de plus en nombre et 12 % en valeur. Les paiements via les terminaux de paiement électronique sont passés de 153,3 à 184,5 millions d’opérations, pour 58,6 milliards de dirhams contre 52,2 milliards, et le sans-contact atteint 113,1 millions d’opérations, contre 94,4 millions, soit 30 % de la valeur des paiements sur terminal, contre 27 %. Le e-commerce progresse de 16 %, à 44,8 millions d’opérations, pour 12,1 milliards de dirhams, et pèse 20 % des paiements en nombre et 17 % en valeur. Les cartes internationales utilisées au Maroc affichent 55,5 millions d’opérations pour 55,7 milliards de dirhams, en hausse de 28 % et 16 %. Sur le plan de la sécurité, la conformité à la norme EMV s’établit à 99,9 % à fin 2025. Le paiement mobile s’appuie sur des comptes de paiement dont le stock a atteint 16,221 millions, contre 13,822 millions en 2024, 10,3 millions en 2023 et 6,8 millions en 2022. Ils se répartissent entre 4,3 millions de comptes de type 1, 6,2 millions de type 2, 5 millions de type 3 et 0,7 million de type 4, avec des plafonds respectifs de 1 000, 4 000, 20 000 et 100 000 dirhams, selon la classification introduite par la circulaire 2/W/2024 du 20 décembre 2024. Vingt offres de M-Wallet sont présentes sur le marché, dont 13 émises par des établissements de paiement, qui concentrent 73 % de l’encours, à 12 millions de portefeuilles sur un total de 16,4 millions, contre 13,7 millions un an plus tôt. Le nombre de transactions est passé de 19,7 à 28 millions, pour 7,3 milliards de dirhams contre 3,9 milliards, en raison principalement du déversement des aides sociales directes sur les comptes de paiement. La nature de ces opérations en dit long sur le stade atteint par le paiement mobile. Pour les portefeuilles émis par des établissements de paiement, le règlement de factures représente 69 % des transactions en nombre (72 % en 2024) et les transferts de mobile à mobile 28 % (26 %), les retraits au GAB étant limités à 2 % et les paiements chez les commerçants à une part marginale. Pour les portefeuilles adossés à des comptes bancaires, les transferts de mobile à mobile deviennent la première catégorie, avec 51 % des opérations contre 26 % un an plus tôt, devant les factures (32 %, contre 53 %), les retraits au GAB (10 %) et les achats chez les commerçants (6 %). En valeur, les paiements chez les commerçants ne dépassent pas 2 % pour les banques et restent quasi inexistants pour les établissements de paiement. Le rapport en conclut que la montée en charge des paiements mobiles auprès des commerçants reste tributaire du développement de l’acceptation marchande et de l’élargissement des cas d’usage de proximité. C’est précisément l’objet de la Stratégie de Développement des Paiements 2024-2028, qui fait passer la priorité de la diversification des instruments à leur utilisation effective, en particulier pour les paiements de proximité, les petits montants et les flux récurrents. La Banque centrale y raisonne en marché biface : l’usage par les porteurs suppose un réseau d’acceptation suffisamment large, et l’intérêt des commerçants grandit à mesure que l’usage progresse. Le suivi s’appuiera sur des indicateurs d’usage, parmi lesquels la part des paiements marchands et l’évolution des retraits d’espèces. Un Comité de Place des Paiements, présidé par Bank Al-Maghrib et réunissant établissements de crédit, établissements de paiement et gestionnaires d’infrastructures, a été mis en place en 2025. Sur le terrain de l’acceptation, la Banque centrale a poursuivi l’ouverture du marché de l’acquisition à de nouveaux acteurs, afin de passer d’un modèle historiquement concentré à un environnement plus concurrentiel, avec des offres adaptées aux petits commerces. Elle a plafonné à 0,65 % hors taxes les commissions d’interchange domestiques sur les cartes émises au niveau national, et des travaux ont été engagés pour en simplifier la structure. Le Fonds de Développement de l’Acceptation, institué début 2026, a fait l’objet en 2025 d’un travail de conception : gouvernance, modèle de financement, modalités d’intervention, critères de ciblage des commerçants, conditions de participation des acquéreurs, mécanismes de reporting. Son efficacité sera jugée au nombre de commerçants actifs, à la fréquence des paiements, aux volumes traités et à la pérennité des usages après la période d’accompagnement, et non au seul équipement en terminaux. L’interopérabilité constitue l’autre chantier. Les travaux sur le Schéma National de Paiement, engagés en 2025, couvrent les standards techniques, les règles d’interopérabilité et de qualité de service, l’harmonisation des formats de messages, la standardisation du QR Code et la création d’un annuaire central des alias de paiement. Parallèlement, un dispositif conventionnel d’Open Banking est en préparation avec le Groupement Professionnel des Banques du Maroc, en vue d’une ouverture progressive vers l’Open Finance. Le rapport rappelle aussi que Bank Al-Maghrib a contribué aux travaux ayant abouti, en janvier 2026, à la loi n° 71-24 modifiant et complétant le Code de commerce. À l’international, la Banque centrale a poursuivi les échanges avec BUNA, le système régional arabe de règlement des paiements transfrontaliers, en vue d’admettre le dirham parmi les monnaies de règlement. Elle a rejoint en juin 2025 le système panafricain de paiement et de règlement PAPSS, qui couvrait à fin novembre 2025 19 pays, plus de 160 banques commerciales et 15 switchs de paiement. La concrétisation des bénéfices attendus pour les entreprises exportatrices reste conditionnée, précise le rapport, à la maîtrise d’enjeux de finalité du règlement, de risque de change et de liquidité, de sécurité et de coopération entre autorités. Les travaux sur la monnaie numérique de banque centrale, menés depuis 2021 avec l’appui du Fonds monétaire international et de la Banque mondiale, restent de nature exploratoire et ne préjugent d’aucune décision d’émission. Une expérimentation de paiement transfrontalier entre particuliers en environnement multidevises a été conduite en 2025 avec la Banque mondiale et la Banque centrale d’Égypte. Quant aux crypto-actifs, un avant-projet de loi n° 42-25, élaboré par un groupe de travail réunissant Bank Al-Maghrib, le ministère de l’Économie et des Finances et l’AMMC, a été soumis à consultation publique en octobre 2025, ses textes d’application étant en cours d’élaboration avec l’appui de la Banque mondiale. items.title: 2027: Akande recounts how Buhari’s govt humiliated Tinubu; urges Atiku to make sacrifices
items.description: Former presidential aide, Laolu Akande, has recounted how President Bola Tinubu was allegedly marginalised and humiliated under the administration of late President Muhammadu Buhari, urging former Vice President Atiku Abubakar to make sacrifices to unite the opposition ahead of the 2027 general election. Akande said Tinubu endured mistreatment within the All Progressives Congress (APC) despite his contributions to Buhari’s emergence as president in 2015, but chose to remain in the party and wait for his opportunity rather than abandon it. Speaking on the Naija Unfiltered Podcast, Akande said he personally witnessed instances in which Tinubu was sidelined during Buhari’s presidency. “What did they not do against Bola Ahmed Tinubu? Tell me, what did they not do? Even between 2015 and 2023, the man was marginalised. I saw him with my korokoro eyes,” he said. “I sat in meetings where they put Bola Ahmed Tinubu behind me,” Akande added. According to him, Tinubu did not allow the treatment to push him out of the APC but remained patient and continued to organise politically until he eventually succeeded Buhari in 2023. “He just waited. He bided his time,” Akande said. He also cited the controversy surrounding the naira redesign policy in the run-up to the 2023 election, arguing that Tinubu responded to the political challenges by mobilising rather than abandoning his ambition. Akande dismissed claims that the ruling APC was responsible for the divisions among opposition leaders, saying political parties must be able to withstand pressure from the party in power. “I’m not saying it’s right, but this is how they have done it. So, if you are serious as opposition, you must be able to withstand it and rise to the top by doing what has become common sense,” he said. The former presidential aide attributed the opposition’s difficulties partly to ego, arguing that Atiku should take the initiative to build a united front against Tinubu. “But to the point, I think it is ego. So, the person that ought to make the move here is Atiku,” he said. Akande urged the former vice president to be willing to put aside his personal ambition in the interest of the opposition’s collective goal. “Atiku is one that was supposed to say, ‘You know what? We are going to make sure that we get this guy out, and I’m going to sacrifice,’” he said. He added that such a move could strengthen the opposition’s chances of mounting a coordinated challenge against the ruling party. Akande also recalled that despite Tinubu’s role in Buhari’s emergence as APC presidential candidate in 2015, some of the people he reportedly nominated for ministerial positions were rejected. “Alake was nominated; Edun was nominated. They went to choose the ones that he did not nominate to just make a point that you can’t dictate for us,” he said, referring to current ministers Dele Alake and Wale Edun. Akande said Tinubu did not abandon the APC despite the alleged rejection of his nominees, describing his decision to remain in the party and wait for another opportunity as a form of sacrifice. He argued that opposition leaders should draw lessons from Tinubu’s experience by prioritising their broader political objectives over individual ambitions. The post 2027: Akande recounts how Buhari’s govt humiliated Tinubu; urges Atiku to make sacrifices appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: Before Emmanuel Uduaghan died!
items.description: Dr. Emmanuel Eweta Uduaghan was just a good man. He was an incredible man of peace, a man who could do anything including daring death to achieve peace. I don’t know how many people in this world would stake their lives, be ready to die for peace to reign. Uduaghan did so as governor of his people. He revealed one instance in the story he told himself that I reproduce here today as part of my tributes to him. It was in a thanksgiving service to mark his birthday after leaving office as governor of Delta State. It was published October 29, 2016 in Vanguard. I present the story today for you to appreciate my description of him as an incredible man of peace. The story titled MY CLOSE SHAVE WITH DEATH also points to his humble background and the humility that made him remarkable. Read about Uduaghan, who called himself the village man who became a medical doctor and later a governor. Read also the second story on him from my archives, a story I reproduce not only in memory of the great achiever but also for the attention of the current Governor of Delta State, Sheriff Oborevwori who may pick interest in fulfilling what Uduaghan considered for the Illah community while hosting Super Eagles when they won the 2013 Nations Cup in South Africa. The headline was ILLAH IN THE EYES OF UDUAGHAN. Of course another chapter of Uduaghan’s life was his love for sports and efforts to develop it. He once asked our Queen of the tracks, Mary Onyali what he could do to get Blessing Okagbare on the podium. Mary told him to place Blessing on a special training allowance. Uduaghan did so. And Blessing truly justified the investment in the Glasgow Commonwealth Games and other international championships with podium performances. Uduaghan lifted sports not only in Delta but also in the country. We leave that for another day. Read the avalanche of tributes since he passed on and you will agree that a good man has joined the stars. Now, read about Uduaghan’s close shave with death as told by the man himself in a Thanksgiving service. MY CLOSE SHAVE WITH DEATH — Uduaghan SIR Tony Obuh described him as an accomplished man of peace in his goodwill message on his facebook page last weekend. Sonny Areh, his media assistant, had also posted, on his facebook page, a birthday message to Dr Emmanuel Uduaghan, the immediate past governor of Delta State. He turned 62 last Saturday. What followed was an avalanche of birthday and goodwill messages. There were some in the newspapers too. And so the goodwill that marked Uduaghan’s two tenures as governor is still on the high. And people showed this at a thanksgiving service at the Guiding Light Assembly Church at Parkview Estate, Ikoyi, Lagos, last Sunday. Uduaghan was at the church to thank God for His mercies all these years. People turned out in numbers in the church where the pastor preached about the Holy Spirit. The word of God was good. And the people reveled in it. As the service was about to end, the pastor invited Uduaghan to make a brief remark after the church had prayed for him and his family. When he was done, the pastor prayed that more good things would continue to follow him. Uduaghan recalled one moment, as Governor of Delta State when he was caught between life and death and God saved his life. Part of his testimony went thus: “There are two things associated with governance. I call them the two Ps. They are Power and Pain. You see a governor and you marvel at the power he commands. He can order the arrest of somebody, he moves in a convoy, he has so much power that he earns tremendous respect everywhere. People see the glamour and the glitz, etc. But they don’t see the pain. There’s pain in governance. You can only rely on the grace of God to guide and guard you. ”When I came in as governor in 2007, the violence we battled then in Delta was more than what is happening now with the Avengers, etc. Kidnapping was high and expatriates were leaving. Militancy was more than what we have now. President Yar’Adua called me and said ‘what’s going on? These things are happening in your state.’ I told him that there were kaytwo ways to handle the militancy in Niger Delta. I asked that the Federal Government should do their own and I would do my own. We set out to work. I had to go to the creeks. We had to dialogue with these people. ”I remember one Sunday, my family and I had prepared to go to church and I received a call that they were going to burn Chevron terminal. The facility they planned to burn was so huge the impact would have been terrible for our oil production. I told them I would come after church service but they insisted I should come immediately otherwise the militants would destroy the terminal. I had to leave. I told my family to pray for me at the church. It was just one of my trips to the creeks. I took helicopter and then did the final journey by boat. And you know that when you go on such trips to the creeks you don’t take escorts or when you take them they don’t carry guns. I went with only my ADC. No guns. It was a huge risk but one that I had to take to engage them and stop the blowing up of the oil facilities. ”It was a terrible place. I got to the place and after discussing with the militants they told me that there were higher authorities further inside that I must meet and that what I had just done was a preliminary one. They were all armed to the teeth, fierce-looking and ready to pull the trigger. You could imagine how dangerous it was in that terrain. I continued the journey further into the creeks to meet their superiors. I got there and they led me into a room. They were kind enough to offer me a seat. With their guns, some pointing at me, they sat on the floor while we held talks on why they should spare the oil facility. I spent hours with the them. I finished with them and left for the journey back home. ”While on the boat going back, we noticed one speed boat racing to where we were. They caught up with us. We didn’t know if it was another group but they caught up with us and one of them pointed his AK 47 at me and put his finger at the trigger. It was terrifying. It was a moment of life or death within seconds. You could see the anger on the face of the militant, who pointed the gun at me. He wanted to shoot. It was terrifying. There was nothing I could do but to pray silently. I was praying. Silently, I prayed and I waved the white handkerchief (peace signal) I had. The man steadied the gun at me. Suddenly another speed boat from nowhere dashed in between and and after some seconds they all sped off. ‘I believe that The Holy Spirit appeared in that white handkerchief and saved my life and I live today to give this testimony. ”There were other terrible encounters one had as governor but people would not know about these pains. What they know is the glamour or power they associate with you in governance. I thank God for what he had done for a village man like me. I come from a village setting where there were no roads, no electricity, no facilities, just village life – our parents were farming and fishing for us to go to school. I remember when I eventually had a Beetle car and how my wife prayed for us to have a better car, a better air conditioned car possibly a Mercedez Benz. And she used to sing a song about this. Today, God’s blessings have gone beyond owning a Mercedez Benz car. And if He could do it for a village boy like me He can do more for you all here.” Applause greeted this and the pastor prayed that good things would continue to follow Uduaghan. “You’ll preach and touch lives even if it is not from the pulpit,” the pastor told him. And so, that was how quietly Uduaghan marked his birthday with a thanksgiving service. Many turned out for him including former governor of Anambra State, Peter Obi. They still admire him. He made peace his trademark throughout his tenure. He was a symbol of humility. He liked sports so much. He played and still plays tennis. As governor, he would even officiate as an umpire while others played. He was that humble. He worked tirelessly for peace in Delta and towards the end of his eight-year tenure he made unbelievable sacrifices for the interest of peace. Nothing can be more apt than Obuh’s description of Dr Emmanuel Eweta Uduaghan as an accomplished man of peace. Many Happy returns. Ilah in the eyes of Uduaghan There was something unique about the reception Governor Emmanuel Uduaghan held for the Super Eagles while celebrating their 2013 Nations Cup feat. Some of the names Nigeria adored long before the present generation were invited. Some of them were already in their 70s and only few who were of the old generation could recognise them. There was George Oganwu, the first university graduate to play for the Green Eagles as they were called at the time. Then Owolo, Ebiwan Didiare, Godwin Etemike and Jossy Dombraye. Stephen Keshi and Sylvanus Okpala are old enough to have watched Dombraye in the 70s but I’m not sure they saw George Oganwu play. It was emotional when the presence of these veterans was announced and they were asked to stand for recognition. Oganwu was called to speak. He interjected humour while speaking but made a point that touched all in the hall. ‘’Our own Austin Ofokwu was being buried here in Nigeria, the same day George Best was being lowered to mother earth in England. While we watched on CNN, Sky News, BBC and other cable stations on how they were burying the former England star, our own star died and was buried unsung. We must begin to celebrate our heroes so that the younger ones would want to emulate them.’’ Austin Jay Jay Okocha was in the hall and sat close to me. ‘’Time is coming when we would be like this man and they would be inviting us to make such speeches,’’ Okocha said, smiling and appreciating what the Delta State Government was doing. At the October 30 sports summit held in Asaba in 2012, former 400m world champion Bert Cameroun of Jamaica awed the audience with some of the things that have made Jamaica great in track and field. He spoke eloquently on mentoring and revealed that even the history of their past heroes is taught in schools. Jamaican heroes are invited to events and schools to give motivational talks. They are adored and the young ones strive to emulate them. It was against this background that Delta invited these past football heroes from Delta to be part of the reception held for the Eagles. The players were rewarded with cash. Keshi got cash, a house and the Asaba Stadium named after him. The governor recalled that the feat achieved by Keshi had only been achieved by Mohammed El Gohary of Egypt. He is late now. He won the Nations Cup as a player and as a coach. Keshi has stepped into his shoes and now a living legend in African football. Uduaghan felt justified to so honour Keshi whom he also told that with time he would be invited to be part of a programme his government has already started. Delta is already implementing the report of the 2012 summit which emphasized on sports in schools and local communities. The Governor’s Cup, a football competition among secondary schools is now in the knock out stage. The school that wins will earn cash, a bus and a foreign trip for a youth competition. Delta is also starting a similar thing in track and field with the Awoturo Eleaya Cup. Cult heroes in track and field will play a role. Christian Chukwu, Davidson Onwumi and Jay Jay Okocha all gave motivational talks at the kick off of the Governor’s Cup in Asaba. Back to the reward night for the Eagles. When Uduaghan stood to speak, he first reacted to the points Oganwu made. Oganwu is from Ilah in Oshimili North Local Government Area of Delta. Uduaghan recalled that Austin Ofokwu that Oganwu remembered hailed from Ilah. He also mentioned Pa John Ojidoh, a veteran sports administrator who at his young age coached track and field, football before becoming an officiating official in athletics and a referee in football. ‘’Pa Ojidoh may not be strong now otherwise he would have been here today,’’ Uduaghan said of the 86 year veteran who still finds time to comment current sports matters. Ojidoh was reacting to developments during the Nations Cup. On January 16, few days to Nigeria’s first match at the Nations Cup, I visited Ojidoh at his home in Ilah. On a sick bed, he spoke on sports, recalling dates in such a manner that marvelled me. His body may be weak but his brain was still sharp. It was my first visit to Ilah and when I told him that I liked the town he cut this way: ‘’It’s a peaceful place. The white men, the missionaries came here in 1888, before they got to Asaba. Ilah produced the first black and non priest (Lay) to be Principal of the famous St. Gregory’s College in Obalende, Lagos. His name was Paul Amenechi. His younger brother, Patrick was first Nigerian to obtain First Class Honours in Chemistry at the University of Ibadan. Ilah produced the first West African female Architect in Joy Ugboda, an elder sister of Mrs Ifeajuna. Julius Chigbolu set British and Commonwealth High Jump record in 1954 with a jump of 6.94 mark. He was from Ilah. We can go on and on about the people of Ilah. Austin Ofokwu, a one time captain of the Eagles came from here. Stephen Keshi is from here and before Keshi was Mathew Onyema who was Eagles captain in acting capacity. I wish Keshi wins the Nations Cup so that he can be among the greats from Ilah.’’ And when this happened and Uduaghan was hosting the team he commended the feat from Ilah people and spoke of a possibility of citing a football academy in Ilah. He respects the potentials the town churns out and hopes that there could be more stars from Ilah. That will be commendable. It is a town that has produced stars and ready to continue if the academy comes to town. Oganwu is interested and wishes this to happen. Vanguard News The post Before Emmanuel Uduaghan died! appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: Police bust money laundering networks involved in $2m fraud, arrest 8
items.description: By Kingsley Omonobi The Nigerian Police Force National Cybercrime Centre has busted an online investment fraud and romance scam syndicate and well as money laundering network involving the scamming of victims abroad of over $2million Assistant Inspector General of Police in charge NPF-NCCC, Akaniyene Ezima made this known while briefing on arrested suspects linked to digital and online cyber fraud in Abuja. Ezima said, “The first case arose from intelligence shared by the United Kingdom National Crime Agency (NCA), a multinational initiative targeting online fraud networks and scam centres. ‘The intelligence indicated that social media accounts linked to a suspected transnational criminal network involved in fraudulent investment schemes targeting victims in the United States, United Kingdom, Canada and Australia and other jurisdictions were being operated from locations within Delta State, Nigeria. “Acting on this intelligence, operatives of the NPF-NCCC, through coordinated investigation and digital forensic analysis, traced the locations to Agbor and Okpanam in Delta State, leading to the arrest of four suspects in October 2026. “The suspects are Ojei Divine, Godwin Umerin, Edema Bright and Peter Kpamichukwu Okoh. “Preliminary investigation revealed that the suspects allegedly employed synthetic identities across social media and messaging platforms to target unsuspecting victims abroad. ‘One of the suspects, Ojei Divine impersonated professional investment traders by using facebook accounts bearing different IDs which included one Mariana Coman and redirected victims from Chatgroups which he created to fraudulent investment websites namely www.andescapitalgrouplc.com, www.navidargroupllc.com and www.stockbase.com. “The websites presented themselves as investment and trading platforms on forex, cryptocurrency, and Oil & Gas – where victims deposits funds in wallets controlled and assessed by the suspect and his syndicate. “The suspect has admitted to moving the proceeds of his crime from different wallet addresses created for victim’s he targets in different countries – including Revolut Trust wallet for European victims and Coinbase for victims from the United States. “Cryptocurrency analysis from one of the wallets controlled by the suspect disclosed 21 approved cryptocurrency transaction receipts amounting to a total of USD 21,150. The team recovered crypto assets worth USD 15,900 which is now secured in a custodial wallet. “Godwin Umerin, a member of the cyber gang, created several Facebook accounts which he admitted to have used in victimizing an Indonesian citizen who paid 7,000,000 Indonesian Rupiah through an account provided by a money mule. “Similarly, Edema Bright, a 300-level student at Delta State University, engaged in sextortion and cryptocurrency fraud targeting victims in Australia, United Kingdom, United States, Canada and other jurisdictions. ‘The suspect posted online hookup advertisements and received responses from unsuspecting victims through a WhatsApp account registered using a United States telephone number. “Preliminary investigation revealed that Edema Bright also engaged victims through an online platform, www.clubhouse.com offering live audio conversations and persuaded them to invest in Bitcoin, claiming to purchase at lower prices and sell at higher rates. “He impersonated Michael Novogratz, CEO Galaxy Digital and used photographs obtained from Pinterest as profile pictures to conceal his identity. “The last suspect, Peter Kpamichukwu Okoh, aged 27, is a website developer and owns 360 Web Tech, an unregistered web development company. He advertised his services on Instagram and TikTok with usernames 360_webtech and 360_webtech02 respectively. “Preliminary investigation revealed that the suspect developed websites for healthcare, investment and online banking services. The online banking platforms were designed to allow administrators to control all functions, including deposits and withdrawals. “The suspect admitted to developing 6 websites used by scammers to carry out fraudulent activities.” Exhibits recovered during the operation includes 36 mobile devices, 3 routers and other exhibits now subject of forensic examination by the Center. The suspects will be arraigned before a court of competent jurisdiction upon conclusion of the necessary investigative and prosecutorial processes. AIG Ezima said, “The second case involves an intelligence-led investigation undertaken by the NPF-NCCC in collaboration with the Royal Canadian Mounted Police (RCMP) and the German Federal Criminal Police Office, Bundeskriminalamt (BKA). “Intelligence received from the RCMP revealed the activities of a suspected Nigeria-based romance fraud network which targeted elderly residents of Canada between 2020 and 2024. “Preliminary investigation indicated that members of the network employed fictitious identities on social media and messaging platforms to establish deceptive romantic relationships with unsuspecting victims. “Having gained their trust, the threat actors solicited funds under various pretences, including purported business investments, financial assistance and loans with promises of repayment. “In one instance, a victim was deceived by a threat actor who impersonated a United States Military physician, William Barabash and sent log-in details of a fake bank website called ‘CB Reserve’ Bank which displaying huge bank balance under the name of the said William Barabash. “Having built trust, the victim subsequently transferred over CA$200,000 between 2020 and 2022. Further investigation linked the transaction to one Uka Chidiebere Gerald ‘M’, 32 years old who with the consent of his wife, Evelyn Ayabare used her email address and phone number, to open a Binance wallet through which funds toalling USDT 1,684,441 was laundered. “Another victim was induced into making cryptocurrency transfers in the sum of CA$214,000 and a wire transfer of CA$3,000. The said digital assets were deposited into two Bitcoin wallet addresses which were traced to one Kenneth Ufuophu, ‘M’, 30 years. “These digital assets were similarly laundered through money mules identified as Tears of Joy LTD (United Kingdom), Henryford Services Inc. and other jurisdictions which includes Canada, the United States, Nigeria, Turkey and Kenya. “So far, five victims have been identified, with the documented financial losses of two victims alone exceeding Four Hundred and Seventeen Thousand Canadian Dollars (CA$417,000). “Acting on the intelligence, operatives of the NPF-NCCC, through digital forensic analysis and coordinated investigation, traced aspects of the financial transactions to Nigeria, leading to the arrest of two suspects in Delta State. “The suspects are Uka Chidiebere Gerald, 32 years old, and Kenneth Ufuophu, 30 years old. Exhibits recovered during the operation include 2 mobile devices and 2 laptops, which are undergoing forensic examination at the Center.” The NPF-NCCC, in collaboration with its partners, said they are sustaining efforts to identify and apprehend other members of the suspected criminal network, trace the movement of illicit funds and facilitate the recovery of proceeds of crime. “The third case arose from cyber threat intelligence shared by the United Kingdom National Crime Agency (NCA) concerning suspected cyber threat actors involved in computer-related fraud, online impersonation and fraudulent investment and wealth management fraud targeting victims across international jurisdictions. “Acting on the intelligence report approved by the Inspector-General of Police, operatives of the NPF-NCCC conducted a coordinated intelligence-led operation in Lekki, Lagos State, on 14th October 2026, leading to the arrest of three suspects. “The suspects are Adebayo Adewale Basit, Omoregie Christian and Adebayo Ibrahim. Preliminary investigation revealed that the suspects allegedly operated fictitious social media accounts to impersonate prominent celebrities and other personalities, with the intention of deceiving unsuspecting victims into transferring funds. “One of the suspects, Adebayo Adewale Basit, aged 23 years, created emails with the ID: elonmuskkit214@gmail.com, elonmusk07588@gmail.com and used his Facebook, WhatsApp, Zangi, Telegram and X account to communicate with victims using Ai Voice cloning, Deep Fake to impersonate the CEO of Tesla, Elon Musk. “These activities targeted victims across different jurisdictions, particularly the United States of America and the United Kingdom. The suspects were also involved in fraudulent cryptocurrency investment representation through a platform identified as Bitcoin Trading Hub. “They used the website bitcointradinghub.org and email address support@bitcointradinghub.org During investigation, the suspects confessed to their involvement in the alleged fraudulent activities. “Exhibits recovered during the operation include: Five iPhones of different models, one Samsung Galaxy mobile phone, one iPad and one Microsoft Surface Pro tablet. Three internet routers, one webcam, one PlayStation 5 console with two controllers, a portable UPS, a charging adapter and two MTN SIM card Three gold-plated necklaces, two wristwatches, two vehicle registration plates, two suspected cannabis crushers, a digital precision scale and rolling papers. “The recovered digital devices are undergoing forensic examination at the NPF-NCCC Cybercrime Laboratory to establish the extent of the alleged criminal activities, identify victims, trace suspected proceeds of crime and determine the possible involvement of other accomplices. “The three suspects are currently in custody, while investigation continues with a view to ensuring that all persons found culpable are brought before the law.” AIG Ezima expressed concern over the deliberate exploitation of public trust through fraudulent investment schemes, deceptive online relationships, identity impersonation and the movement of illicit funds through multiple financial channels, including cryptocurrency. His words, “The Nigeria Police Force recognises that effectively addressing these emerging threats requires more than reactive enforcement. It demands proactive, intelligence-led policing, advanced digital forensic capabilities, timely intelligence sharing and sustained international cooperation. “Under the leadership of the Inspector-General of Police, IGP Olatunji Rilwan Disu, the NPF-NCCC will continue to strengthen its investigative and forensic capabilities, deepen strategic partnerships and deploy technology in identifying, disrupting and dismantling criminal networks operating within and beyond Nigeria’s borders.” The post Police bust money laundering networks involved in $2m fraud, arrest 8 appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: Approvisionnement en carburant : la tutelle annonce un retour à la normale à partir de ce samedi
items.description: L'approvisionnement en carburant à travers la capitale sénégalaise reviendra à la normale à partir de ce samedi 24 octobre 2026. C’est ce qu’a indiqué le ministère de l’Énergie et du Pétrole à travers un communiqué de presse. Ce vendredi 23 octobre 2026, des files d'attente ont été observées devant certaines stations-service, dont l'approvisionnement en supercarburant et en gasoil a été perturbé. Cette situation s'explique, selon la tutelle, par les difficultés d'acheminement nées du mouvement de grève générale de trois jours auquel ont pris part les transporteurs d'hydrocarbures. « Le ministère de l'Énergie et du Pétrole tient à rassurer les populations. Les dépôts pétroliers disposent de stocks de supercarburant et de gasoil. Les perturbations observées ne sont donc pas liées à un manque de carburant, mais à l'interruption des livraisons vers les stations », renseigne la tutelle à travers son communiqué. A lire aussi : Carburants automobiles : ajustement des prix du supercarburant et du gasoil à partir de ce samedi La fin de ce mouvement de grève, poursuit le texte, ce vendredi, permet la reprise des livraisons. Ainsi, le ministère affirme que dans quelques heures, à compter du samedi 24 octobre 2026, les stations-service concernées seront réapprovisionnées et la distribution retrouvera son cours normal. Sur ce, il invite les usagers à éviter les achats de précaution, afin de ne pas ralentir le retour à une distribution normale. Mariama DIEME
