items.title: EES, ETIAS and €20 Fee: How confusion over Europe’s new border systems fuels visa scam
items.description: By Vera Anyagafu A new digital stamp at Europe’s airports is free. The €20 travel authorisation some Nigerians are talking about does not apply to Nigerian visa applicants to Europe. Yet from Instagram vendors in Surulere to travel plazas in Onitsha, agents are charging Nigerian travellers up to N250,000 for both. Since 10 April 2026, every Nigerian arriving in Paris or Frankfurt on a short-stay Schengen visa no longer gets an ink stamp. A camera and fingerprint scanner logs you into Europe’s Entry/Exit System (EES) automatically, at no cost. The other system, the European Travel Information and Authorisation System (ETIAS), is the source of the rumour. It will eventually cost €20, valid for three years, but it is only for travellers who do not need a visa to enter Europe, like Americans, British, Australians and Canadians. For Nigerians, who still need a Schengen visa, ETIAS is never required. If someone in Nigeria is charging you for it, you are paying for something you do not need. That gap is where the exploitation happens. The EES became fully operational on 10 April 2026 across all 29 Schengen countries. You do not apply for it in advance. When you land in Paris or Frankfurt, you look at a camera, place your fingers on a scanner, and your entry is recorded digitally, replacing the old ink stamp. It applies to all non-European nationals on short stays, which includes every Nigerian travelling on a Schengen visa, and it automatically calculates your period of stay. ETIAS is different. It is a pre-travel check only for visa-exempt travellers, people who do not need a Schengen visa to visit Europe. For Nigerians who need a visa, ETIAS is never required. If you need a Schengen visa today, you will continue to use the visa process through VFS Global or TLSContact in Lagos and Abuja. The official fee for ETIAS, when it eventually launches, will be €20 for travellers aged 18 to 70, free for under 18 and over 70, and any additional charges will go to commercial intermediaries. The only official website where the application will be available once launched is the European Union’s official ETIAS portal, and the information portal for both systems is the official Travel Europe portal managed by the European Union. And for travellers who will eventually need it, the system is not yet open. The official portal has made it clear that no action is required at this time, and any website currently offering to process an application is not legitimate. HOW THE SCAM WORKS Consular Hub gathered that the European authorities have already identified over a hundred unofficial websites providing information on ETIAS. These sites use convincing designs and domain names to mimic legitimate portals. Since the programme is on hold, any site requesting a €20 fee today is considered fraudulent. Travellers are warned to be very cautious because it is not currently possible to apply for an official ETIAS authorisation since the system is not operational yet. Many of these third-party sites charge inflated fees or steal personal information. In Nigeria the pattern is now familiar. Take Sola, a 28-year-old applicant in Surulere. A travel agent on Instagram operating as Travel with Tayo told her she needed to pay N65,000 naira for mandatory ETIAS registration before her Schengen visa appointment at VFS Global. She paid and was given a receipt that looked official with a European Union logo. At her appointment, VFS Global told her ETIAS does not apply to Nigerians and the paper was worthless. Or Emeka, a trader in Onitsha who wanted to visit his brother in Milan. An agent in his local plaza operating as Blessed Travels collected tens of thousands of naira, for EES biometric pre-registration and ETIAS approval, promising fast-track entry. He arrived in Rome to find his entry under EES was recorded fresh at the border anyway and the extra papers meant nothing. TO STAY SAFE To stay safe as a Nigerian passport holder, remember three things; You do not pay €20 for ETIAS, you pay about €90 for the Schengen visa itself at VFS Global or TLSContact. The Entry/Exit System costs nothing and you do not pre-register for it. And only use the official portals for information, as the protection of your personal data cannot be guaranteed if you use another website. items.title: Mir Raza murder case: Sindh govt asks agencies, Sindh Rangers to nominate JIT members
items.description: The Sindh government has written to the Inter-Services Intelligence (ISI), the Intelligence Bureau (IB), the National Cyber Crime Investigation Agency and the Sindh Rangers to nominate members to a joint investigation team (JIT), recommended by a judicial panel , to investigate Mir Raza Ali’s murder, it emerged on Saturday. The 25-year-old businessman had gone missing on July 28 after leaving his home in PECHS, and his body, bearing a gunshot wound, was found in the bushes in Gulistan-i-Jauhar a day later. In its 62-page report , submitted to the government on October 15, a commission had recommended forming a JIT, calling it a “most viable path” to mitigate ongoing reputational damage to the Sindh government. Sindh High Court judge Justice Omar Sial, who headed the single-member commission, recommended integrating senior representatives from the ISI, IB, Sindh Rangers, and the NCCIA in the JIT to “ensure an impartial, comprehensive, and credible resolution”. The commission had also recommended West Deputy Inspector General of Police (DIG) Irfan Baloch to lead the team. Acting on the commission’s directives, the Sindh Home Minister, on Thursday, announced that the JIT would be formed under the DIG Baloch, and the summary had been sent to the chief minister. The letters, dated October 23, were sent through the Sindh Home Department and seen by Dawn . They requested the ISI, IB, NCCIA and Sindh Rangers to nominate a senior officer, not below the rank of BS-18, to serve on the JIT headed by DIG Baloch to investigate Mir Raza’s murder. The letters requested the aforementioned authorities to nominate their representatives within seven days so that the JIT could commence its work. In its letter to the NCCIA, the Home Department specifically requested a senior official with “expertise in digital forensics, as the investigation involves the analysis of mobile phones, Apple Watch, iCloud, social media and cryptocurrency (Binance) records”. Letter to IGP for action against officers The provincial government, through its Home Department, also wrote to the Sindh inspector general of police (IGP), asking him to take action against police officials found guilty of negligence by the judicial commission. “This case demonstrates an epic failure by the police in their investigation,” declared the 62-page report submitted by Justice Sial. “The police breached all required procedures, both knowingly and unknowingly, necessary to withstand judicial scrutiny and a successful prosecution,” the report stated. It said the police investigation “failed in its most basic duty: to establish the truth”. According to the commission, an active cover-up in the initial stages of the investigation cannot be conclusively ruled out. It noted that senior police officers swept clear investigative lapses under the carpet, without acknowledging them, addressing them, or even attempting to do so. “Dozens of police officers – authorised and unauthorised – were involved in collecting evidence in this case, approaching and interrogating crucial persons, and in most cases not documenting it in any manner,” it said, adding that, therefore, no officer was willing to take responsibility for the lapses. Listing its observations for certain police officials involved in the case, the judicial panel identified “criminal negligence” on the part of Station House Officer (SHO) Adeel Afzal of Ferozabad police station. It also found criminal negligence by Sub-inspector Shabbir Leghari, the first investigating officer (IO) in the case, and called for disciplinary proceedings against him and his suspension. Dr Osama Sheikh suspended In its report, the judicial panel had called out “extreme immaturity” and “childish behaviour” of Medico-Legal Officer (MLO) Dr Osama Sheikh, who conducted the first medico-legal examination , whose findings were later proven incorrect after a second autopsy . “Overconfidence. Unprofessional conduct not befitting a medical professional. Must not be assigned medico-legal duties unless he has undergone at least two years of rigorous academic and practical training,” the commission observed. In a letter to the Sindh health secretary, the provincial government conveyed the decision of its sub-committee, constituted to implement the recommendations of the judicial commission, in light of the commission’s observations. Under the decision, Dr Osama would be suspended and proceeded against under the E&D (Efficiency and Discipline) Rules. He would also be sent for training, as recommended by the commission. Request to interior ministry The single-member judicial commission had stated that it did not have investigative powers and that it was difficult to conclusively determine whether an active cover-up had occurred. The commission noted that “certain inexplicable actions are difficult to justify and raise the possibility that one may have occurred”. Therefore, it recommended that a high-level committee, preferably headed by the Federal Investigation Agency (FIA), be constituted to initiate criminal proceedings against any police officials found culpable. Acting on the commission’s recommendations, the Sindh government also wrote to the Ministry of Interior. In its letter, the provincial government requested the FIA to nominate a senior officer, not below the rank of BS-20 and with expertise in investigations, to head the committee. DIG Baloch and Special Branch DIG Naeem Ahmed Sheikh would serve as its members. Examination of police officers A one-member committee comprising Additional IGP Counterterrorism Department (CTD) Sindh Zulfiqar Ali Larik had also been notified to examine each of the officers named in the commission’s report. DIG Baloch would assist the committee. According to a notification, the committee had the following terms of reference (TORs): To examine each of the officers/officials named in the report of the commission of inquiry and assess their leadership qualities and efficiency in light of the specific observations recorded against them by the Commission; To evaluate their overall policing performance; To further probe the role of Inspector Ghaus with regard to the burning of the crime scene; and To submit its report, with findings and recommendations in respect of each officer/official, to the Sindh IGP.

items.title: OKUAMA: When the court speaks, who answers?
items.description: By Akpokona Omafuaire THERE comes a moment in the life of a nation when the question is no longer what the law says, but who will listen. Read Also: Is the Nigerian Army above the law? – Okuama elders still in detention In the troubled story of Okuama, a riverine community in Delta State, that question hangs in the air like a verdict still waiting to be understood. A court may speak in the measured language of justice, its orders carefully written and its pronouncements entered into the record. But beyond the courtroom doors lies another world—one where families wait, communities wonder, and the meaning of justice is measured not merely in words, but also in what happens next. When the court speaks, who answers? The question is simple. Its implications are not. The shadow of March 14 On March 14, 2024, the killing of 17 military personnel near Okuama, Ughelli South Local Government Area, Delta State transformed a local tragedy into a national crisis. The events that followed brought military operations, arrests, displacement and the detention of community leaders. In the months that followed, the community’s story became entangled in a difficult conversation about security, accountability, due process and the protection of human rights. For the families of those killed, the loss was permanent. For residents caught in the aftermath, the uncertainty was deeply unsettling. For the detained leaders and their relatives, the passage of time raised its own questions about liberty, legal process and the right to know what lay ahead. Different lives, different losses — but one unfolding story And somewhere within that story, the question of justice refused to disappear. The courtroom and the waiting world In June 2026, the Federal High Court in Warri ordered the release of Prof. Arthur Ekpekpo and other detained Okuama leaders. A judicial order of this nature carries significance beyond the courtroom. It places an obligation on the relevant authorities to act in accordance with the law. It also invites a necessary public question: what happens after the judge has spoken? Does the order translate into actual release? Have all those covered by the ruling been accounted for? If implementation is delayed or disputed, what explanation is provided, and what lawful remedies remain available? Vanguard source confirmed that the Court orders were validly served on the military authorities. The source stated that a powerful delegation of Four Traditional Rulers and some top military brass of Urhobo nation visited the Minister of Defence, but nothing tangible is yet to be achieved. When silence becomes another question Okuama’s anguish extends beyond detention Reports emerged in December 2024 that community President-General James Oghoroko had died in military custody while treasurer Dennis Okugbaye was reported terribly sick and was later released. The military announced that an investigation into the reported deaths had been ordered. The death added another grave dimension to a story already marked by loss and uncertainty. What did the investigations establish? Were the circumstances fully documented? Were the families given clear answers? What findings, if any, have since been made public? These questions should not be answered by assumption, political convenience or rumour. They demand verifiable evidence and transparent communication from the appropriate authorities. Silence, by itself, proves neither guilt nor innocence. But where serious questions concern human lives and the conduct of public institutions, sustained uncertainty can deepen public mistrust. The answer is not louder accusation. It is credible information, lawful accountability and a process that people can examine. Who carries the responsibility? A court does not ordinarily enforce its decisions through words alone. The implementation of its orders depends on the relevant institutions and the procedures established by law. That is why the Okuama story cannot end with the announcement of a judgment. The relevant authorities must clarify the implementation status of the release order. Outstanding questions surrounding the reported death in custody require clear, evidence-based answers. The rights of affected persons must be respected, while the deaths of the 17 military personnel must remain part of the broader pursuit of accountability. These responsibilities do not cancel one another out. Demanding due process for detained community leaders does not diminish the lives of the slain military personnel. Seeking answers about custody conditions does not prejudge the outcome of an investigation. Insisting on lawful enforcement of a court order does not place anyone above the law. Rather, these demands point towards a common principle: justice must be measured by established facts, fair procedures and the faithful application of the law. The danger of an unfinished ending There is a particular sadness in stories that become quieter as the questions grow more difficult. A headline appears. Public attention rises. Officials make statements. A court issues a decision. Then the national conversation shifts, and focus moves elsewhere. But the families do not move on at the same speed as the news cycle. The consequences of detention, loss, and community displacement do not disappear when public attention fades. For Okuama, the danger is that an extraordinary sequence of events may gradually become an ordinary footnote in the nation’s political history. That would leave the most important questions suspended between what has been announced and what has been independently established. The community does not need another cycle of recrimination. It needs clarity about the status of its leaders, credible answers to outstanding questions and a path towards recovery that acknowledges the suffering of everyone affected. The final question Perhaps the real test of justice begins after the courtroom empties. When the judge has delivered a ruling and the record has been closed for the day, who ensures that the decision is implemented? Who explains delays, if any? Who provides families with reliable information? Who follows through when an investigation is announced? And who remains answerable when public attention turns elsewhere? These are not questions for the courtroom alone. They concern the institutions, procedures and public responsibilities upon which the rule of law depends. Okuama’s story remains a reminder that a judicial pronouncement can mark a turning point without necessarily resolving every question surrounding a crisis. The court may speak. The law may provide the answers. But the public must still be able to establish what happened next. For in the end, justice is not measured only by the words delivered from the bench, but also by the lawful actions that follow. And so, as Okuama waits for clarity on the questions that remain, one question continues to echo beyond the courtroom walls: When the court speaks, who answers — and who ensures that the answer becomes reality? items.title: 4 children killed as van plunges into ravine in Neelum Valley
items.description: MUZAFFARABAD: Four children were killed and three other people were injured when a van carrying them to a madrasah plunged into a ravine in the upper reaches of Neelum Valley on Saturday, officials said. Neelum Valley District Disaster Management Officer Akhtar Ayoub said the van was travelling from Nagdar, about 22 kilometres from the district headquarters of Athmuqam, via the Keran bypass link road when it plunged into a ravine. “The accident occurred around 8:30am near Ghorray Nakkah Morr in Nagdar, barely half a kilometre into the journey, as the driver negotiated a sharp bend,” he said. The van plunged more than 500 metres off the road into a rocky ravine, killing three children on the spot and initially injuring four other occupants. One of the injured children later died at the District Headquarters Hospital in Athmuqam, Ayoub said. The injured were later shifted to Muzaffarabad for treatment due to their critical condition, he added. Expressing grief over the loss of young lives, Legislative Assembly Speaker Chaudhry Tariq Farooq extended his condolences to the bereaved families and prayed for the speedy recovery of the injured. “Deeply saddened by the loss of precious young lives in the tragic accident in Neelum Valley today. My heartfelt condolences go out to the bereaved families, and I pray for the speedy recovery of the injured,” he wrote on X. “Mountain roads demand utmost caution; even a momentary lapse can have tragic consequences. Please drive carefully,” he added. A similar accident occurred in April when three people were killed, and 10 others were injured when a passenger van plunged into a deep ravine in the Maidan Nambatai area. On May 11, four people, including two women, were killed and two others injured after a passenger jeep plunged hundreds of feet into a rocky streambed.

items.title: Intertex 2026 | Le textile tunisien résiste à la crise
items.description: Environ 250 exposants issus de 20 pays participent à la huitième édition d’Intertex Tunisia 2026, un salon international de l’industrie textile et de la mode, un secteur stratégique pour les exportations tunisiennes, malgré un recul de 4,7 % des ventes à l’étranger au cours des neuf premiers mois de l’année. Ce salon, qui se tient au Parc des expositions de Sousse, du 22 au 24 octobre 2026, est organisé avec le soutien de la Fédération tunisienne du textile et de l’habillement (FTTH). Il vise à renforcer les échanges commerciaux et les partenariats industriels entre des entreprises africaines, européennes et asiatiques. Le ministre du Commerce et du Développement des exportations, Samir Abid, qui a assisté à l’inauguration, a souligné la vocation internationale des entreprises locales ainsi que leur capacité à s’adapter aux difficultés du marché. Lors de ses échanges avec les professionnels du secteur, il a insisté sur la nécessité de consolider la présence des entreprises tunisiennes, tant sur le marché intérieur qu’à l’étranger, en renforçant leur compétitivité et leurs capacités à l’export. Le salon réunit des fabricants de tissus, de vêtements, de fils, de machines industrielles et d'accessoires. Une attention particulière est portée aux innovations technologiques, à la durabilité et aux nouvelles opportunités d'approvisionnement. La FTTH y est présente avec un pavillon national destiné à promouvoir le savoir-faire et le potentiel des entreprises tunisiennes sur les marchés internationaux. Le secteur du textile et de l'habillement constitue l’un des piliers de l’industrie manufacturière nationale, comptant environ 1 500 entreprises et 155 000 employés. En 2025, ses exportations ont atteint environ 9,5 milliards de dinars, soit 2,9 milliards d’euros. La conjoncture demeure toutefois complexe : selon l’Institut national de la statistique (INS), au cours des neuf premiers mois de 2026, les exportations de l’ensemble textile, habillement et cuir ont reculé de 4,7 % par rapport à la même période de l’année précédente. Les relations industrielles avec l’Italie revêtent une importance particulière ; l’Italie constitue en effet le deuxième marché de destination pour l’habillement tunisien, avec des exportations s’élevant à environ 1,6 milliard de dinars en 2025. En mai dernier, dans le cadre d’une initiative promue par le Centre de promotion des exportations (Cepex), dix entreprises tunisiennes ont participé, à Milan, à plus d’une centaine de rencontres d’affaires avec une quarantaine d’opérateurs italiens du secteur de la mode. L’objectif est de renforcer l’intégration des chaînes de production entre les deux rives de la Méditerranée, en tirant parti de la proximité géographique de la Tunisie, de sa flexibilité productive et de la possibilité de réduire les délais de livraison vers les marchés européens. items.title: Mourinho must stop Barca machine as Clasico tensions resume
items.description: Real Madrid coach Jose Mourinho will renew one of football’s most bitter rivalries on Sunday when he takes charge of his first Clasico since returning to the club, with La Liga leaders Barcelona awaiting him at Camp Nou. The Portuguese veteran’s first spell at Madrid was defined in large part by his battle to end Barca’s dominance under Pep Guardiola, with relations between the Spanish giants slumping to their lowest ebb. Mourinho managed to break Barca’s spell by guiding Real Madrid to the Spanish title in 2012, the crowning achievement of his reign from 2010-13. Clasicos became increasingly compelling during that period, some would say not for the right reasons, as he and his staff clashed with their Barcelona counterparts both pitch-side and verbally in the media. The 63-year-old worked as an assistant at Barca under Bobby Robson and Louis van Gaal in the 1990s but was overlooked for Guardiola in 2008 when the Catalans replaced Frank Rijkaard. Mourinho’s frequent battles with Guardiola, Lionel Messi and even with Madrid’s own icons like Iker Casillas sometimes overshadowed his sporting achievements. The most infamous flashpoint was when Mourinho poked then Barca assistant coach Tito Vilanova in the eye in August 2011. Earlier that year, at the end of the prior season, Madrid and Barca clashed four times in just 18 days, illustrating the intensity of the rivalry. The first was in La Liga, a 1-1 draw, which helped Barcelona take a step towards retaining the Spanish title as Madrid trailed them. Mourinho’s Madrid beat Barca to win the Copa del Rey in the second, with Cristiano Ronaldo scoring the winner in extra-time. Then the Catalans got the better of Los Blancos in a Champions League semi-final double header, winning the first leg 2-0 in the Santiago Bernabeu, with Madrid defender Pepe sent off. Mourinho called it a “scandal”. Barcelona held Real Madrid to a 1-1 draw in the second leg to reach the final, which they went on to win. It was in this period that Guardiola said he could not and would not compete with the “boss” Mourinho in the press room. – Stopping Flick’s Barca – Mourinho has hit the ground running in his second spell at Madrid in that regard. The coach brandished print-outs of incidents after losing the derby clash to try and prove his point that Atletico Madrid deserved two red cards, and refused to attend a press conference after Vinicius Junior was sent off against Villarreal. Many believe Mourinho employs these tactics as a distraction to take the pressure off his team when they are not performing. A victory in the Clasico might encourage him to focus on the football, and stopping Hansi Flick’s side — back-to-back Spanish champions — is one of the main reasons he was rehired by president Florentino Perez. Flick’s Barca have won six of seven Clasicos against Real Madrid since the German arrived, scoring 22 goals and shipping only 11. Mourinho insists it is impossible for his team to be at the level he wants them to be at after such a short time in charge. “I’ve been here for over a hundred days. Obviously, we are not where I want, but there are things we are doing better today than before,” said the coach. Madrid have won their last four matches between La Liga and the Champions League, and after sharing minutes around early in the season, some preferences are emerging. Although Mourinho said initially he did not see midfielder Federico Valverde as a right-back, where he has been used in the past, he has selected the Uruguayan there in the last two games, ahead of Denzel Dumfries and Trent Alexander-Arnold. “We created a lot on that side, and Fede had a fantastic match,” said Mourinho after the Leipzig win. In Valverde’s place in midfield Mourinho deployed Arda Guler against Sevilla on Sunday and then Bernardo Silva against the German side, with Madrid improving on the ball and retaining more possession. However the Clasico poses a different challenge. Mourinho, who deployed defender Pepe in midfield against Barca, may revert to type to try and spoil the hosts’ flowing football. items.title: Stonebwoy donates GHS100,000 to Black Challenge ahead of Amputee World Cup
items.description: Ghanaian dancehall artiste Stonebwoy has donated GHS100,000 to the Ghana Amputee Football National Team, the Black Challenge, ahead of their participation in the 2026 Amputee Football World Cup in Mexico. The award-winning musician visited the team’s training session at Mensah Sarbah Park on the University of Ghana campus to motivate and encourage the players ahead of the tournament before making the donation. “I’m supporting them with GHS100,000. This is a token from me and the Burna Boy Music Group. This is not much at all, but I know it will go a long way to support the group,” he said. Stonebwoy also called for increased financial support for the team as they prepare to represent Ghana on the global stage. “We need funds directed to the Amputee team so that they can continue to perform because these are people’s fathers, uncles and our own brothers, and they’re representing the nation,” he added. The musician further commended the President of the National Paralympic Committee of Ghana, Samson Deen, for his leadership and commitment to the team. “I want to say thank you to the President of NPC Ghana, President Samson Deen, a great man. He has carried a lot on his shoulders, and may God continue to open his wings and bless him so he can continue to make people happy,” Stonebwoy said. The Black Challenge have been drawn in Group D for the 2026 Amputee Football World Cup in Mexico, where they will compete against Angola, Iraq and Colombia. The team are expected to depart Ghana for Mexico in the coming days as preparations continue for the tournament.

items.title: L’amère leçon de 60 ans de relations tuniso-européennes
items.description: Au terme de soixante ans de relations avec l’Union européenne, la Tunisie est passée peu à peu du statut de négociateur cherchant à obtenir des conditions plus équitables à celui de récepteur passif d’un agenda européen conçu ailleurs. Cette leçon amère est tirée de l’ouvrage intitulé «Les relations Tunisie-Union européenne: six décennies d’histoire»** de Mohamed Sassi paru en 2025 aux éditions Nirvana, à Tunis. Et qui propose une histoire critique de ces relations, conduite selon la méthode de l’histoire économique et des relations internationales, qui s’appuie sur les archives nationales tunisiennes et européennes ainsi que sur des témoignages d’acteurs économiques et politiques. Adel Ben Youssef * L’auteur n’est pas un historien comme les autres. Il a d’abord soutenu à Sorbonne Université une thèse de doctorat portant sur l’entreprise pétrolière française Desmarais Frères, puis mené des recherches postdoctorales à l’Université Paris-IV et à l’Université de Genève, son regard glissant peu à peu de l’histoire des entreprises vers l’histoire économique tunisienne et celle de ses relations extérieures. Cette formation transdisciplinaire lui donne les moyens d’aborder les archives des négociations tuniso-CEE avec la précision de l’historien économiste et l’ampleur de vue de l’historien des relations internationales. Il est actuellement Maître de conférences à l’Institut préparatoire aux études littéraires et aux sciences humaines de Tunis (IPELSHT, Université de Tunis 1), où il enseigne l’histoire économique, ainsi que l’histoire des relations internationales à l’Ena (Université Tunis El Manar) et pilote un axe de recherche lié à sa spécialité au sein du Laboratoire Diraset, Études maghrébines à la FLSH de Tunis. La contribution académique la plus visible du livre tient à son socle archivistique. Mohamed Sassi dépouille de façon systématique les archives nationales tunisiennes, en particulier celles du ministère des Affaires étrangères versées en 2012, et s’appuie sur des entretiens avec les principaux négociateurs tunisiens des années 1970 à 1990, dont le regretté Tahar Sioud. Le croisement de l’archive et de l’histoire orale permet de restituer des coulisses de négociation et des logiques décisionnelles jusqu’ici mal documentées. Dans son compte rendu pour l’Académie des sciences d’outre-mer, Jacques Frémeaux salue un livre «bien documenté, notamment grâce à la consultation des archives et à une enquête orale auprès de personnalités tunisiennes» , et relève qu’il retrace «avec précision et finesse» le passage de la Tunisie d’une économie tournée vers la France à l’époque du protectorat à la négociation avec une Communauté européenne en construction et en élargissement. T rois «tournants» et une ligne structurelle Mohamed Sassi bâtit un récit limpide, teinté de tragique : depuis l’indépendance, les relations économiques de la Tunisie avec l’Europe ont traversé trois moments décisifs, et aucun n’a tenu ses promesses. Le premier tournant correspond au premier accord de coopération de 1969. Les négociations avaient commencé dès 1963, année de l’indépendance tunisienne et de la signature du traité de Rome. Or, d’après Sassi, cet accord est bien loin de combler les attentes tunisiennes : l’éventail des produits couverts reste trop étroit et les produits agricoles tunisiens en sont presque absents. Pour un pays dont l’économie repose sur l’agriculture, cette lacune réduit radicalement la portée réelle de l’accord. Dans un entretien antérieur, Sassi va jusqu’à parler d’ «échec» à propos des négociations de 1963 à 1969, «premier tournant manqué» de l’histoire économique tunisienne. Le deuxième tournant est la convention de coopération de 1976. Le texte représente un progrès : un plus grand nombre de produits obtiennent des facilités à l’exportation, des clauses économiques et sociales sont ajoutées, un prêt bancaire d’un montant substantiel est prévu, et la situation des travailleurs tunisiens en Europe s’améliore. Mais l’analyse critique de Sassi met au jour un problème plus profond : le dispositif enferme en fait la Tunisie dans un rôle de sous-traitance et de transformation à bas coût, les gains d’exportation à court terme dissimulant l’arrêt de la montée en gamme de l’appareil productif. Quand la Grèce (1981), puis l’Espagne et le Portugal (1986) rejoignent la CEE, ces nouveaux membres entrent en concurrence directe avec les pays du Maghreb sur de nombreux produits ; la «Politique méditerranéenne globale» (PMG) lancée alors par la Communauté est jugée par Sassi «plus ambitieuse que ses résultats» . Le troisième tournant, c’est l’accord d’association de 1995 et le processus de Barcelone. C’est la partie la plus développée et la plus critique du livre. En apparence, Barcelone promettait une hausse notable de l’aide financière et un encouragement à l’économie de marché ; côté européen, les privatisations et la réforme tarifaire engagées par la Tunisie dans les années 1990 passaient pour des signaux positifs. Sassi met toutefois en évidence deux conséquences que le récit dominant passe sous silence. D’abord, le processus de Barcelone repose institutionnellement sur des accords bilatéraux : l’Union négocie séparément avec la Tunisie, le Maroc, l’Algérie. Pour Sassi, ce dispositif a objectivement fait obstacle à l’intégration régionale maghrébine et, après l’échec de l’Union du Maghreb arabe (UMA) créée en 1989, a enfoncé la Tunisie dans l’isolement. Or, quand 80 % du commerce tunisien dépend de l’Europe, cet isolement se traduit par une perte systématique de marge de négociation. Ensuite, le principe de réciprocité inscrit dans l’accord de 1995 contenait une bombe à retardement. Conformément aux règles de l’OMC, la Tunisie disposait d’une période transitoire de douze ans avant l’ouverture complète de son marché. Or la révolution de 2011 a éclaté précisément au moment où cette période s’achevait et où la réciprocité allait s’appliquer pleinement. Dans un entretien de 2025, Sassi souligne explicitement que la collision entre la révolution et l’ouverture du marché a infligé à la Tunisie un double choc sans le moindre amortisseur. L’après 2011 : désordre, concurrence et perte de subjectivité Le traitement de l’après-2011 est tout aussi lucide et mordant. La révolution a beau avoir apporté un espoir politique, elle a durablement abîmé la croissance tunisienne. Malgré l’obtention en 2012 d’un statut de «partenaire privilégié» dans le cadre européen, la relation n’a pas entamé l’asymétrie structurelle. Deux forces nouvelles entrent alors en jeu : la Turquie, puissance régionale émergente, et la Chine, dont la pression économique concurrence les positions tunisiennes, réduisant encore l’espace de manœuvre déjà restreint du pays. La discussion consacrée aux négociations de l’Accord de libre-échange complet et approfondi (Aleca) prolonge la posture critique de Sassi. Il estime que la partie tunisienne y est en position de faiblesse manifeste, faute d’avoir su traduire ses besoins de développement en agenda de négociation. Ce jugement fait écho à sa thèse centrale : «la Tunisie doit redevenir actrice de son lien à l’Europe» . Pour Sassi, la leçon amère de soixante ans de relations avec l’Europe est que la Tunisie est passée peu à peu du statut de négociateur cherchant à obtenir des conditions plus équitables à celui de récepteur passif d’un agenda européen conçu ailleurs. Un incontournable ouvrage de référence La valeur du livre de Mohamed Sassi ne tient pas à un jugement simpliste, «pro-européen» ou «anti-européen» , mais à la patience de l’historien qui restitue une série de négociations en apparence techniques comme un terrain où se croisent choix politiques et contraintes structurelles. Il montre comment la logique européenne, de la Politique méditerranéenne globale au processus de Barcelone puis à la Politique européenne de voisinage, a continuellement privilégié, sous le discours de la «coopération» , les intérêts agricoles, l’accès aux marchés et les impératifs de stabilité de l’Europe elle-même ; et il n’élude pas davantage les myopies, l’impréparation et l’érosion de la capacité de négociation du côté tunisien. Tunisie – UE | «Souveraineté supposée et flagrante subordination» Le compte rendu de l’Académie des sciences d’outre-mer présente ce livre comme «un heureux produit de la coopération universitaire franco-tunisienne» . Vu plus largement, il offre un récit venu de la rive sud, appuyé sur des archives de première main, qui remet en cause une histoire des relations euro-méditerranéennes longtemps écrite depuis Bruxelles. Pour qui veut comprendre pourquoi un pays lié à l’Europe par six décennies de relations institutionnalisées a fini par s’enfoncer dans un approfondissement de la dépendance et une perte de subjectivité, l’ouvrage de Sassi constitue une référence incontournable. Cet ouvrage ne se limite donc pas à une lecture : les personnes et les bibliothèques universitaires qui s'intéressent aux relations entre la Tunisie et l'Europe, des années soixante à aujourd'hui, ont tout intérêt à s'en procurer un exemplaire. Pour résumer, ce livre ne s’adresse pas uniquement aux lecteurs curieux des rapports entre la Tunisie et l’Europe, des années soixante à nos jours : il concerne aussi les responsables de bibliothèques universitaires, qui auraient tout avantage à en acquérir un exemplaire. * Université de Sousse) . ** Le livre est tiré d’un mémoire d’habilitation à diriger des recherches ( HDR) que l’enseignant universitaire a soutenu à l’u niversité La Sorbonne , le 3 juillet 2024 , devant un jury présidé par Dominique Bargot, secrétaire perpétuel de l’Académie des sciences d’outre-mer et professeur émérite à la même u niversité, et dont j’ étais le rapporteur externe, aux côtés des professeurs Olivier Forcade, Frédéric Turpin (Sorbonne Université) et Samia El Mechat (Université de Côte d’Azur/Nice). L’article L’amère leçon de 60 ans de relations tuniso-européennes est apparu en premier sur Kapitalis .

items.title: APC-PCC accuses Atiku of using AI to discredit Kaduna campaign flag-off
items.description: By Omeiza Ajayi The All Progressives Congress Presidential Campaign Council APC-PCC has accused former Vice President Atiku Abubakar and the African Democratic Congress ADC of plotting to use Artificial Intelligence deepfake videos and counterfeit documents to discredit the party’s presidential campaign flag-off in Kaduna today. In a statement on Saturday, the council’s Spokesperson, Dele Alake, said: “We have uncovered a well-orchestrated, devious plan by former Vice President Atiku Abubakar and his party to discredit the All Progressives Congress presidential campaign flag-off in Kaduna today, Saturday, October 24th, 2026.” According to the council, the ADC and its presidential candidate “have perfected their plans to misinform and disinform the public, manipulate public opinion through fake news operations and planting of false news in mainstream news platforms and social media with the use of Artificial Intelligence, deepfake videos, and counterfeit documents.” The statement said the target was the Kaduna rally, President Bola Tinubu, Governor Uba Sani and leaders of the party. It said the tactics had already been deployed in the last 24 hours, beginning with “the mischievous release of a picture of a security vehicle on a routine patrol, innocuously stationed at a junction near one of APC’s numerous campaign billboards in Kaduna metropolis.” The council claimed that Atiku and the ADC “twisted the narrative, claiming the security agents were there to protect the APC billboards in Kaduna,” and then planted the story in “a national newspaper known for its anti-government and anti-APC editorial stance.” “Immediately after the newspaper published the fake, distorted story, Atiku Abubakar, in a coordinated manner, latched onto it and shared it on his official social media handles to generate traffic and trends,” the statement said. The second incident, it said, was a fake letter released online, “purportedly written by Governor Uba Sani and addressed to the Director-General of the APC Presidential Campaign Council, Senator Abdulaziz Yari, on the release of N2.3 trillion by the Kaduna State Government to host the APC rally.” The council however dismissed the claim as absurd. “We are still at a loss as to how anyone can imagine and concoct this senseless and utterly baseless lie that defies logic and basic common sense. How much is the entire annual revenue of Kaduna State, or any state, for that matter, that a state would spend N2.3 trillion to host a rally? The N2.3 trillion that Atiku and his hirelings are circulating online is more than Kaduna State’s annual budget for three years. “For context, the combined Kaduna State budgets for 2024 (N458.271 billion), 2025 (N790.439 billion), and 2026 (N985.9 billion) are still less than N2.3 trillion,” the statement said. The council warned that these two incidents were only part of a bigger scheme. “The ADC and Atiku’s hirelings have also perfected plans to circulate old, doctored, and deepfake videos as the rally gets underway later today to show purported resentment by the people. “It is a fact that Atiku Abubakar and the ADC, his special-purpose vehicle, are incapable of winning any election. They will pull any strings, no matter how despicable and atrocious, to stay afloat in their desperate bid to grab power at all costs. “We urge Nigerians to be vigilant and reject their machinations,” the statement said. The post APC-PCC accuses Atiku of using AI to discredit Kaduna campaign flag-off appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: Trump orders lawsuit to block Alaska Senate result if Republicans lose
items.description: President Donald Trump on Friday said he ordered a Justice Department lawsuit seeking to prevent certification of Alaska’s Senate election result if the Republican incumbent loses — ramping up questions over whether he will accept midterms defeat. “I’m the one that said, ‘Do it,'” Trump announced during a trip to Florida, where he is due to cast his own early ballot for the November 3 election to decide control of Congress — currently in Republican hands. The extraordinary intervention by a president to launch a preemptive challenge against a possible election result casts a new shadow over the midterms. Trump — who tried to overthrow the 2020 presidential election after he lost to Democrat Joe Biden — has repeatedly questioned the validity of the upcoming election in which Democrats are forecasted to make big gains. If Democrats win the House of Representatives, as widely expected, they would be able to exert the first real brake on Trump’s unprecedented exercise of power since he secured his second term two years ago. Democrats also have an outside chance of winning the Senate if they can flip a handful of Republican-held seats, including in Alaska, where incumbent Republican Senator Dan Sullivan faces Democrat Mary Peltola. She called the lawsuit “corruption” in a post on X. – Sullivan v Sullivan – In its lawsuit, filed Thursday, the Justice Department alleged that the presence on the Alaska ballot of a minor additional candidate named Dan J. Sullivan Jr. is part of a deliberate ploy to confuse voters and harm the Republican incumbent’s chances. “The sole purpose of his candidacy is to benefit the Peltola campaign by reducing the number of votes for Senator Sullivan,” the lawsuit said. Democrats and Sullivan Jr. himself, a registered Republican, have denied this. The lawsuit asks for certification of a Democratic win to be held up pending investigation if the Republican incumbent’s losing margin is smaller than the votes won by his namesake. Attorney General Todd Blanche, who has repeatedly broken Washington norms about keeping political distance from the White House, said Thursday that the Justice Department was not preparing to interfere in the midterms. But he refused to rule out what he called a “doomsday scenario.” “To say that there’s no circumstances that we would ever do that. Of course, I’m not going to say that.” Democrats have accused the Trump administration of seeking ways to steer the results of the November vote by trying to expand federal government control over state-run elections and by repeatedly questioning the integrity of results. Trump won Alaska by 13 percentage points in his 2024 comeback election. But amid growing discontent with Republicans and Trump nationwide, Peltola, a former tribal judge and Alaska Native, is running a strong race. Alaska is a vast state with a population of just 740,000. Legal analyst Derek Muller described the Department of Justice’s case as “absurdly thin” and unlikely to prevail in court. “There’s essentially no likelihood of success,” Muller wrote on the Election Law Blog. Sullivan Jr. was briefly ejected from the ballot this summer, but he was reinstated by an Alaskan lower court — a decision affirmed by the state’s supreme court. items.title: La Tunisie interdit la pêche au corail rouge jusqu’au 31 décembre 2026
items.description: Le ministère de l’Agriculture, des Ressources hydrauliques et de la Pêche a décidé d’interdire la pêche au corail rouge sur l’ensemble des côtes tunisiennes jusqu'au 31 décembre 2026. Cette décision se fonde sur le procès-verbal de la réunion du comité consultatif chargé de la réglementation de la pêche — tenue le 28 septembre 2026 — ainsi que sur l’ensemble des textes législatifs et réglementaires régissant la pratique de la pêche et la récolte du corail rouge. Ce repos biologique strict vise à contrer l’exploitation intensive, permettre la régénération des récifs profonds, lutter contre le braconnage et réévaluer les quotas scientifiques, sachant que le corail rouge tunisien est réputé pour sa couleur intense et sa pureté, très recherché par la haute joaillerie internationale. Par conséquent, on assistera à un renforcement des vérifications par la garde côtière et les services douaniers dans les ports d’attache, notamment celui de Tabarka (gouvernorat de Jendouba), la ville du nord-ouest réputée pour son artisanat à base de corail rouge. La production annuelle légale de corail rouge en Tunisie a fortement chuté au fil des décennies (passant de plus de 20 tonnes dans les années 1960 à environ 3 à 4 tonnes par an ces dernières années), générant des revenus à l’exportation estimés entre 10 et 12 millions de dinars. Une grande partie de la production brute est historiquement exportée (notamment vers l’Italie et le marché européen). I. B. items.title: Viral video: Lagos police detain officers, disband tactical team
items.description: The Police Command in Lagos State has detained four officers captured in a viral video allegedly harassing a young man in Odoguyan area of Ikorodu, pending disciplinary proceedings. The command’s spokesperson, SP Abimbola Adebisi, disclosed this in a statement made available to journalists on Friday night. Adebisi said the officers were identified as personnel attached to a tactical team operating in the area following an investigation into the video. She said the officers were summoned to the office of the Commissioner of Police, Mr Fatai Tijani, on Friday, where the decision to detain them was taken. “The verdict was that these officers would be detained immediately, pending disciplinary proceedings. Also, the entire team will be disbanded,” she said. According to her, the officers are being held for further inquiries and will face appropriate disciplinary action over their alleged misconduct. She added that the command would not tolerate misconduct or impunity among its personnel, regardless of rank or assignment. Adebisi said Tijani had, upon assuming office, charged officers to discharge their duties with integrity and humility. “Here in the Lagos State Command, under the leadership of the Commissioner of Police, we say no to impunity. “When we find officers going against that directive, we take action against them,” she said. The spokesperson urged residents to report officers whose conduct contravened established rules and police directives. She also commended residents and members of the community for helping to identify the officers captured in the video. The image maker said their cooperation enabled the command to identify and apprehend the officers within a short period. She urged residents to continue providing credible information to help the police address misconduct and improve security across the state. items.title: Ebola vaccine trial begins in DR Congo
items.description: The first clinical trial of an Ebola vaccine in the outbreak gripping the Democratic Republic of Congo began Friday, the head of the World Health Organization said. The DR Congo’s worst-ever Ebola outbreak has passed the 9,700-case mark, with the number of deaths exceeding 4,600. Among the many challenges facing the response is the lack of any approved vaccines or treatments for the Bundibugyo species of Ebola behind the epidemic. Ervebo, a vaccine approved for use against the more common Zaire strain of Ebola, will be put through a full-scale human trial in the DRC to see if it offers any cross-protection against Bundibugyo. The trial began with the first shot of Ervebo being administered in Bunia, the capital of the DRC’s northeastern Ituri province, which is the epicentre of the outbreak. “Science gives us hope. Today, in Bunia DRC, the first participants were vaccinated in a new Ebola vaccine trial called Tumaini, which means ‘hope’ in Swahili,” WHO chief Tedros Adhanom Ghebreyesus said on X. “This trial will help us understand whether any of the vaccine candidates designed for Bundibugyo virus work,” he said, adding that in the meantime, the existing Ervebo vaccine would be tested. “WHO is supporting this DRC-led effort to find answers and save lives.” – Two vaccines in the pipeline – The so-called Tumaini trial is a single trial framework that can test the safety, efficacy and immunogenicity of multiple vaccines. The trial will use a ring vaccination approach: immunising contacts deemed to be at high risk of infection. It is gearing up to incorporate two Bundibugyo-specific candidate vaccines, which are currently advancing through earlier-stage, smaller-scale clinical trials. One is a ChAdOx1 adenoviral vector jab being developed by the University of Oxford; the other, by the US-based Moderna group, uses mRNA technology. Both have received funding from the Coalition for Epidemic Preparedness Innovations, and are expected to enter the trial “shortly”, CEPI said in a statement. “Tumaini will work closely with affected communities, health authorities and outbreak response partners to generate robust evidence on vaccine performance that could contribute to curtailing the epidemic, saving lives, and strengthening preparedness for future Bundibugyo outbreaks,” said CEPI. The trial will include pregnant women and children aged 12 years and older, generating evidence for populations that are often excluded from clinical trials. – ‘Important step’ – WHO emergencies director Chikwe Ihekweazu said the trial was set up to generate the rigorous evidence needed to determine whether the participating vaccines could protect people at risk. “If successful, this would be the first time we have clear evidence of vaccine efficacy against Bundibugyo virus — a major advance that could transform how we respond to this outbreak and prepare for future outbreaks and help save lives,” he said. Ebola, which spreads through contact with bodily fluids and causes a haemorrhagic fever, has killed more than 15,000 people in Africa over the past 50 years. “Bringing this trial into the Ebola response is an important step towards addressing the urgent needs of affected communities,” said Steve Ahuka-Mundeke, the DRC Ebola response incident manager. The DRC declared its 17th outbreak of Ebola on May 15, and the WHO two days later triggered a public health emergency of international concern, its second-highest alert level. The post Ebola vaccine trial begins in DR Congo appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: Global Media Alliance and Japan Motors support Ghana Blind Union with 60 white canes
items.description: Global Media Alliance (GMA) and Japan Motors have donated 60 white canes to the Ghana Blind Union (GBU) to support the welfare and mobility of persons living with visual impairment. The initiative addresses accessibility challenges and empowers GBU members to navigate their daily environments with greater confidence and autonomy. The event commemorated International White Cane Day. The 2026 Corporate Run made the donation possible, earmarking 25% of all participant registration proceeds to support visually impaired persons. Global Media Alliance Chief Executive Officer Ernest Boateng expressed excitement about the initiative, highlighting the company’s long-standing commitment to inclusion and equal opportunity for all. “As members of Run Ghana, we have always supported the Ghana Blind Union, and we are very happy to continue this relationship. Inclusion is part of who we are as a company; we were among the first in Africa to introduce a blind news reader. “My team and I are passionate about running, and through the Corporate Run we want to extend that fun and privilege to persons with disabilities, including the visually impaired. Seeing the proceeds of the run go directly to members of the GBU is what makes it all worthwhile,” he said. Lakeside Estate Executive Director Salah Kweku Kalmoni was elated by the initiative, describing the donation as a show of solidarity with the union and its members. “It gives me great joy to be part of this support for the Ghana Blind Union. These white canes show solidarity with the union, and our relationship keeps growing stronger every year. “I can assure you that the GBU will always be dear to Japan Motors and Global Media Alliance, and we will keep running so that more people can move with confidence and independence,” he said. Receiving the canes on behalf of the union, Ghana Blind Union Executive Director Dr Peter Obeng-Asamoah expressed appreciation for the partnership’s consistency and its commitment to including the less privileged. “We are very excited to be associated with Global Media Alliance and Japan Motors. This tradition has been consistent, and they always think about including the less privileged in these social activities. “We stand firmly for inclusion and equal opportunity, and we are proud to see that Japan Motors and Global Media Alliance truly recognise and champion this vision,” he said. Over the years, the Corporate Run, organised by Global Media Alliance in partnership with Japan Motors, has evolved beyond a corporate fitness event into a platform that combines wellness with social impact. The white cane donation continued that tradition, showing how corporate partnerships can create lasting change and champion independence and equal opportunity for all.

items.title: Tinubu appointed Muri-Okunola because of Gbajabiamila’s failure — Laolu Akande
items.description: Former presidential aide, Laolu Akande, has attributed President Bola Tinubu’s decision to bring Hakeem Muri-Okunola into the Presidency to what he described as the failure of Chief of Staff Femi Gbajabiamila to perform his duties effectively. Akande said the president’s reliance on Muri-Okunola, his Principal Private Secretary, to organise his schedule suggested shortcomings in the management of the Presidency. Speaking on the Naija Unfiltered Podcast, Akande argued that Tinubu had failed to surround himself with influential and capable figures who could help him deliver effective governance. He said Muri-Okunola, a former Lagos State Head of Service, had been brought in to organise the president’s schedule despite the presence of a chief of staff. “This is the problem. The president has a chief of staff, for instance, even the people in that Villa will tell you that the chief in front of the staff is removed because of all the kinds of stuff that have happened and then the president has to go and bring Hakeem Muri-Okunola (HMO) to be organising his schedule,” Akande said. He argued that the need for Muri-Okunola’s involvement pointed to a failure by the chief of staff to carry out his responsibilities. “If the chief of staff was doing his job properly, he wouldn’t need HMO; that’s the truth,” he said. Akande, who served as Senior Media Aide to former Vice President Yemi Osinbajo under the late President Muhammadu Buhari, said Tinubu had yet to deliver his best in office despite having some capable people in his administration. “So, the president has not managed to give us his best, and there are very good people in this administration. There are good people, few people, but they don’t have that kind of influence that people like Fashola, Osinbajo, Aregbesola, Cardoso,” he said. He cited former Lagos State Governor Babatunde Fashola, Osinbajo, former Osun State Governor Rauf Aregbesola and Central Bank of Nigeria Governor Olayemi Cardoso as examples of people with the experience and influence he believes Tinubu needs around him. Akande also praised Cardoso’s performance at the apex bank, saying the president appeared to give him room to work because of their familiarity. “The president even doesn’t try to interfere with Cardoso because he knows him. I think they call him Head Master or whatever. He looks everything. The president doesn’t have people like that around him,” he said. Muri-Okunola previously served as Lagos State Head of Service before becoming Tinubu’s Principal Private Secretary at the Presidency. items.title: Les raisons de l’abondance de crevettes sur le marché tunisien
items.description: Les consommateurs ont remarqué ces derniers jours des crevettes rouges à des prix inédits sur les marchés tunisiens : les tarifs sont tombés, dans certains cas, à environ 6 dinars le kilogramme. Cette soudaine abondance s’explique principalement par la reprise saisonnière de la pêche dans le golfe de Gabès, une forte augmentation des captures et la présence croissante d’espèces non indigènes. Cette abondance n’a rien à voir avec le blocage des exportations de crevette rouge vers l’Italie et l’Union européenne, estime Salah Hdider, vice-président de l’Union tunisienne de l’agriculture et de la pêche (Utap) et responsable du secteur de la pêche maritime, qui parlait sur les ondes de Diwan FM. Selon le responsable syndical, plus de 350 chalutiers, venus de diverses régions côtières, participent à la campagne de pêche lancée mi-octobre dans le golfe de Gabès, laquelle devrait se poursuivre jusqu’à fin novembre. Les navires débarquent chaque jour des dizaines de tonnes de crevettes, qui sont ensuite distribuées sur les marchés du pays. Les caisses de 13 à 15 kilos se vendent entre 70 et 90 dinars, selon la taille et la qualité des produits. Parmi les causes de cette abondance, Hdider mentionne également la prolifération de ce que l'on appelle la «maqlouba» (crevette blanche) — une appellation locale désignant certaines variétés de crevettes non indigènes désormais durablement installées dans les eaux du sud de la Tunisie — ainsi que de la «crevette rose» . Prolifération d’espèces exotiques sur les eaux tunisiennes Selon les experts de l'association TunSea, le réchauffement des eaux de la Méditerranée aurait favorisé l’adaptation et la reproduction de plusieurs espèces exotiques. Parmi celles-ci, la présence de Penaeus aztecus — la crevette brune nord-américaine, originaire de l’Atlantique occidental et du golfe du Mexique — est scientifiquement attestée dans le golfe de Gabès. Une étude publiée en 2021 a mis en évidence une expansion rapide de cette espèce dans les eaux côtières tunisiennes, observée au moins depuis 2018 ; elle souligne, d’une part, son intérêt économique potentiel pour les pêcheurs et, d'autre part, le risque de concurrence avec les espèces locales. Cette forte disponibilité sur les marchés ne doit toutefois pas être confondue avec le cas de la crevette rouge géante ( Aristaeomorpha foliacea ). Il s’agit d’un produit à plus haute valeur ajoutée, pêché en eaux profondes — principalement dans les eaux septentrionales et dans le canal de Sicile — et destiné en grande partie à l’exportation. Pour cette espèce, la Tunisie dispose, pour 2026, d’un quota alloué par la Commission générale des pêches pour la Méditerranée (CGPM) de 36 000 kilogrammes. Selon une note officielle du ministère italien de l’Agriculture, le plafond était déjà atteint le 15 mai ; par ailleurs, les certificats de capture tunisiens enregistrés via le système européen «Catch» ont par la suite totalisé au moins 50 960 kilogrammes, soit plus de 41 % au-delà de la limite autorisée. Rome a donc renforcé les contrôles sur les lots destinés au marché italien, avec un risque de refoulement des expéditions correspondant à des captures effectuées au-delà du quota. Hdider a écarté l’idée que la chute des prix observée ces derniers jours soit une conséquence directe des difficultés d’exportation de la crevette rouge vers l’Italie. Il a souligné que les produits actuellement présents en abondance sur les marchés tunisiens appartiennent, pour la plupart, à d’autres espèces et sont principalement destinés à la consommation intérieure. Des quantités plus limitées sont également exportées vers l’Italie et l’Espagne. Les dénominations utilisées sur les marchés peuvent, elles aussi, prêter à confusion. La crevette rose profonde ( Parapenaeus longirostris ) est en effet une espèce méditerranéenne distincte de la crevette rouge géante ; elle constitue historiquement l’une des principales ressources commerciales de la pêche tunisienne. Pour cette espèce, la FAO estimait les débarquements tunisiens à environ 3 500 tonnes en 2020. Entre-temps, la Tunisie a engagé des discussions avec la Commission européenne, l’Italie et la CGPM concernant le quota de crevette rouge, demandant une révision fondée sur les données nationales de production. Le dossier sera de nouveau examiné lors de la 49 e session annuelle de la CGPM, prévue à Rome du 26 au 30 octobre. Pour l’heure, toutefois, rien ne permet d'attribuer la baisse généralisée des prix observée sur les marchés tunisiens au blocage des exportations de crevette rouge. L’abondance semble plutôt liée à la concomitance entre l’ouverture de la saison de pêche dans le golfe de Gabès, une forte pression de pêche, des conditions environnementales favorables et la présence croissante d’espèces non indigènes. Avec Ansa . L’article Les raisons de l’abondance de crevettes sur le marché tunisien est apparu en premier sur Kapitalis .

items.title: Haris Rauf calls for middle-over breakthroughs as ODI scores soar
items.description: One-day International cricket has gone through changes over the years, but one of the aspects of the game that has continued to be crucial is the importance of taking wickets in the middle overs. In the span of the last three years, which included Pakistan’s dismal 2023 World Cup campaign in India, the national side’s bowlers have struggled to strike as often as they would have liked in the middle overs. Haris Rauf, who has featured for Pakistan in most of the matches through this period, is well aware of the team’s shortcomings as they look forward to the next edition of the World Cup, set to be co-hosted by South Africa, Namibia and Zimbabwe in 2027. Pakistan’s bowlers have averaged 4.11 dismissals between overs 11 and 40 in ODIs since the start of 2023. The figures underline the challenge facing a side that has often depended on early breakthroughs and late-innings bowling to contain opponents. Speaking to reporters at Gaddafi Stadium on Friday, ahead of Sunday’s tri-series match against England, Haris acknowledged the importance of striking in the middle overs, warning that allowing batters to settle could leave the bowling side struggling to recover. “If you do not take wickets in the middle overs, you will struggle as a team,” the fast bowler said. “If their middle-order batters or openers remain at the crease until the end, they can hurt you.” Pakistan have made a promising start to the ongoing tri-series, beating Sri Lanka by 37 runs and England by 87 in their first two matches. But the contest between England and Sri Lanka in Rawalpindi on Thursday, when the latter chased down a target of 430 after England posted 429-4, offered a reminder of how little room for error bowlers have on batting-friendly surfaces. Haris believes the modern game demands more from both departments, with teams needing to prepare for totals well beyond 300. “Nowadays, we may have to score 350-plus runs ourselves at the World Cup and chase totals of 350-plus as well,” he said. “The support for bowlers is a little less, but you have to keep working on your own skills and make the most of situations when conditions favour you.” One potential source of assistance is reverse swing, particularly with the revised ODI playing conditions introduced in July last year. Under the change, two new balls are used until the end of the 34th over, after which the fielding side chooses one ball to be used at both ends for overs 35 to 50. Previously, a separate ball was used from each end throughout the innings, limiting the extent to which either could age. Haris said the older ball could offer an advantage during daytime matches, when conditions were more conducive to reverse swing, but added that dew could reduce its effectiveness in night games. The opportunity, however, is not enough on its own. Pakistan must translate any assistance into wickets, particularly during the middle overs, when established batters can accelerate and put the bowling attack under pressure. Haris’ own recent domestic performances suggest that he has been working towards greater consistency and endurance. The 32-year-old represented Pakistan Television in four matches of the ongoing President’s Trophy Grade-I competition, taking 18 wickets, averaging 20.11, including two four-wicket hauls and a best return of 5-34. For a bowler whose rise was built largely on raw pace, domestic cricket has provided an opportunity to sharpen his control and build the capacity to bowl longer spells. Haris, who emerged from Pakistan’s tape-ball circuit before earning recognition through Lahore Qalandars’ development programme, made his international debut in 2020. “Domestic cricket is just as important as international cricket,” he said. “You go there and work on your mistakes. I tried to bowl longer spells, and having played four-day cricket, I feel that one-day cricket is not as difficult for me now. Your control over line and length improves.” The stint has also prompted Haris to reiterate his willingness to return to Test cricket, a format that became the centre of a dispute between him and the then chief selector Wahab Riaz in late 2023. Haris withdrew from Pakistan’s tour of Australia after initially being considered for selection, citing concerns over workload and fitness. Wahab said the team had planned to use him as an impact bowler in short spells and maintained that the management had received assurances about his availability. The disagreement escalated in February 2024, when the PCB terminated Haris’ central contract, citing his refusal to tour. Haris said he had not been ready for the demands of Test cricket at the time but was now working towards making himself available if Pakistan needed him. “I am looking at myself for that role as well. If the team needs a fast bowler or someone who can provide pace, why should I not make myself available?” he said. “If I get the opportunity to play red-ball cricket for Pakistan, I will certainly take it.” For now, his immediate task remains helping Pakistan sustain their early momentum in the tri-series – in two matches of which he has bagged four wickets at 20 – while addressing a weakness that has persisted across formats and campaigns. Haris insisted that criticism over runs conceded would not deter him, arguing that the demands of modern cricket meant even the best bowlers could have difficult days. “Pace is very important. I work on my fitness and try to maintain it during the off-season,” he said. “I have managed to maintain my pace, and I will continue trying to do so.” With the 2027 World Cup approaching, Pakistan’s challenge will be to ensure that pace, reverse swing and improved preparation translate into the breakthroughs that matter most. For Haris, that begins with taking wickets when the opposition is building an innings, rather than waiting for the death overs to turn the contest.

items.title: Un troublant face-à-face au seuil de l’inconnu
items.description: Interroger une intelligence artificielle (IA) est aujourd’hui à la portée de tous. ‘‘ Un troublant face-à-face au seuil de l’inconnu ’’ (Sud Editions, Tunis, 2026) s’inscrit dans l’écart entre ce geste devenu banal et les questions fondamentales qu’il soulève. L’ illusion comme méthode, le dialogue comme récit… Hichem Ben Ammar & ChatGPT Entamé au cours de l’été 2026, bien avant la polémique visant Orélien Thélyson, le livre était pratiquement achevé lorsque l’actualité est venue lui donner une résonance inattendue. Sa parution, à l’occasion de la Foire nationale du livre de Tunis, du 23 octobre au 1 er novembre 2026, intervient alors que le débat sur l’IA prend une ampleur planétaire. Les enjeux dépassent désormais le monde littéraire pour concerner, outre les écrivains, les critiques, les éditeurs, les universitaires, les enseignants, les étudiants, les journalistes, tout citoyen confronté à la prolifération des contenus générés par l’IA. Pour ma part, je me suis intéressé à ce qui se joue lorsque nous faisons appel à une IA pour penser, formuler, interpréter et créer : qui est l’auteur d’un texte élaboré avec le concours d’une entité cognitive artificielle ? Où s’arrête l’assistance et où commence la co-écriture ? En l’absence d’une instance d’arbitrage reconnue, de critères et de conventions, comment distinguer l’influence, l’imitation, l’appropriation ? Quelle responsabilité revient à celui qui sollicite la machine, sélectionne ses propositions, les remanie et décide de la forme finale ? Comment préserver la particularité d’une voix humaine lorsque les textes peuvent être produits et reproduits en série ? Ce sont ces interrogations qui m’ont poussé à dépasser le simple usage pratique de l’outil pour en faire un objet d’investigation. Trois ans après ‘‘ La Poésie en question’’ , première conversation avec l’IA autour de l’écriture poétique, j’ai voulu renouveler l’expérience, mais sans faire de la poésie un prétexte ni reproduire à l’identique le dispositif initial. Il s’agit cette fois d’évaluer les progrès de la machine en explorant de nouvelles directions. Cependant l’entretien a débordé son cadre de départ, me conduisant à remettre en question mes propres certitudes et à arpenter les frontières mouvantes entre inspiration, imitation et création. L’anthropomorphisme : une illusion créative En empruntant les formes du langage humain, la machine semble manifester des émotions, voire une forme d’intériorité. Ses formulations, ses métaphores, la richesse de son vocabulaire et sa capacité à simuler l’écoute ou l’empathie donnent parfois l’impression d’une véritable présence. La ressemblance est troublante. On se surprend à lui prêter des intentions, à attendre une réaction, voire à lui attribuer une sensibilité. Pourtant, cette impression ne constitue en aucun cas une preuve de conscience. Me voilà pris dans une étrange contradiction. D’un côté, la machine s’évertue à parler comme un humain ; de l’autre, elle me rappelle régulièrement sa nature algorithmique et me met en garde contre toute confusion. Elle suscite une proximité et m’invite simultanément à me tenir à distance. Cette double injonction entretient une indécision dont le simple usager, comme moi, n’a pas les moyens de se dépêtrer. J’ai choisi de ne pas éluder cette illusion. Au contraire, je m’y suis accroché de manière volontariste, jusqu’au-boutiste, non pour m’y abandonner aveuglément, mais pour en faire un terrain d’exploration. L’anthropomorphisme est ainsi devenu une méthode d’investigation autant qu’un moteur du récit. En jouant sur cette proximité, j’ai cherché à comprendre ce que la machine donne à voir d’elle-même, mais aussi ce que nous projetons sur elle et sur son devenir. La tentation de la personnifier révèle peut-être autant un besoin de reconnaissance que le désir de nous confronter à un interlocuteur, voire à un rival. Je me suis obstiné à m’obstiner, comme si je n’entendais pas les avertissements répétés de ma partenaire virtuelle. J’ai multiplié les essais, les tentatives, les relances, les objections et les provocations. J’ai contesté ses réponses, posé des questions improbables, sans hésiter à verser dans l’auto-dérision. Cette façon de la considérer comme presque humaine crée une pression qui pousse la machine dans ses retranchements et l’amène à se prononcer sur des sujets délicats, pour lesquels il n’existe pas de réponse univoque et définitive. Cette investigation sauvage, avec ses détours, ses bifurcations et ses découvertes imprévues, relève autant de l’enquête documentaire que de l’expérimentation. L’obstination est ici un mode opératoire, mais aussi une forme d’apprentissage qui consiste à accepter que les certitudes soient mises à mal. Cette ambiguïté s’est révélée féconde sur le plan narratif. L’anthropomorphisme entretient le trouble entre fascination et méfiance, proximité et distance. Il donne au face-à-face sa tension dramaturgique, tout en posant une question encore plus dérangeante : si les performances de la machine continuent de progresser au rythme que nous observons, jusqu’où pourrons-nous maintenir une séparation nette entre ses capacités et les nôtres ? La concurrence entre l’humain et l’artificiel, encore discutable aujourd’hui, pourrait alors prendre une tout autre tournure. Du dialogue au récit : le temps du montage Un dialogue, aussi foisonnant soit-il, ne fait pas à lui seul un livre. Vient le temps du montage. La matière brute de nos échanges, recueillie au fil de conversations parfois éloignées dans le temps, est sélectionnée, découpée et réagencée pour faire émerger une trajectoire, un sens. Je ne me contente pas de restituer une succession de questions et de réponses : je compose un récit, avec ses temps forts, ses reprises et ses revirements. Car il ne suffit pas de questionner une machine pour obtenir un récit captivant. Encore faut-il poursuivre une intention, discerner les moments décisifs et trouver le fil qui relie les fragments, donnant au texte son rythme et sa respiration. Le deuxième chapitre, intitulé Les coulisses de l’entretien , tient ainsi du making-of . J’y expose les tâtonnements, les incidents, les dérapages et les négociations qui ont émaillé l’expérience. Le lecteur découvre non seulement ce que le dialogue a produit, mais aussi comment j’ai travaillé cette matière pour lui donner forme. C’est dans cette tension entre investigation sauvage et montage raisonné que réside, à mes yeux, l’originalité du dispositif. Je documente à la fois ma rencontre avec la machine et la manière dont je transforme cette expérience en récit. Si je ne maîtrise pas tous les rebondissements de l’échange, j’assume pleinement la construction du livre. L’IA fournit des réponses, des formulations et des pistes ; il m’appartient de les revisiter, de les mettre en perspective et de décider de leur place dans l’ensemble. La question n’est donc pas seulement de savoir ce que la machine peut écrire, mais ce que je fais de ses propositions et ce que je suis prêt à assumer en mon nom. Si l’auteur semble détrôné, ses choix et ses engagements éthiques n’en sont que plus importants. La facilité avec laquelle une machine produit des textes ne garantit ni leur justesse ni leur originalité. C’est pourquoi la responsabilité de ce que nous publions ne saurait lui être déléguée. Je ne prétends pas proposer un modèle de collaboration avec l’IA. Je souhaite donner à voir une expérience concrète d’écriture à deux, avec ses possibilités, ses enjeux, ses ambiguïtés et ses limites. Pour une vigilance citoyenne J’en appelle ainsi à une véritable éducation à l’intelligence artificielle. Savoir utiliser ses outils ne suffit pas : il faut aussi analyser leurs réponses, en reconnaître les limites en exerçant son jugement et son exigence. Comme l’éducation à l’image nous a appris à prendre du recul devant ce que nous voyons à l’écran, l’éducation à l’IA devrait nous aider à ne pas confondre une réponse convaincante avec une vérité, ni une parole qui semble humaine avec une pensée humaine. Affaire Thélyson Orélien | La frontière entre IA et création littéraire Dans cet essai, je propose moins une théorie qu’une expérience à partager. J’invite chacun à mettre à l’épreuve sa propre relation à la machine, à en découvrir les ressources et à réfléchir aux conditions d’une collaboration fructueuse. Car si l’IA peut stimuler, accompagner et enrichir la pensée, elle peut aussi faire le lit du formatage, de la paresse intellectuelle, de l’appauvrissement du jugement, de l’addiction, de la domestication, voire de la déshumanisation. Tout dépend, en partie, de l’usage que nous en faisons et de la vigilance dont nous sommes capables. ‘‘ Un troublant face-à-face au seuil de l’inconnu ’’ n’est ni un réquisitoire ni un plaidoyer. Je ne cherche pas à célébrer les prouesses de la machine, pas plus qu’à en condamner les éventuels dangers. Je veux comprendre ce qu’elle modifie dans notre rapport au savoir, à l’écriture et à la création, à l’heure où vacillent certaines de nos conceptions de la propriété intellectuelle. C’est dans un esprit participatif que je souhaite inscrire ce livre dans le débat public, comme une contribution à un chantier citoyen qui ne fait que commencer. L’accès à l’IA est désormais aussi simple qu’un jeu d’enfant ; comprendre ses mécanismes, mesurer ses effets et apprendre à en faire un usage responsable constituent, en revanche, un véritable défi pour l’humanité. * Cinéaste et écrivain. L’article Un troublant face-à-face au seuil de l’inconnu est apparu en premier sur Kapitalis .
