items.title: The next president Ghana needs after this sham reset
items.description: We have been here before. Big slogans. Big promises. A government comes in shouting “Reset.” But what has been reset? Not the price of kenkey. Not the cedi. Not the attitude of those in power. Only loyalists’ bank accounts have been reset. The evacuation of 1,964 Ghanaians from South Africa exposed it all. GH¢49.72 million spent. GH¢5,000 given to a man who lost a shop he built for 10 years. A Foreign Minister telling American citizens, “We will forgive them.” Forgive them for what? For losing everything? That is not a reset. That is a sham. It is old wine, arrogant wine, in a new bottle. So Ghana’s next conversation cannot be about NDC vs NPP. It cannot be about who shouts loudest on the radio. The next election must be about CHARACTER. The next President to get it right for us must have three things this current lot does not have: 1. Good Character Over Good English We don’t need a President who can speak big grammar at the UN while insulting citizens at home. We need someone with good character. A person who understands that public office is not a chiefdom. A Ghanaian who lost his livelihood in South Africa is not a beggar to be forgiven, but a citizen to be restored. Good character means you tell us the truth the first time, not after the Minority exposes you. Good character means you don’t hide that a private businessman paid GH¢16 million for a state evacuation. Good character means you don’t call GH¢5,000 an achievement. 2. Courage to Choose Merit Over Loyalty The reason Ghana is not developing is not a lack of ideas. It is loyalty over merit. Both NPP and NDC do it. When in opposition, they cry about protocol. When in power, they break protocol even worse. They sack a competent director because he was appointed by the other party and replace him with a loyal youth organiser who cannot manage a district budget. The next President must be prepared to do what it takes: Keep the competent Ghanaian even if he wears the other party’s colours. Sack the incompetent loyalist even if he followed you in opposition for 8 years. If your child needs heart surgery, you will not choose the most loyal surgeon. You will choose the most competent one. Why then do we give the heart of Ghana to loyalists? 3. A Unifier, Not a Divider The reset we have seen is divisive. It is “us versus them.” If you complain about GH¢5,000, you are ungrateful. If you ask for an audit, you are unpatriotic. A country cannot develop when half the country is treated as enemies. The next President must bring us together as Ghanaians. Ewe, Akan, Dagomba, Ga, Frafra, we all suffer the same economic conditions. The next President must be a President for the returnee from South Africa, the nurse who wants to travel to Canada, the trader at Makola, and the farmer at Ejura. We are tired of leaders who forgive us. We want leaders who serve us. The sham reset will end, as all sham projects end. When it ends, Ghana will need more than a politician. Ghana needs a person of good character, prepared to do what it takes to get it right. Not for his party. For all of us.

items.title: Iran says US military not allowed to enter Gulf ‘under any circumstances’
items.description: Iran said on Saturday that US military ships would never be allowed to enter the Gulf “under any circumstances” and President Donald Trump will “take that dream to his grave”. The remarks came amid mounting US and Israeli threats of renewed attacks on Iran, as US ambassador to Turkey Tom Barrack warned that Washington could “absolutely” strike Iran as soon as this weekened. “We will not allow US military ships in the Persian Gulf under any circumstances and at any time,” said Iran’s armed forces chief of staff Ali Abdollahi, according to Iranian state television. “The US president must dream of seeing the armed forces enter the Persian Gulf. He will take that dream to his grave.” Iranian forces have restricted traffic through the Strait of Hormuz, a vital energy conduit and gateway to the Gulf, since the war with the United States broke out on February 28. In retaliation, the United States has imposed a counterblockade on Iranian ports and ships. Tehran has required vessels to seek permission to transit, and repeatedly targeted ships attempting to pass through Hormuz via a southern route close to the Omani coast. According to the Guards, several tankers attempting to transit Hormuz through the route Tehran considers “illegal” were hit by mines in recent days. On Friday, the Guards said two supertankers carrying more than 4.5 million barrels of crude oil have been abandoned at sea after hitting mines in the strategic waterway. “Their engine rooms were disabled by an explosion and a fierce fire,” the Guards said in a statement carried by their Sepah News website. In peacetime, around a fifth of the world’s oil and gas passed through Hormuz. AFP The post Iran says US military not allowed to enter Gulf ‘under any circumstances’ appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: Why some people in Tinubu’s govt don’t want Fashola around – Laolu Akande
items.description: Former presidential aide, Laolu Akande, has alleged that some people around President Bola Tinubu do not want former Minister of Works and Housing, Babatunde Fashola, in the current administration because he would not tolerate certain practices within the government. Akande said Fashola’s absence from the government could partly be due to fatigue but argued that the opposition of some people around Tinubu was a more significant factor. He spoke during an interview on the Naija Unfiltered Podcast, where he also discussed Tinubu’s government and the perceived fallout between the president and former Vice President Yemi Osinbajo. Akande, who served as Senior Media Aide to Osinbajo under former President Muhammadu Buhari, described Fashola as someone who would not compromise his principles to accommodate those around him. “I think the reason why Fashola is not in this government, two reasons. I think Fashola himself has a bit of fatigue, more importantly, I think there are people around the president who don’t want to see Fashola because Fashola is not going to tolerate many of those things that you are seeing around,” he said. Akande added that Fashola was known for standing his ground, suggesting that his disposition might have made some people in the president’s circle uncomfortable. “Whatever you say about Fashola, he doesn’t take nonsense and the people who wanted to get some nonsense going, they didn’t want Fashola,” he said. The former presidential aide, however, said Fashola remained close to Tinubu and had not had a major public disagreement with the president. He suggested that, despite the absence of an open confrontation, there could be underlying tensions between the two politicians. “Even somebody like Fashola, who is still very close to the president — no problems openly, although they are also under current which he will speak about, but at least he didn’t have any blowout problem with the man,” Akande said. He maintained that some people around Tinubu did not want individuals like Fashola in the administration for reasons beyond the former minister’s own reluctance to return to government. Fashola served as governor of Lagos State from 2007 to 2015 before joining Buhari’s cabinet, where he was first appointed Minister of Power, Works and Housing and later served as Minister of Works and Housing. He has not held a position in Tinubu’s administration. The post Why some people in Tinubu’s govt don’t want Fashola around – Laolu Akande appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: Lagouira, monnaie d’échange d’un marchandage entre Nouakchott et Rabat
items.description: Dans les milieux diplomatiques, on dit volontiers « insondable comme un Mauritanien ». La formule résume la capacité de Nouakchott de préserver ses marges de manœuvre, d'entretenir l'ambiguïté et de négocier sur plusieurs fronts sans jamais dévoiler ses intentions. Le dossier de Lagouira en offre aujourd'hui une parfaite illustration. Les démentis officiels restent timides et en demi-teinte et aucune revendication territoriale n'est formulée. Pourtant, des chercheurs, des journalistes et des analystes mauritaniens rouvrent la question du statut de cette zone stratégique. S'appuyant sur les accords de Madrid du 14 novembre 1975 et sur les arrangements conclus ensuite avec le Maroc, ils soutiennent que tout accord devra préserver absolument les intérêts mauritaniens à Lagouira, bien que Nouakchott ait officiellement renoncé en 1979 à ses prétentions territoriales sur le Sahara occidental. Ces prises de position confortent l'hypothèse que j'avançais dans mon article du 11 octobre sur TSA, « La Mauritanie, Lagouira et le Sahara occidental : marchandage en vue ? ». J'envisageais que la Mauritanie cherche une concession de longue durée, ou un statut particulier, pour protéger ses intérêts économiques et sécuritaires à Lagouira, en échange d'un infléchissement de sa position sur la question du Sahara occidental. Pourquoi Lagouira est importante pour la Mauritanie L'enjeu est d'abord économique et sécuritaire. À l'extrémité Sud de la péninsule du cap Blanc, face à Nouadhibou, Lagouira commande l'avenir du principal pôle portuaire mauritanien. Le port, la pêche et les infrastructures d'exportation du minerai de fer forment des piliers de l'économie nationale. C'est ce qui fait de Lagouira la pièce maîtresse d'un marchandage. Un arrangement global porterait sur des garanties économiques, un statut particulier pour Lagouira et un deal diplomatique avec Rabat. Nouakchott reconnaîtrait la souveraineté marocaine sur le Sahara occidental et retirerait sa reconnaissance de la RASD, ce qui marquerait un tournant majeur de sa politique. Rabat y gagnerait un appui diplomatique de poids, et Nouakchott des avantages concrets et garantis. Ces avantages pourraient prendre plusieurs formes sans transfert de souveraineté : une concession de longue durée, une zone industrielle commune ou une zone franche à statut spécial. Nouakchott obtiendrait ainsi un rôle dans le développement de Lagouira, avec des garanties sur les infrastructures portuaires, la pêche, le minerai de fer et la sécurité frontalière. L'enjeu dépasse d'ailleurs Lagouira. La Mauritanie est un passage obligé pour les échanges du Maroc avec l'Afrique de l'Ouest et pour ses projets régionaux stratégiques, notamment l'initiative atlantique et le gazoduc Nigeria-Maroc. La Mauritanie, verrou stratégique pour l’influence marocaine en Afrique de l’Ouest Nouakchott ne manquera pas de tirer parti de cette position de verrou stratégique pour la monnayer contre des avantages économiques et politiques durables. Rabat serait alors contraint de s’y plier, de bonne ou de mauvaise grâce, sous peine de se retrouver confronté à un scénario catastrophe : celui de l’insularité stratégique avec un accès à l’Afrique de l’Ouest considérablement compromis. Reste qu'un accord bilatéral ne règle pas la question du Sahara occidental et ne remplace pas le droit du peuple sahraoui à l'autodétermination. Si Lagouira devient la monnaie d'échange du marchandage entre Rabat et Nouakchott, une question politique et morale demeure : Deux États peuvent-ils négocier l’avenir d’un territoire non autonome et le sort de son peuple au mépris des principes fondamentaux du droit international et de son droit à l’autodétermination ? L’article Lagouira, monnaie d'échange d'un marchandage entre Nouakchott et Rabat est apparu en premier sur TSA .

items.title: Annoh-Dompreh earns double honours for environmental advocacy
items.description: Minority Chief Whip and Nsawam-Adoagyiri MP, Frank Annoh-Dompreh, has received two awards for his advocacy on environmental sustainability and efforts to advance green legislation. He received the Green Societal Impact and Sustainability Ambassadorial Award and the ICESDA Green Capital Partnership Award at the third International Conference on ESG and Sustainable Development of Africa (ICESDA). The conference was held under the theme, “The Africa We Want: Driving Transformational Inclusive Green Growth Through ESG and Digitalisation.” Presenters recognised the MP’s efforts to bring community-level environmental concerns to Parliament and support legislative action on sustainability. They highlighted his advocacy at times when such issues attracted limited political attention. The Green Societal Impact and Sustainability Ambassadorial Award acknowledged his contribution to promoting environmental concerns through Parliament. He also received the ICESDA Green Capital Partnership Award at the ceremony. The recognition highlighted lawmakers’ role in connecting environmental challenges in their constituencies to national policymaking. Presenters also stressed the importance of considering environmental evidence when debating and passing legislation. The conference brought together stakeholders to examine how environmental, social and governance (ESG) principles, alongside digital technologies, could support Africa’s development. Discussions focused on inclusive green growth and the need for collaboration among policymakers, businesses and civil society organisations to balance economic development with environmental protection.

items.title: Kaylia Nemour au pied du podium à Rotterdam : « Garde la tête haute, notre championne »
items.description: Première déception pour Kaylia Nemour aux Mondiaux de gymnastique de Rotterdam. Après avoir dominé avec brio les qualifications, la championne olympique algérienne aux JO de Paris 2024 a terminé au pied du podium vendredi soir à Rotterdam. La jeune gymnaste de 19 ans a terminé à la 4ᵉ place avec 54,998 points, derrière l’Américaine Skye Blakely, qui a survolé la finale avec une note de 57,733, la Russe Liudmila Roshchina avec 55,199 points et la Chinoise Ke Qinqin avec 55,032 points. Le DTN de la Fédération de gym à Kaylia Nemour : « Garde la tête haute, notre championne » Kaylia Nemour a été pénalisée par sa prestation sur le cheval où elle a obtenu 12,366 points seulement et une 21ᵉ place. Sa remontée au classement n’a pas été suffisante pour faire mieux qu’à Jakarta en 2025, où elle avait terminé également à la 4ᵉ place au concours général. La championne algérienne peut se rattraper dès ce samedi en décrochant l’or sur les barres asymétriques, un agrès où elle écrase la concurrence depuis les JO de Paris 2024. Pour cela, elle a tout un pays derrière elle. Le directeur technique national de la Fédération algérienne de gymnastique, Rabah Mekachi, lui a adressé un message fort de soutien à Kaylia Nemour après la finale du concours général. « Garde la tête haute, notre championne. Tu as déjà tant donné à l’Algérie et tu as encore de très belles choses à nous faire vivre. Chaque nouvelle épreuve est une occasion de briller davantage. Alors, continue d’avancer avec confiance, sérénité et cette belle détermination qui te caractérise », a-t-il écrit. items.title: MOMO FinTech Lab backs young innovators in northern Ghana
items.description: Young innovators in northern Ghana are getting an opportunity to turn ideas into technology-driven solutions to local challenges, as MOMO FinTech steps up efforts to nurture talent beyond Accra and develop the next generation of financial technology entrepreneurs. Four top-performing teams from the northern zone have secured places at the National Demo Day in Accra, where they will be paired with mentors to refine their projects before presenting them to investors and other stakeholders. The initiative, known as the MOMO FinTech Lab, seeks to identify promising young innovators, equip them with practical skills and support them to develop solutions that can improve livelihoods in their communities. Speaking to the media after the hackathon in Tamale, the Chief Executive Officer of MOMO FinTech, Shaibu Haruna, said the initiative was introduced after the company observed that FinTech businesses were largely concentrated in Accra, despite the availability of talented young people across the country. He said the company wanted to create opportunities for young people to develop ideas that addressed local needs and had the potential to compete on the national and international stages. “We took it upon ourselves to say there are so many talented young men and women across the length and breadth of Ghana who have great ideas and who can be groomed to solve for their local needs,” he said. Mr Haruna disclosed that the competition had attracted more than 1,000 entries nationwide, with submissions from northern Ghana accounting for 14 per cent of the total. Participants in the northern zone spent four days working with experts to refine their ideas through practical testing, market research and technical guidance. He said the company was impressed by the effort participants had put into developing solutions aimed at tackling everyday problems and improving the livelihoods of ordinary people. The programme is also expected to open up opportunities for partnerships and investment to help promising innovators turn their ideas into practical, market-ready solutions. Mr Haruna added that selected participants would have opportunities to undertake internships with organisations to deepen their technical knowledge and gain practical work experience. He encouraged young people, particularly those in northern Ghana, to believe in their ideas, develop them carefully and take advantage of available opportunities to advance their innovations. “I encourage all young people who have ideas across the length and breadth of Ghana, especially in the northern sector of Ghana, to be bold about their ideas, to think through them, and then take advantage of some of these opportunities,” he said. Mr Haruna described the programme as a talent-development initiative that would require sustained support to help participants improve their ideas and build viable solutions. Contestants look ahead Meanwhile, members of the four selected teams said their qualification for the national showcase was an important milestone after days of competition and project development. The Team Lead of Team MoMoCovert, Lukman Seidu, said the competition had been demanding but expressed excitement about the team’s success. “It’s been a tough competition but we are excited that we have been able to make it out which means a lot to us,” he said.

items.title: Trump’s threat to strike Iran raises public concerns, congressional questions
items.description: WASHINGTON: President Donald Trump has renewed his threat of military action against Iran, raising questions about public support for the war and Congress’s ability to restrain further escalation . With midterm elections approaching on November 3, polls show widespread dissatisfaction with the war , particularly over rising fuel prices and the risk to American troops. Reports of renewed US-Israeli military planning have also raised concerns about possible strikes after the elections. Trump made his latest threat at a rally in Florida on Friday. “We may do another little Epic Fury ,” he said, referring to the US military operation against Iran. He gave no details about when another operation might begin. The remarks followed an ABC News report on Thursday that the US military and the Israel Defence Forces had drawn up options for renewed joint strikes. The report cited two Israeli sources familiar with the plans, who said the strikes would most likely take place after the midterms. White House spokesperson Anna Kelly, however, told ABC News that “the United States will not be attacking Iran at any time prior to the midterm elections.” The reports indicate that further military action is being considered, but they do not establish that Trump has ordered an attack. Negotiations remain another possibility. Strategic choices and political pressure In an analysis published on October 23, James M. Lindsay, a senior fellow at the Council on Foreign Relations, outlined three options for Trump: escalate the conflict, negotiate with Tehran or maintain the current position. “All three options have substantial downsides and a questionable likelihood of succeeding,” Lindsay wrote. Further attacks could increase pressure on Iran but might prolong the conflict without securing a political settlement. Negotiations would require the two sides to bridge their differences, while maintaining the current position could leave the conflict unresolved. Andrew Payne, research director for Europe, Russia and the Americas at Chatham House, argued in an October 15 analysis that foreign policy could play an unusual role in this year’s midterm elections. The war’s economic consequences could influence voters who might otherwise focus primarily on domestic issues, particularly the cost of living. Public opinion turns against the war A Pew Research Centre survey conducted from September 28 to October 4 among 5,062 US adults found that 65 per cent disapproved of Trump’s handling of the military action against Iran, while 33pc approved. The survey also found that 73pc were extremely or very concerned about higher fuel prices, and 71pc about American troops being wounded or killed. Nearly half, 47pc, expected the military action to continue for more than another year. A separate Associated Press -NORC poll published on October 22 found that roughly seven in 10 registered voters wanted the next Congress to make ending the Iran war a top priority. About eight in 10 gave similar priority to reducing the cost of living. The poll surveyed 1,119 US adults from October 8 to 12. The findings point to pressure on the administration to address the war’s duration and economic consequences. However, dissatisfaction with Trump’s handling of the conflict does not necessarily mean that voters would oppose every possible military operation. Can Congress restrain Trump? Congress can scrutinise military operations, hold oversight hearings and use its control over federal spending to influence the course of the war. Lawmakers can also invoke the War Powers Resolution to challenge military action. The resolution requires the president to notify Congress in certain circumstances when US forces enter hostilities. It also establishes procedures for lawmakers to consider whether military action should continue. Funding could become particularly important if the conflict expands. Congress can approve, restrict or condition spending for military operations, potentially increasing the political cost of a prolonged campaign. The extent of congressional pressure would depend partly on whether Republicans remain united behind Trump. If some Republican lawmakers join Democrats in challenging the war, the administration could face greater scrutiny of its objectives and plans for ending the conflict. Even a congressional challenge, however, would not automatically prevent the president from ordering another strike. The question after November 3 The immediate question is whether Trump will maintain his stated position against attacking Iran before the midterms. The larger issue is whether the election results will alter the political constraints on his decisions. The reported military planning and Trump’s latest remarks keep the prospect of renewed strikes alive, but neither establishes that an attack has been scheduled. A change in control of either chamber of Congress could affect oversight and funding debates, although it would not automatically prevent further military action. Whether the combined pressures of public dissatisfaction, economic concerns and congressional scrutiny lead Trump towards negotiations or renewed strikes remains unclear.

items.title: Pakistan denounces ‘heinous’ church attack in Jordan, reiterates condemnation of terrorism
items.description: Pakistan has strongly condemned the “heinous terrorist attack” on a funeral procession at a church in Jordan’s Karak Governorate, reiterating its condemnation of terrorism in all its forms and manifestations. Gunmen killed at least seven people and wounded dozens at a church in southern Jordan on Friday. According to reports, the assailants stormed the compound of a Greek Orthodox church in the village of Hammoud in Karak Governorate and opened fire. According to a statement issued by the Foreign Office (FO), Pakistan extended its heartfelt condolences to the government and people of the Hashemite Kingdom of Jordan, particularly the bereaved families, and expressed its wishes for the speedy recovery of those injured. “Pakistan stands in firm solidarity with the brotherly people of Jordan in their fight against terrorism, and reiterates its strongest condemnation of terrorism in all its forms and manifestations”, the statement added. The incident occurred when gunmen got out of a vehicle and opened fire during a funeral procession, Jordan’s Public Security Directorate said in a statement, adding that a manhunt was under way for the perpetrators. “The terrorist attack against Karak will be met with the harshest retaliation,” King Abdullah II said in a post on X. “We will strike with an iron fist against those who dare to threaten our nation.” According to images from state broadcaster Al-Mamlaka , the king arrived in Karak on Friday evening. After authorities gave a death toll of six, Director of Public Security Major General Abdullah Al-Maaytah said it had risen to seven with 34 injured, 27 of whom were still receiving treatment. Footage aired by Al-Mamlaka showed two gunmen dressed in casual clothes and brandishing pistols, with a third carrying a long gun as they opened fire on the church. A witness said the gunmen fired continuously for five minutes before fleeing. Between 150 and 200 people were in and around the church at the time, the witness said.

items.title: Fela lives on in Kwara as state celebrates his life, legacies
items.description: By Ben Njoku Memories of Afrobeat pioneer and activist, Fela Anikulapo-Kuti, will be relived in Ilorin, Kwara State, from Monday, October 26, 2026,as an art exhibition celebrating his life and legacy opens to the public in a grand style. The event, titled “Fela— A Retrospective,” is organized in alignment with the vision of the Kwara State Governor to promote the local creative economy and cultural heritage. Holding at the Institute of Contemporary African Art and Film,ICAAF, Ilorin, the exhibition , which will be curated and produced by June Creative Art Advisory, JCAA, runs until December 31, 2026, with free admission for members of the public. According to a statement issued in Ilorin by the state’s Commissioner for Communications, Hon. Bolanle Olukoju (@BolanleOlukoju), the exhibition will feature photographs, archival materials, music, film and historical objects documenting Fela’s contributions to Afrobeat, art and social thought. It will also highlight his historic performance at the Niger Hotel, Ilorin, on August 30, 1971. The initiative will feature guided tours, school visits and workshops aimed at exposing young people and the general public to creative disciplines, promoting cultural heritage and supporting the growth of Kwara State’s creative economy. The exhibition is also expected to inspire emerging creatives by demonstrating how music, art, film, design and other creative disciplines can serve as tools for self-expression, cultural preservation and social change. Olukoju said the initiative aligns with the vision of Governor AbdulRahman AbdulRazaq to harness Kwara State’s cultural heritage, creative talent and tourism potential as drivers of development. items.title: Circulation nocturne : Près de 400 motocyclistes interpellés pour défaut de casque à Ouagadougou
items.description: La Direction régionale de la police nationale du Kadiogo a intensifié les contrôles nocturnes du port du casque, ce 23 octobre 2026 à Ouagadougou, dans le cadre de l’opération « Bouclier tête durcie », portant sur la répression du défaut du casque. En trois heures, près de 400 usagers ont été interpellés dans la ville. Au carrefour du Rond-point des Nations unies, 34 motocyclistes ont été interpellés entre 18 h et 19 h 50 pour défaut de port du casque ou port non conforme. Au carrefour du Moogho Naaba, 26 usagers ont été concernés. Ils étaient 54 au carrefour de l’ASECNA et 37 à celui de Total Gounghin. Ces chiffres concernent quatre carrefours visités par la mission sur les 19 annoncés pour cette sortie. Pour Abdoulaziz Yonli, Directeur régional de la Police nationale du Kadiogo, cette opération répond au constat que malgré que le port du casque soit devenu plus fréquent en journée, les comportements changent à la tombée de la nuit, surtout dans les quartiers périphériques. « Les accidents ne préviennent pas. Les accidents ne choisissent pas de survenir dans la journée et de ne pas survenir la nuit. Les accidents peuvent survenir à tout moment » , a-t-il rappelé. Le Directeur régional souligne également que l’obscurité réduit la visibilité des usagers et que les phares peuvent éblouir les conducteurs. Il estime que les accidents nocturnes peuvent être particulièrement graves, d’où la nécessité de maintenir le port du casque à toute heure et quelle que soit la distance à parcourir. « Nous n’avons pas deux têtes, nous n’avons qu’une seule tête, nous n’avons qu’une seule vie. Et protéger sa vie en portant le casque, c’est d’abord protéger sa famille » , a insisté Abdoulaziz Yonli. Il rappelle qu’un accident peut également priver une famille d’un soutien et entraîner une perte pour la collectivité. « Je partais juste à côté » : des oublis qui se répètent-©Faso7 Parmi les personnes interpellées figure Ousmane Kaboré, vendeur de téléphones. Contrôlé au carrefour du Rond-point des Nations Unies, il explique avoir oublié son casque après avoir fermé sa boutique et s’être arrêté à une station-service. Reconnaissant son erreur, il salue l’action des policiers. « Je suis très conscient ce soir que c’est pour sensibiliser la population, la jeunesse. […] Le port du casque, c’est pour la santé de tout le monde» , a-t-il déclaré, avant de résumer le message de l’opération : « Mon casque, ma vie. » Au carrefour de l’ASECNA, Abdoulaye Kodia a lui aussi été interpellé. Il était sorti acheter de l’eau, avec une casquette sur la tête, après avoir oublié son casque à la maison. Il affirme avoir compris la raison du contrôle lorsque le policier lui a signalé son infraction. Pour le Directeur régional de la police nationale, ces explications reviennent régulièrement lors des contrôles. « La réponse est la même partout : “J’ai oublié mon casque ”, ou bien “ je partais juste à côté ”, ou bien “ je partais à la pharmacie, je n’avais pas l’esprit tranquille ”. C’est toujours la même chose », a-t-il relevé. Il insiste sur le fait qu’aucun déplacement ne justifie de se passer de cet équipement de protection. « Que vous partiez à la pharmacie ou que vous partiez à côté, il faut porter le casque. Ceux qui partent même à la pharmacie doivent avoir à l’esprit qu’ils doivent porter le casque, pour ne pas aller à la pharmacie deux fois. Pour aller à la pharmacie, faire un accident et être encore victime parce qu’on voulait sauver une vie », a-t-il lancé. La police appelle à maintenir les bons réflexes-©Faso7 Selon Abdoulaziz Yonli, les contrôles menés sur l’ensemble du dispositif ont permis d’estimer à près de 400 le nombre d’usagers interpellés en trois heures dans la ville de Ouagadougou. Ce bilan ne comprend pas les communes rattachées ni les zones périphériques situées en dehors du périmètre concerné. Le responsable déplore notamment que certains motocyclistes portent le casque pour se rendre au centre-ville, puis l’enlèvent une fois de retour dans leur quartier. D’autres le suspendent au guidon ou le posent sur la tête sans l’attacher correctement. La police nationale appelle ainsi les usagers à faire du port du casque un réflexe permanent, de jour comme de nuit, y compris pour les trajets de proximité. Elle invite également les responsables d’associations et les acteurs de la sécurité routière à poursuivre les actions de sensibilisation. « Que je puisse inculquer ça à mes enfants, que je puisse les amener eux-mêmes à m’interpeller lorsque je ne porte pas le casque et à moi aussi de les interpeller lorsqu’ils ne portent pas le casque » , a exhorté Abdoulaziz Yonli. L’opération « Bouclier tête durcie » se poursuit dans un contexte où la police entend faire respecter le port obligatoire du casque sur les engins à deux et trois roues. Au-delà des contrôles et des interpellations, l’enjeu reste d’ancrer durablement ce geste de protection dans les habitudes des usagers. Josué TIENDREBEOGO Faso7 L’article Circulation nocturne : Près de 400 motocyclistes interpellés pour défaut de casque à Ouagadougou est apparu en premier sur Faso7 .

items.title: Israel launches major West Bank operation after soldiers killed
items.description: Israel’s military launched an operation in the occupied West Bank on Friday, which it said would last several days and include searches and building demolitions, after gunmen killed two soldiers days ahead of Israeli elections in which security has been a key focus. Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu is locked in a tight race to keep his job in Tuesday’s vote, having campaigned on promises to keep Israelis safe , and he and his right-wing allies visited the scene of the attack to pledge an even harder line on West Bank militancy. Security forces were searching targets and questioning Palestinians to “locate and dismantle terrorist infrastructure” in the Hebron area from where they said the attackers had emerged, according to a joint statement from the Israeli military and Shin Bet domestic security agency. Israeli forces were also “demolishing illegal structures that could pose a security threat at the site of the encounter”, they said, adding that “counterterrorism operations” were underway at dozens of locations. The operation “is expected to continue for several days,” the statement, released late on Friday, said. Hamas, without claiming responsibility, praised Friday’s fatal attack on two Israeli soldiers as a “heroic operation” and called on supporters to carry out more. A Hebron-based AFP photographer heading to another assignment witnessed the gun battle break out at the Farsh al-Hawa checkpoint between the soldiers and two Palestinian men armed with a handgun and an automatic rifle. Israeli forces eventually shot dead the attackers. Netanyahu credited the soldiers with having “prevented what could have been a major attack”, and ordered a lockdown in the West Bank. Visiting Hebron, the premier said he and Defence Minister Israel Katz were “considering a very extensive IDF operation in Judea and Samaria, such as has not been carried out since” the 1967 war. The first step would see Israeli forces “enter the neighbourhood from which the terrorists came, evacuate the residents, go from house to house, and destroy the terrorist infrastructure,” he claimed. The military would apply a model previously used in refugee camps in the northern West Bank, he said, the scene of a large-scale operation launched in January 2025 that the United Nations said forcibly displaced thousands. Israeli rights group B’Tselem called for urgent international pressure to prevent Israel from pursuing “plans for collective punishment and acts that could constitute war crimes”. UN Secretary-General Antonio Guterres, through a spokesman, voiced concern over Israeli closures that affect Palestinian livelihoods and called for a halt to violence on all sides. ‘Exactly like Gaza’ Far-right Israeli Finance Minister Bezalel Smotrich, who also holds a position within the defence ministry, called for a large-scale military offensive in the West Bank “ exactly like in Gaza ”. National Security Minister and far-right firebrand Itamar Ben Gvir said the Ramallah-based “Palestinian Authority must be dismantled”. No evidence suggests that the Palestinian Authority — which exercises limited self-rule in parts of the West Bank — was connected to Friday’s attack. Both Ben Gvir and Smotrich are especially vocal supporters of Israeli settlements in the occupied West Bank, which have proliferated under Netanyahu’s government but are illegal under international law. Israel vowed to obliterate the group in the wake of the October 7, 2023 attack . Gadi Eisenkot, the former army chief who is Netanyahu’s top rival in the upcoming vote, said he was praying for soldiers wounded in Friday’s shooting. The operation comes as tensions soar in the West Bank, including over attacks by extremist Israeli settlers against Palestinian olive harvesters. According to an AFP tally based on data from the Palestinian health ministry, Israeli forces and settlers have killed 1,117 Palestinians in the territory since the start of the Gaza war in October 2023. Israeli figures show that at least 51 Israelis, including civilians and security personnel, have been killed in Palestinian attacks or during Israeli military operations during the same period.

items.title: Second Global Rosary Congress convenes in Wa to foster peace and religious tolerance
items.description: Thousands of Catholics, alongside diverse religious groups and traditional leaders, have convened at the Wa Malik Jaabre Sports Stadium for the second edition of the Global Rosary Congress. The three-day spiritual gathering, aimed at promoting evangelisation and peace, has drawn high-profile clerics and state officials advocating for religious harmony and spiritual renewal. Delivering the keynote address, Bishop of Damango Diocese Peter Paul Yelezuome urged the Christian community to see the Rosary as a powerful tool for evangelisation, not a passive tradition. He challenged the faithful to bear witness to Christ’s teachings in their daily lives to counteract societal vulnerabilities such as poverty, illiteracy, and tribal tensions that threaten the region’s peace. The rosary must be utilised as a weapon of prayer rather than a simple accessory, he stated, urging believers to actively pair their prayers with concrete acts of Christian charity. Founder and Leader of the Global Rosary Network Reverend Father David Obeng Paintsil recounted the origins of the Congress, which evolved from digital prayer sessions held during the 2022 pandemic closures. Highlighting the transformative power of the devotion, he shared a personal testimony of surviving a near-fatal car accident in 2016, attributing his miraculous escape from a burning vehicle to the intervention of the Blessed Virgin Mary. “The doors were opened on their own. No human intervention. The seat belt was released,” he recounted, noting that the incident solidified his dedication to spreading the Rosary. Upper West Regional Minister Charles Lwanga Puozuing expressed the region’s enthusiasm in hosting the monumental event. He emphasised the devotion’s capacity to foster peace and mutual respect across different religious denominations. Pledging his support for the spiritual exercise, the regional minister promised to purchase 50 rosaries for distribution among attendees lacking the prayer beads. The traditional leadership also threw its weight behind the Congress. Representing the Overlord of the Waala Traditional Council Wa Naa Fuseini Seidu Pelpuo IV, Divisional Chief Naa Wayodi Saaka delivered a message underscoring the deep-rooted religious tolerance in the municipality. “Whether Muslim, Christian, or traditionalist, we are all one people under one skin,” he stated, noting that religious diversity in Wa families has always been a source of strength rather than division. The Wa Naa’s representative welcomed the spiritual gathering, affirming the palace’s belief that where prayer goes up, blessings come down.

items.title: Fire breaks out at Hitler's mountain retreat, suspect detained: police
items.description: German police said Saturday they had detained a suspect following a fire at Adolf Hitler’s mountain retreat, known as the Eagle’s Nest, in the state of Bavaria. Around 200 firefighters were deployed to tackle the blaze at the Nazi dictator’s remote Kehlsteinhaus residence, on the peak of Obersalzberg in southern Germany. Firefighters saw flames rising high into the air as they approached the scene, only to find the building “completely ablaze”, police said. “A suspicious person was taken into temporary custody,” they said in a later statement, adding that nobody was injured in the blaze. Police spokeswoman Lisa Maier said firefighters struggled to tackle the blaze due to its location at an altitude of 1,834 metres. The building was only accessible with “heavy breathing apparatus”, she said. Authorities were alerted to the fire on Friday evening, when a smoke detector triggered a fire alarm at around 9:50pm (1950 GMT), police said. “The criminal police investigation is ongoing,” Maier added. German tabloid Bild reported that the authorities arrested a motorcyclist they came across on their way to the scene and that they suspected the fire was the result of arson. Built in the 1930s, the Eagle’s Nest forms part of the toxic legacy of Germany’s bitter 20th-century history.

items.title: 13 first-offender inmates discharged from Wa Central Prison under 2026 presidential amnesty
items.description: Thirteen first-offender inmates have been officially discharged from the Wa Central Prison after benefiting from the 2026 presidential amnesty granted by President John Dramani Mahama. The release ceremony, held on October 23, 2026, marked the discharge and reintegration of these individuals back into society. Upper West Regional Prisons Commander DDP Alhaji Ousmane Tasembedo revealed that 18 names were initially submitted to the prison headquarters for amnesty consideration. Out of this number, 13 were approved by the President in conformity with Article 72(1) of the 1992 Constitution. However, only three inmates were discharged at the ceremony, as the remaining 10 had already gone home through the standard one-third sentence discharge process before the amnesty reached them due to bureaucratic processes. The regional commander emphasised that the amnesty represents an opportunity for transformation and a fresh beginning rather than merely a release from custody. He noted that the Wa Central Prisons has successfully reformed and rehabilitated 34 inmates since 2024. Among the 13 approved amnesty beneficiaries, two acquired vocational skills in smock sewing and tailoring. He assured them that the service would provide them with start-up materials to begin their new lives. Assembly Member for Jonga and Wa Municipal Justice and Security Chairman Daubile Alhassan Ibrahim, representing the Municipal Chief Executive, cautioned the beneficiaries to conduct themselves properly as they reintegrate into society. He clarified that the amnesty does not provide immunity from future prosecution. “It doesn’t mean that when you are granted this amnesty today and you go out there and commit any offense the law will not say oh some time ago the president was granted you amnesty to go home and rest,” he warned. Speaking on behalf of the beneficiaries, 39-year-old Yakubu Anas expressed deep appreciation to the President for the unique opportunity. Anas also extended gratitude to the regional command for the vocational training received during their incarceration, promising to put the acquired skills to good use and maintain good behaviour. Nuokpem Richard, speaking for the families of the beneficiaries, thanked the government and prison officials for the training provided to the inmates. “We are praying that they should go and continue and then achieve their aim at the end of the day they should be somebody in the near future,” he stated.

items.title: NA body summons Punjab police chief over Hina Javed murder case
items.description: RAWALPINDI: The National Assembly Standing Committee on Interior and Narcotics Control has summoned the Punjab inspector general of police (IGP), regional police officer (RPO), city police officer (CPO) Rawalpindi, SSP Investigation and additional inspector general of the Crime Control Department (CCD) to brief it on the investigation into the alleged brutal murder of Hina Javed. The committee meeting is scheduled for Thursday, October 29, 2026, at 2pm in the committee room at Parliament House, Islamabad. The police officials will brief committee members on the latest developments in the high-profile murder case. The Punjab government has also formed a three-member high-powered committee to review the investigation into Hina Javed’s murder. Her husband and domestic servant have been placed on judicial remand at Adiala Jail in connection with the case. The committee has already visited Rawalpindi, questioned the deceased woman’s husband and domestic servant at Adiala Jail, met her family and inspected the crime scene. The panel comprises Additional IG CCD Sohail Chatta, DIG Lahore Shoaib Khurram Janbaz and SSP Investigation Rawalpindi Saifullah. According to the postmortem and DNA report analysis , evidence collected during the investigation indicated that Hina Javed had been brutally tortured. The report noted blue marks on her hands and arms and a 27-centimetre-deep wound on her neck. The report also stated that DNA collected from bloodstains, bedsheets allegedly used in the strangulation, a door lock and a door handle matched the DNA of the domestic servant. Evidence collected for DNA testing included swabs from the deceased’s left-hand fingernails, samples taken from her body and pieces of cloth from a bedsheet bearing suspected bloodstains and spermatozoa. According to the report, the samples matched the domestic worker’s blood. A reddish piece of carpet bearing suspected stains was also recovered from the southeastern bedroom of the apartment where the crime occurred. The report said the stains matched the blood and sperm attributed to Zeeshan Arshad. The investigation has focused on the domestic servant’s alleged involvement, with the reported DNA findings forming part of the evidence under examination. Meanwhile, Hina Javed’s family has again expressed mistrust in the Rawalpindi police investigation and the claims made by the CCD chief, demanding the formation of a judicial commission to probe the murder. The family has alleged that police are protecting the main accused while holding the domestic servant responsible for the crime. The initial postmortem examination and police report stated that Hina Javed’s body was found in the washroom of her apartment with signs of torture, including a strangulation mark around her neck, an injury below her right lip and bleeding from her nose. Published in Dawn, October 24th, 2026

Joyce Bawah Mogtari urges unity as NDC holds constituency elections
items.description: Senior Presidential Advisor and Senior Aide to President John Dramani Mahama, Joyce Bawah Mogtari, has urged members of the National Democratic Congress (NDC) to prioritise unity and solidarity as the party holds its constituency elections today, Saturday, October 24. In a Facebook post on Saturday, she extended her best wishes to aspirants, delegates and party members working to ensure a peaceful, transparent, credible and successful electoral process. She said the strength of the NDC had always rested on its members, particularly those who dedicate their time, energy and resources to the party’s growth, often without recognition. “To every aspirant, thank you for stepping forward to serve. To our cherished delegates, I trust that you will exercise your responsibility with wisdom, fairness, and the collective interest of our great party at heart,” she said. Mrs Bawah Mogtari urged successful candidates to lead with humility and reach out to those who lose, while encouraging unsuccessful aspirants to remain committed to the party. She stressed that the elections should not undermine the relationships built among members, insisting that the party’s collective responsibility to Ghanaians must remain paramount. “Our focus must remain on the bigger picture: supporting His Excellency President John Dramani Mahama and his government to ensure our shared commitment to improving the lives of the Ghanaian people,” she added. She said while the elections would pass and positions would change hands, the bonds of comradeship and the party’s responsibility to the people must endure. Mrs Bawah Mogtari concluded by wishing the NDC a peaceful and successful electoral process and called for continued solidarity among members.

items.title: Nigerian woman jailed seven years for human trafficking in Tamale
items.description: A 24-year-old Nigerian woman has been sentenced to seven years’ imprisonment with hard labour for human trafficking after a trial at the Gender-Based Violence Court in Tamale. Mariam Yussif was convicted on October 22, 2026, following a police investigation into the alleged recruitment and movement of victims from Nigeria to Ghana for sexual exploitation. The Northern Regional Police Command said Yussif and her 22-year-old sister, Precious Clement, were arrested at Yendi on August 17, 2026, over their alleged involvement in the operation. Yussif was subsequently charged under Section 2(1) of the Human Trafficking Act, 2005 (Act 694), and appeared before the court on August 19. She pleaded not guilty and was remanded into custody while the case proceeded. After several adjournments, the court concluded the trial and found her guilty, leading to the custodial sentence. She has since been transferred to Tamale Central Prison to begin serving her term. Sister released, victims reunited with families The police said no case was established against Clement, who was released. The two victims connected to the case have also been repatriated to Nigeria and reunited with their respective families. The outcome brings the prosecution to a close against Yussif, while the release of her sister underscores the need for individual responsibility to be established through evidence in trafficking investigations. The Northern Regional Police Command said the conviction demonstrated the importance of intelligence-led operations, thorough investigations and effective prosecution in tackling human trafficking. It urged members of the public to report suspected trafficking cases to the appropriate authorities, reaffirming its commitment to protecting vulnerable people and pursuing those involved in the crime. Human trafficking involves the recruitment, movement or receipt of people through prohibited means for the purpose of exploitation. Sexual exploitation is one of the forms of abuse traffickers may seek to facilitate. The police have encouraged the public to remain alert to suspected cases and provide information that could help law enforcement agencies intervene and protect potential victims.

items.title: À une semaine des élections de mi-mandat, Obama s’engage dans la campagne
items.description: L’ancien président démocrate se rendra à Cleveland aujourd’hui, samedi 24, aux côtés d’Amy Acton, candidate au poste de gouverneure de l’État, et de Sherrod Brown, candidat au Sénat, qui se présente contre le républicain Jon Husted. Celui-ci avait été nommé en janvier 2025 par le gouverneur Mike DeWine en remplacement de J.D. Vance. Obama tiendra ensuite à Détroit un meeting de soutien à Abdul El-Sayed, candidat au Sénat face au républicain Mike Rogers, et à Jocelyn Benson, candidate au poste de gouverneure. Obama était jusqu’à présent resté largement en retrait de la campagne démocrate sur le terrain. Mis à part une courte apparition en mai aux côtés du candidat au Sénat du Texas James Talarico – qui pourrait devenir le premier démocrate élu sénateur de l’État depuis 1988 – puis une vidéo de soutien, en juillet, à Josh Turek, candidat au Sénat en Iowa, il s’était surtout consacré à des levées de fonds et à l’enregistrement de spots de campagne. Des sondages favorables ou serrés dans des États remportés par Trump en 2024, au Texas mais aussi au Kansas et dans le Nebraska – où les démocrates soutiennent l’indépendant Dan Osborn –, pourraient priver les républicains de leur majorité à la chambre haute du Congrès. Avec une majorité à la Chambre des représentants pour laquelle les démocrates font figure de favoris, une telle victoire réduirait considérablement les marges d’action de Trump pour les deux dernières années de son mandat. Barack Obama est le plus populaire des anciens présidents encore en vie : selon un sondage CNN/SSRS conduit en mai, 57 % des Américains en ont une opinion favorable, contre 34 % pour Trump et 30 % pour Joe Biden CNN poll on presidents , CNN/SSRS, 18 juin 2026.'> 1 . Il est également le plus à même de jouer un rôle de « faiseur de rois » : selon une enquête NBC de septembre, 43 % des électeurs se disent plus enclins à voter pour un candidat soutenu par Obama, contre 33 % pour Bernie Sanders et 30 % pour Trump NBC September 2026 Poll , 20 septembre 2026.'> 2 . Son implication vise également à soutenir les finances des démocrates. Si les candidats du parti devancent leurs opposants républicains en levées de fonds dans plusieurs campagnes clefs (James Talarico au Texas, Adam Hamilton au Kansas, Troy Jackson dans le Maine…), les méga-donateurs républicains ont injecté des centaines de millions de dollars ces derniers mois dans les super-PAC qui soutiennent le GOP. À lui seul, Elon Musk a contribué environ 289 millions de dollars à des groupes républicains et à son propre super-PAC entre juillet et septembre. Le milliardaire, proche allié de Trump, a injecté 158 millions de dollars dans la course au Sénat au Texas pour soutenir le procureur général de l’État, Ken Paxton, qui affrontera Talarico le 3 novembre. Selon les derniers sondages, agrégés par l’analyste électoral Nate Silver, Talarico dispose d’une courte avance de 2,4 points. L’article À une semaine des élections de mi-mandat, Obama s’engage dans la campagne est apparu en premier sur Le Grand Continent .

items.title: Mr Drew’s X Space outburst would not happen under my watch – NanaYaw Wiredu
items.description: Media entrepreneur and talent manager NanaYaw Wiredu says the recent social media incident involving Ghanaian musician Mr Drew would not have happened under his watch. Speaking to Evergreen Asantewaa on Woezor TV’s Breakfast Café , NanaYaw referred to Mr Drew’s heated exchange with a participant during an X Space discussion. The incident escalated after the participant addressed the singer as “chale”, prompting Mr Drew to insist that they were not age mates and to argue that differences in age and financial standing should command respect. The exchange ended with insults from both sides. “Recently you saw what happened to Mr Drew. It will never happen under my watch,” Nana Yaw said. He explained that artistes working with him are trained on how to speak on television, participate in radio interviews and respond when provoked. “Because you don’t want to put somebody off by saying the wrong thing,” he added. NanaYaw made the remarks during a discussion on building a successful music career. He stressed that artiste development involves more than producing hit songs and promoting music. It also requires preparing musicians to handle public attention and maintain a good relationship with their audience. Mr Drew’s X Space controversy The incident involving Mr Drew occurred during an X Space he hosted to interact with fans and promote his single Steeze . The discussion turned tense after a participant addressed him as “chale”, a popular Ghanaian expression often used informally among friends and peers. Mr Drew objected to the manner in which he was addressed, insisting that the participant was not his mate and arguing that differences in the age, social status and financial standing should be recognised. “I am not your mate. A lot of people think I am their mate, but I am not your mate. A lot of the boys think they are my age mates. When it comes to money and age, I am not your mate, and you need to put that in your head,” he said. The participant challenged the singer’s response, arguing that he was not an A-list artiste to make such a distinction. The exchange escalated, with both parties trading insults and Mr Drew threatening to block the participant. The confrontation attracted criticism on social media, with some users questioning the musician’s response, while others argued that artistes should be treated respectfully during online interactions. Mr Drew later clarified that his outburst was directed at trolls rather than his genuine fans. The importance of media training in artiste development NanaYaw Wiredu’s comments raises concerns about the importance of preparing musicians for public engagement as part of their professional development. Media training can help artistes communicate effectively during interviews, manage difficult questions and respond to provocation without escalating disagreements. In September 2023, Mr Wiredu, founder and creative director of Oneplay Africa, announced a free online Music Master Series aimed at helping emerging entertainment executives understand the business side of the music industry. His experience spans artiste management, publicity, publishing, events management and digital media. He has also managed artistes, including Nana Yaa, D-Flex and Mzbel, and worked on events such as Ghana Meets Naija and Mzbel at 10, according to published profiles. He is currently the PR Manager for Edem Goget’em.

items.description: The Akwamu Royal Family of Nchiraa in the Bono Region has appealed to the President, John Dramani Mahama, and the Inspector-General of Police (IGP) to intervene in a fatal shooting incident that allegedly claimed the life of a six-year-old boy during the town’s Fofie Yam Festival. The deceased, Agyei Agyapong Gethro, was buried on Friday, October 23, 2026, following the incident on October 3, 2026. At a press conference, the acting head of the Akwamu Royal Family, Opanin Paul Kwabena Baffoe, called for a thorough and impartial investigation to establish the circumstances surrounding the shooting and ensure that anyone found culpable was dealt with in accordance with the law. The family also appealed to the Bono Regional Minister, the Wenchi Municipal Chief Executive (MCE) and the Wenchi Divisional Police Command to intervene and provide answers to the bereaved family and the people of Nchiraa. It said it wanted the authorities to clarify what led to the shooting, identify those involved and explain the progress of police investigations. The family expressed concern about recurring misunderstandings and gunfire during celebrations of the Fofie Yam Festival, questioning why such incidents continued to occur during an occasion that should bring the community together. It called for calm while urging the security agencies to pursue the matter to its logical conclusion. The Assembly Member for the Dwomoo/Nteema Electoral Area, George Nketia, also appealed to the youth of Nchiraa to remain calm and allow the police to investigate the incident. He said those found to have been involved would be arrested, echoing the royal family’s call for accountability. Mr Nketia further cautioned the youth against carrying guns to public gatherings and other community events, warning against conduct that could lead to violence and loss of life.

items.title: Man held for torturing female scooty rider in Lahore
items.description: LAHORE: The police on Friday claimed to have arrested a man who had allegedly tortured and injured a young woman riding a scooty on busy Mozang Link Road in the city. Identified as Ghulam Mustafa, the attacker was tracked down and arrested by the police with the help of data of dozens of the Punjab Safe Cities Authority (PSCA) cameras, besides using traditional investigation techniques. He was sent behind the bars after being nominated in a criminal case. A CCTV footage of the incident, which took place late on Thursday, sparked widespread public outrage once footage was aired. The footage showed the suspect overtook the scooty rider on the busy road, placed his bike in front of her two wheeler and subjected her to brutal torture in the presence of several passersby. It was shocking to observe that none of the onlookers tried to intervene and rescue the woman. The man pulled her hair and slapped her repeatedly. As per initial police reports, the woman suffered facial injuries, including nasal bone fracture, during the brutal attack. A police official says the attacker also threw the victim’s bag on the ground that contained a laptop valuing around Rs90,000, resulting in severe damage to the laptop. The suspect later fled the scene in the presence of several onlookers, he adds. A special police team, under the supervision of Civil Lines Superintendent of Police (SP) Maniza Karamat, tracked down and arrested the suspect using modern digital tracking technology. The official says that a case has been lodged against the attacker on the complaint of the victim’s father. Published in Dawn, October 24th, 2026

items.title: Une IA estime le risque de mortalité des patients atteints de cancer à partir d’un selfie
items.description: Des chercheurs américains ont développé un outil d’intelligence artificielle capable d’évaluer le risque de mortalité à court terme chez des patients atteints de cancer à partir d’une simple photographie du visage. Publiée dans la revue The Lancet Digital Health, cette étude ouvre des perspectives pour le suivi médical, tout en soulignant les limites de cette technologie. Une simple photo du visage pourrait-elle fournir des indications sur l’état de santé d’un patient atteint de cancer ? C’est la piste explorée par une équipe de chercheurs de l’hôpital Mass General Brigham, dans le Massachusetts, aux États-Unis. Leur outil, baptisé FAHR-FaceSurvival, utilise l’intelligence artificielle pour analyser certains traits du visage et estimer le risque de mortalité à court terme. Le modèle repose sur FAHR-Face, une intelligence artificielle préentraînée sur plus de 40 millions d’images faciales, puis adaptée à cette application médicale grâce à 34 363 photographies de patients atteints de cancer. Les chercheurs ont ensuite évalué ses performances sur un sous-groupe de 3 820 patients issu de la base de données Harvard-RT. Selon les résultats publiés dans The Lancet Digital Health, l’outil a identifié un groupe de 122 patients considérés comme présentant un risque élevé de mortalité. Parmi eux, 52,5 % sont décédés dans les 90 jours suivant l’évaluation. À l’inverse, seuls 2 % des 975 patients classés dans la catégorie de risque la plus faible sont décédés au cours de cette même période. Ces résultats suggèrent que les informations extraites d’une photographie faciale pourraient contribuer à repérer certains patients particulièrement vulnérables. Ils ne signifient toutefois pas qu’un selfie permet, à lui seul, de déterminer avec certitude l’évolution d’un cancer ou les chances de survie d’une personne. Une IA pour estimer aussi l’âge biologique Les chercheurs ont également développé un second outil, baptisé FAHR-FaceAge, conçu pour estimer l’âge biologique d’une personne à partir de son visage. Contrairement à l’âge chronologique, qui correspond au nombre d’années écoulées depuis la naissance, l’âge biologique cherche à refléter certains aspects du vieillissement de l’organisme. Testé sur plusieurs ensembles de données, ce modèle a notamment permis d’observer des différences de mortalité à court terme selon l’écart entre l’âge biologique estimé et l’âge réel des patients. Parmi 1 060 patients dont l’âge biologique estimé dépassait d’au moins 20 ans leur âge chronologique, 21 % sont décédés dans les 90 jours suivant l’évaluation. À l’opposé, environ 6 % des 4 195 patients dont l’âge biologique estimé était inférieur d’au moins dix ans à leur âge réel sont décédés pendant la même période. Les chercheurs soulignent que les deux outils apportent des informations complémentaires. Les résultats de FAHR-FaceAge et de FAHR-FaceSurvival sont faiblement corrélés, et leurs associations avec la survie restent indépendantes lorsqu’ils sont étudiés conjointement. L’étude relève également que certains facteurs liés au mode de vie, notamment le tabagisme et une consommation importante d’alcool, sont associés à un vieillissement prématuré du visage. Les modifications cosmétiques, comme le maquillage ou la chirurgie esthétique, n’ont pas affecté les performances de FAHR-FaceAge dans les tests rapportés. Des résultats prometteurs, mais des limites importantes Pour les auteurs, ces technologies pourraient, à terme, compléter les évaluations médicales classiques. Les photographies faciales présentent notamment l’avantage d’être faciles et peu coûteuses à obtenir, ce qui pourrait faciliter leur utilisation dans certains contextes de soins. Les chercheurs insistent néanmoins sur un point essentiel : ces outils ne sont pas destinés à remplacer les médecins ni à se substituer à leur jugement clinique. Ils pourraient plutôt contribuer à enrichir l’évaluation de l’état de santé et à accompagner certaines décisions thérapeutiques personnalisées. La performance de ces modèles devra donc être confirmée par des recherches supplémentaires, dans des contextes médicaux et auprès de populations plus diversifiés. The post Une IA estime le risque de mortalité des patients atteints de cancer à partir d’un selfie appeared first on Hespress Français - Actualités du Maroc .

Burkina : le gouvernement veut mobiliser 67,2 milliards pour renforcer l’autonomie économique des ménages vulnérables en 5 ans
items.description: Le Conseil des ministres a marqué jeudi son accord pour la ratification d’un financement de 67,2 milliards de FCFA destiné à la mise en œuvre du Projet d’autonomisation économique des ménages pauvres et vulnérables pour la résilience et la protection sociale adaptative (PARPS), qui vise à soutenir 120 000 ménages pauvres et vulnérables sur l’ensemble du territoire national sur une période de cinq ans. Selon le compte rendu du Conseil des ministres, le projet prévoit notamment l’organisation de 120 000 ménages pauvres et vulnérables en coopératives communautaires autour d’unités économiques, ainsi que la mise en place de 4 800 coopératives communautaires et de 1 200 unités économiques locales destinées à soutenir les activités de production et de transformation. Il prévoit également la construction de six magasins d’une capacité de 5 000 tonnes chacun, de deux entrepôts modernes de stockage et de 20 magasins d’une capacité de 1 000 tonnes chacun. En matière de logistique, le projet prévoit l’acquisition de huit véhicules, de 20 camions monoblocs, de 20 camions-bennes et de deux camions-citernes. Sa mise en œuvre concernera prioritairement les régions des Koulsé, de Yaadga, du Nakambé, de Nando, des Bankui et du Sourou, en tenant compte du déploiement progressif du Registre social unique (RSU). La ratification de l’ordonnance relative à ce financement intervient conformément à la loi n°23-2025/ALT du 29 décembre 2025 portant habilitation du Gouvernement à autoriser, par voie d’ordonnance, la ratification des accords et conventions de financement signés entre le Burkina Faso et ses partenaires techniques et financiers. D’un montant total de 120 millions de dollars, soit 67 222 473 360 FCFA, ce financement est composé d’un accord de crédit et d’un accord de don signés le 14 juillet 2026 entre le Burkina Faso et l’Association internationale de développement (IDA), selon le compte rendu du Conseil des ministres du jeudi 22 octobre 2026. Agence d’information du Burkina NAK/yos/ata L’article Burkina : le gouvernement veut mobiliser 67,2 milliards pour renforcer l’autonomie économique des ménages vulnérables en 5 ans est apparu en premier sur NetAfrique.net .

items.title: ¿Dónde viven los caseros? Barrios de renta alta y zonas turísticas concentran a quienes declaran ingresos de alquiler
items.description: Los barrios de mayor renta del país y los distritos con mayor dinamismo turístico suelen concentrar una mayor proporción de contribuyentes que declaran en su IRPF ingresos por el alquiler de inmuebles . En algunas de las urbanizaciones más acomodadas y exclusivas del país, aproximadamente una de cada tres personas perciben rendimientos inmobiliarios. Dos ejemplos llamativos de Madrid son Fuente del Fresno (San Sebastián de los Reyes) y La Moraleja (Alcobendas), donde los porcentajes de caseros alcanzan el 39% y el 36%. La proporción también supera con holgura el 30% en otros barrios acomodados como Pla del Remei (Valencia), Ciudalcampo (San Sebastián de los Reyes) o Pedralbes-Sarriá y Vallvidrera-Tibidabo i Les Planes (Barcelona), en los que la renta media total por contribuyente supera los 100.000 euros. items.title: Bolt Food’s Kumasi business has more than doubled as growth continues into its second year
items.description: Nearly two years after expanding to Kumasi, Bolt Food saw strong growth in the city, with activity increasing by more than 100% year-on-year in its second year of operations. The continued growth points to sustained adoption of app-based delivery beyond Accra and the growing role of Kumasi as an important market for Bolt Food in Ghana. Since entering Kumasi, Bolt Food has continued to connect customers with local restaurants through its platform, giving local restaurants and other food merchants an additional channel to reach customers beyond physical footfall. Bolt Food’s General Manager, Ali Zaryab, said Kumasi’s performance demonstrates why expanding beyond the capital was an important part of Bolt Food’s growth strategy in Ghana. “When we expanded Bolt Food to Kumasi, we saw an opportunity to serve one of Ghana’s largest and most commercially active cities. Nearly two years later, the fact that the business is still growing at more than 100% year-on-year shows that the demand was not simply an initial launch effect. Customers are continuing to adopt delivery as part of how they access restaurants and increasingly other everyday products across the city,” he said. The growth also reflects a broader evolution in how customers are using delivery platforms. While restaurant meals remain an important part of the delivery experience, the sustained growth suggests that delivery is becoming a familiar option for customers seeking convenience. “What is particularly encouraging about Kumasi is not just the growth, but the breadth of demand we’re beginning to see,” Zaryab added. “Food delivery may have been the starting point, but customers are increasingly looking for convenience across different parts of their day. That creates an opportunity for restaurants to reach customers in new ways.” Bolt Food said it will continue working with local merchants and couriers as it strengthens its operations in Kumasi and responds to changing customer demand. The performance comes as Bolt Food continues to grow its delivery offering in Ghana, connecting customers with restaurants and retailers through its app.

items.title: Leer a Pedro Almodóvar: “El escritor es egoísta por naturaleza”
items.description: Libros que los personajes escriben, leen, regalan. Libros que saltan de una película a otra, que inspiran tramas, que se adaptan. La filmografía de Pedro Almodóvar está plagada de referencias literarias. Ha publicado numerosos relatos a lo largo de las décadas, algunos de ellos reunidos en El último sueño (2023). Pero ha esperado hasta los 77 años para publicar su primera novela: El hombre que solo escribía en los aviones (Reservoir Books), que llega a las librerías el 29 de octubre. Un libro frenético y libre, como su cine, atravesado por la pasión lectora. Lo protagoniza Flavio Guijarro, nueva incorporación al fecundo plantel de personajes almodovarianos. Un coach de autores obsesionado con escribir. Como tantos protagonistas del manchego, Flavio tiene mucho de él. Es sabido que la obra de Almodóvar es un ente poroso por el que circulan la ficción, la realidad, lo vivido, lo escuchado, lo leído. Esta entrevista discurre por esos poros y se centra en el Almodóvar lector y escritor. Recibe a Babelia en las oficinas madrileñas de El Deseo, su productora, con las paredes llenas de recuerdos y carteles de sus películas llegados de todos los rincones del mundo. Preside su despacho una gran estantería llena de libros que, advierte, son sobre todo novedades que le llegan. Su biblioteca más personal, admite, está en su casa. Sobre la mesa, eso sí, el último libro que le ha fascinado, Cosamala, de Alana S. Portero , autora hacia la que se deshace en elogios. Se enciende la grabadora y aparece un Almodóvar sereno, amable, cómodo con una conversación ajena a la clásica promoción del cine, alejado de la ansiedad que, dice, ha sido un motor de su novela.
