items.description: Ni un euro. El Ayuntamiento de Madrid quiere pasar los gastos que deriven de la acampada de la Puerta del Sol ―limpieza, reparaciones, desperfectos― a quienes están durmiendo o han dormido en el campamento. Con estas palabras lo expuso la vicealcaldesa, Inma Sanz: “Por supuesto, trataremos de repercutir hasta el último euro que se vaya a gastar este Ayuntamiento a los causantes de esta situación, que son los que están allí de manera ilegal y los que lo están consintiendo por dejación de funciones [por la delegación del Gobierno]. No vamos a parar hasta tratar de que a los madrileños no nos cueste un euro”, dijo el jueves en la rueda de prensa semanal posterior a la Junta de Gobierno, sin explicar nada más al respecto. A cómo prevén hacerlo, un portavoz responde que “se está estudiando”. Seguir leyendo

items.title: Cinco días frenéticos en los consulados para cumplir el ultimátum del Supremo: “Es como reparar un avión en pleno vuelo”
items.description: “Nos va a volver locos este asunto”. Una fuente consular resume así el desconcierto que se ha instalado estos días en los consulados, obligados a hacer frente a una carrera contrarreloj para cumplir con la orden del Tribunal Supremo de identificar a los nacionalizados por la ley de nietos que hayan acreditado la condición de exiliados de sus antepasados. Este viernes, el alto tribunal puso en marcha la cuenta atrás, y dio cinco días a los ministerios de Exteriores y Justicia para que remitan a la Sala de lo Contencioso-Administrativo, a la Junta Electoral Central y a la Oficina del Censo Electoral los nombres de los 163.020 afectados por la suspensión del derecho al voto . Seguir leyendo

items.title: Los murales para el Waldorf Astoria de Nueva York en 1929 acaban en Boadilla tras una disputa entre Madrid y Cataluña
items.description: Se crearon para decorar el hotel más exclusivo de Nueva York y han terminado protegidas por Madrid en la ciudad financiera del Banco Santander en Boadilla del Monte. Para cubrir ese viaje transoceánico de casi un siglo, las quince pinturas murales de Josep María Sert , pintor de vida novelesca, y testigo de las convulsiones de un tiempo marcado por la Guerra Civil y las dos guerras mundiales, han protagonizado un recorrido excepcional. Primero, por su coste: 150.000 dólares de 1929, una cifra nunca vista, “desorbitada”, en descripción de los técnicos de la Comunidad de Madrid que las han estudiado. Luego, por su emplazamiento original: el hotel Waldorf Astoria , por entonces la medida del lujo, que honró al artista bautizando una sala con su nombre (la Sert Room) sin esperar a que muriera, como destacó él mismo. Y finalmente, por haber estado en un limbo administrativo inusitado: aunque la Generalitat de Cataluña fue quien inició los trámites para declarar Bien de Interés Cultural los lienzos cuando volvieron a España (lo que impide venderlos en el extranjero y obliga a conservarlos) ha sido Madrid quien ha logrado darles esa protección casi 40 años después. Seguir leyendo

items.title: Santiaga Sánchez Porcel, pastora y agricultora: “Yo no estudié y ahora vienen de la Universidad a ver cómo trabajo mi finca”
items.description: Lleva el maletero lleno de tierra, una mirada limpia y porta una riñonera con unas bolsitas de las almendras que vende a través de una cooperativa. Santiaga Sánchez Porcel (59 años, Fuente Grande, Vélez-Rubio, Almería) ha llegado a Madrid para acudir a una feria con la misión de dar a conocer Alvelal , la asociación que preside y que impulsa la regeneración ambiental, social y económica del Altiplano Estepario del sureste de España (con zonas de Almería, Granada y Murcia). “Además, llevo 10 kilos de nuestro suelo en el coche para dejarlos en la Universidad Politécnica de Madrid. Tenemos un proyecto a tres años con ellos en los que analizan por qué aumenta la materia orgánica de nuestra tierra”. Seguir leyendo

items.title: La mujer que cosió un supermercado: “Me dedico a crear universos paralelos hechos de fieltro”
items.description: Lucy Sparrow (Bath, Reino Unido, 40 años) es una de las creadoras más disruptivas del mundo. Sus trabajos, siempre situados en entornos cotidianos y comunitarios para “resultar inmediatamente reconocibles para cualquier público” han ido creciendo en ambición, volumen y expansión desde su primera instalación, en 2014, llamada Corner Shop. “Erra una tienda tradicional británica de barrio que llené con 4.000 objetos hechos a mano con fieltro. Tras el éxito de aquella exposición, asumí el reto de llevar mi práctica artística hacia exposiciones cada vez más grandes y complejas, hasta llegar a la instalación de 1.000 metros cuadrados que actualmente se puede visitar en The Momentary Museum de Bentonville, Arkansas”, cuenta Sparrow a ICON. Seguir leyendo

items.title: ‘Matar a un oso’: la serie que cuenta cómo el asesinato de un plantígrado se convirtió en una exhaustiva investigación judicial
items.description: Fue una de las muertes más sonadas ocurridas durante el confinamiento de 2020. Y eso que el asesinado era un oso, Cachou, plantígrado poco querido por los ganaderos del Valle de Arán porque en los meses anteriores a su muerte se había cebado con la ganadería equina. Pero el crimen escondía conflictos lastrados, enfrentamientos soterrados y dio pie a una investigación judicial con secreto de sumario incluido, un cóctel que ha acabado convertido en serie, Matar a un oso, liderada por los hermanos Sánchez-Cabezudo, y que Movistar Plus estrena el 10 de diciembre, aunque antes se ha proyectado, este viernes, en la primera jornada de la Seminci. Ha llegado antes un producto audiovisual que una sentencia: los dos acusados por el asesinato del plantígrado aún siguen a la espera de juicio. Seguir leyendo

items.title: Juicio latino al trumpismo
items.description: Estados Unidos ya lleva una semana votando y los primeros datos del sufragio anticipado para las legislativas del 3 de noviembre transmiten que los estadounidenses tienen ganas de decir algo en las urnas sobre la situación de su país. Aún no sabemos exactamente qué es. Hasta el viernes, ya habían participado más de 23 millones de personas, un aumento generalizado respecto a 2022. En Texas, donde está en juego un escaño del Senado que supondría un vuelco político sensacional si cayera en manos demócratas, las dos principales áreas metropolitanas, Dallas y Houston, registraron un récord de votos en el primer día hábil, el pasado lunes. El 30% de los electores de Texas son latinos. Las encuestas generales indican más movilización entre los demócratas. Seguir leyendo

items.title: Perder las formas
items.description: Manuel Fernández-Montesinos apenas se acordaba de su padre ni de su tío Federico, asesinados los dos, con un día de diferencia, cuando él tenía cuatro años. Las fotos le concedían un espejismo de memoria. En la vida de un niño las personas desaparecen y nadie se ocupa de darle explicaciones, por un deseo de protección que a Fernández-Montesinos le pareció siempre equivocado. El padre y el tío tan querido unas veces están y otras ya no están, y ni siquiera vuelven a aparecer en ese porvenir indeterminado de la conciencia infantil, regresados de un viaje, trayendo ese regalo que quizás el niño no olvide nunca, aunque no pueda recordar al que fue su porrtador. El espacio en blanco de los muertos lo ocuparon en la niñez y la juventud de Manuel Fernández-Montesinos dos hombres mayores que a él se lo parecerían más aún, físicamente bien sólidos, a diferencia de los queridos fantasmas fotográficos, con un aspecto formal de señores de otro tiempo, casi de otro siglo: su abuelo Federico y quien él llamó siempre el tío Fernando, Fernando de los Ríos. En las fotos don Federico García Rodríguez tiene una gran cabeza cuadrada sobre un torso cuadrado y fornido, más rotundo aún por los hombros rectos y las anchas solapas de la chaqueta de un traje negro que durante los últimos nueve años de su vida fue un traje invariable de luto. En el paraíso de la Huerta de San Vicente , en la que el niño conoció y perdió muy pronto la eternidad feliz del verano, el abuelo era el gigante bondadoso que velaba por el nieto y le regalaba caramelillos y herramientas de hortelano hechas a la medida de las manos y las fuerzas infantiles por un herrero amigo. La silueta de encina del abuelo se recorta con la misma nitidez en la huerta familiar, en la cubierta del barco donde lo que queda de la familia va a exiliarse en Estados Unidos, en la orilla del río Hudson y entre los robles y los arces de Riverside Park, donde el antiguo niño hortelano ahora juega al beisbol y habla inglés sin ningún rastro de acento. Seguir leyendo

items.title: Susan Sarandon: “A veces me llaman comunista. Creo que es la manera que tienen algunos de decir que alguien está como una cabra”
items.description: El 25 de septiembre, apenas una semana después de esta entrevista, Susan Sarandon (Nueva York, 80 años) fue detenida a las puertas de la ONU en Nueva York. Protestaba, junto a otras actrices como Hannah Einbinder o Cynthia Nixon , contra la comparecencia en la Asamblea del primer ministro israelí, Benjamin Netanyahu. No era la primera vez que la detenían y quizás no sea la última. Susan Sarandon, actriz en más de 100 películas, ha protagonizado éxitos de Hollywood como El cliente, Quédate a mi lado o Las brujas de Eastwick; películas de culto como The Rocky Horror Picture Show o Thelma y Louise ; y películas comprometidas como Pena de muerte , que le valió un Oscar. Ha aparecido en la serie Friends y ha rodado con Louis Malle. Porque Sarandon escoge sus proyectos como vive, de forma desprejuiciada, con una mezcla de curiosidad y desafío: “Cuando leo un guion quiero que me conmueva. Quiero que el personaje sea algo que no haya hecho antes. Está muy bien si hay un director con una buena trayectoria, pero a veces son directores nuevos. Es genial si te pueden pagar, pero a veces no pueden”. Es el caso de su último proyecto, The Accompanist (aún pendiente de título en español), donde interpreta a Sylvia, una madre de acogida atormentada y excéntrica. Seguir leyendo Estilismo: Juan Cebrián Maquillaje, peluquería y manicura: Genevieve Herr (Sally Harlor), Matthew Monzon (TMG LA) y Pattie Yankee. Producción: Cristina Serrano. Asistente de producción: Pete Koukov. Diseño de set y editor en set: Elaine Winter y Mari Siviakova. Retoque fotográfico: La machine. Producción local: Drita Curanaj (R3 Mgmt) y Wojtek Szaulinski. Sastre: Margarita Babina. Asistentes de fotografía: Christopher Morel y Keegan Eckart. Asistente de estilismo: Fern Cerezo y Jan Anthonio Diaz.

items.title: Dafne Fernández, actriz: “Nunca me ha gustado escuchar cosas positivas de mí, quizás porque siempre me han dicho las negativas”
items.description: Dafne Fernández (Madrid, 41 años) acapara las miradas desde un rincón. La actriz y bailarina ha entrado sigilosa en el Salón Carlos III del Teatro Real de Madrid , donde una veintena de periodistas e influencers esperan a que imparta un breve taller de danza clásica con motivo del 25º aniversario de la película Barbie en El Cascanueces (2001), del que es la embajadora en España. Ya en el centro de la sala, después de agradecer su nombramiento y de dar las primeras indicaciones, parece tan cercana que apetece seguirla. Plié, demi-plié, relevé; las presentes intentan imitar sus movimientos hasta que, de pronto, rompe la disciplina y se sienta en el suelo, animando al resto a hacer lo mismo mientras suena el emocionante Pas de Deux compuesto por Chaikovski para el ballet estrenado en 1892: “Así supe lo que era el síndrome de Stendhal. Es la música que me pongo cuando paso por un momento difícil y quiero escapar a otro lugar”, dice. Mientras, en el suelo, escucha con los ojos cerrados. Seguir leyendo

items.title: Cooperativas para comprar vivienda a precio de coste: ¿una fórmula olvidada para aliviar la crisis de acceso?
items.description: Solo 18 días después del final de la Guerra Civil, el 19 de abril de 1939, se creó el Instituto Nacional de la Vivienda para hacer frente a la grave escasez de casas y a la destrucción del parque residencial provocada por el conflicto. Entre las fórmulas utilizadas figuraba las cooperativas, que han permitido la construcción de más de 2,5 millones de viviendas desde 1957, alrededor del 10% del parque residencial español, según la Confederación de Cooperativas de Viviendas y Rehabilitación de España (Concovi). Seguir leyendo

items.title: Wendy Brown, politóloga: “Llevamos un tipo de vida insostenible y lo sabemos”
items.description: En esta época posterior a todo y anterior a nada, la politóloga Wendy Brown va a lo fundamental. Habla de la transcendencia de las próximas elecciones , de la espiral nihilista del neoliberalismo, del problemón de la lógica masculinista naturalizada, de las demandas que comparten los votantes de izquierda y derecha, y de los movimientos sociales que buscan salida a un mundo en combustión, víctima de un fuego alimentado por demagogos oportunistas. Seguir leyendo

items.title: ‘Palos de ciego’, una columna por dentro
items.description: El título genérico de la columna, ‘Palos de ciego’, se me apareció mientras daba vueltas a una frase de William Faulkner : “La literatura tiene el mismo impacto que una cerilla encendida en medio de un campo en medio de la noche; la cerilla ilumina relativamente poco, pero nos permite ver cuánta oscuridad nos rodea”. Esta columna siempre ha aspirado a entregarle al lector un pedazo de prosa decente, a entretenerle un rato, a hacerle un poco de compañía; en el mejor de los casos, a que ambos, lector y autor, podamos intuir a tientas algo de la oscuridad que nos rodea. No se me ocurre un propósito más ambicioso. Seguir leyendo El País Semanal 50 Aniversario Este artículo forma parte del especial aniversario de la revista que se publica en su edición impresa el domingo 25 de octubre.

items.title: Tenkodogo : Un crocodile capturé près d’un poulailler et relâché dans le barrage
items.description: Un crocodile qui rôdait près d’un poulailler dans une cour du quartier Gommisi, en face du Groupement de gendarmerie de Tenkodogo, a été capturé sans incident le jeudi 22 octobre 2026, puis relâché dans le barrage de la ville. L’alerte a été donnée par un habitant qui s’est présenté aux services compétents après avoir aperçu le reptile dans la concession. Aussitôt saisis, les agents du Service départemental des Eaux et Forêts (SDEF) de Tenkodogo, appuyés par la Brigade des Eaux et Forêts du Nakambé, se sont rendus sur les lieux. Selon la Direction régionale des Eaux et Forêts du Nakambé, l’animal a été maîtrisé dans le respect des mesures de sécurité, puis relâché dans le barrage de Tenkodogo. Aucun dégât n’a été constaté. L’intervention souligne l’importance de la vigilance citoyenne à proximité des points d’eau. Les Eaux et Forêts rappellent qu’il ne faut pas s’approcher ni tenter de capturer un animal sauvage, mais signaler immédiatement sa présence aux services compétents. items.title: SIAO 2026 : Plus de 800 000 visiteurs attendus, des innovations majeures annoncées
items.description: Le président du comité d’organisation de la 18ᵉ édition du Salon international de l’artisanat de Ouagadougou (SIAO), Alassane Ouédraogo, a annoncé vendredi lors d’une conférence de presse que plus de 800 000 visiteurs sont attendus à la biennale de l’artisanat, prévue du 30 octobre au 8 novembre 2026, avec notamment plusieurs innovations. Ouagadougou, 23 oct. 2026 (AIB)- Le président du comité d’organisation de la 18ᵉ édition du Salon international de l’artisanat de Ouagadougou (SIAO), Alassane Ouédraogo, a annoncé vendredi, lors d’une conférence de presse , que plus de 800 000 visiteurs et plus de 6 000 exposants sont attendus à la biennale de l’artisanat, prévue du 30 octobre au 8 novembre 2026, avec notamment plusieurs innovations. Le PCO Alassane Ouédraogo a soutenu qu’outre les visiteurs, les organisateurs prévoient la construction de 800 stands et l’accueil de plus de 6 000 exposants. La 18e édition compte réunir au moins 30 pays, plus d’une centaine d’acheteurs professionnels des cinq continents et mobiliser au moins 350 journalistes issus de 50 médias nationaux et internationaux. S’agissant des innovations de l’édition, l’organisation évoque la climatisation de tous les pavillons, l’augmentation du nombre de portes d’entrée et de sortie et la mise en place de « points i » pour orienter les visiteurs et centraliser les préoccupations des exposants. Un « Village du pays invité d’honneur » sera également créé, de même que des ateliers thématiques au Village artisanal de Ouagadougou (VAO) pour mieux faire connaître les métiers de l’artisanat, a-t-il affirmé. Le comité d’organisation a également annoncé des prix et distinctions dans plusieurs catégories, notamment le Grand Prix du Président du Faso, le prix du Président de l’Assemblée législative du peuple, le prix de la créativité Thomas Sankara, le prix du ministre chargé de l’Artisanat et celui de l’Organisation pour le développement et la promotion de l’artisanat africain (ODEPA). Placée sous le haut patronage du chef de l’État, le Capitaine Ibrahim Traoré, l’édition se déroulera sur le thème « Artisanat africain et industrialisation : quelle synergie pour une meilleure organisation et valorisation des produits locaux et du patrimoine culturel ». Pendant dix jours, le public pourra découvrir des expositions-ventes, le concours de la créativité au Pavillon Thomas Sankara, des rencontres d’affaires B to B, un séminaire sur le thème central, des compétitions entre artisans, la journée du pays invité d’honneur, des animations culturelles et artistiques, ainsi que la nuit des artisans méritants. Des activités sportives, dont une course cycliste le 24 octobre à 7 heures sur le boulevard des Tansoba et un cross populaire le 29 octobre, seront également au programme. Le président du CNO a lancé un appel à la mobilisation générale. Il a invité les artisans à présenter leurs meilleures créations et à conquérir de nouveaux marchés, exhorté les entreprises, les banques et les assurances à accompagner la manifestation, et sollicité l’appui des médias pour la promouvoir. Né de l’exposition-vente « Artisanat 84 », selon le camarade Ouédraogo, le SIAO a connu sa première édition du 20 au 27 février 1988 à la Maison du Peuple de Ouagadougou. Il s’est depuis imposé comme l’un des grands rendez-vous de l’artisanat africain. Le Ghana est annoncé comme pays invité d’honneur, tandis que le Mali et le Niger, membres de la Confédération de l’Alliance des États du Sahel (AES), seront les pays invités spéciaux. items.title: Boulgou/Garango : une exciseuse condamnée à 24 mois avec sursis pour avoir mutilé une fillette de 9 ans
items.description: Le Tribunal de grande instance (TGI) de Tenkodogo a condamné une exciseuse à vingt-quatre mois d’emprisonnement avec sursis et à une amende de cinq cent mille francs CFA, dont deux cents cinquante mille fermes. Elle avait pratiqué une mutilation génitale féminine (MGF) sur une fillette d’environ neuf ans à Garango, dans la province du Boulgou. Le jugement a été rendu lors des audiences foraines correctionnelles tenues du 13 au 15 octobre 2026 dans cette commune. Les faits remontent au mois d’août 2026. Selon les informations recueillies, la mère de la victime a conduit sa fille auprès de R. A., présentée comme exciseuse, pour lui faire subir une excision. À la suite de l’intervention, la fillette a présenté une importante hémorragie nécessitant une prise en charge médicale urgente. Elle a d’abord été admise au Centre médical avec antenne chirurgicale (CMA) de Garango, avant d’être évacuée au Centre hospitalier régional (CHR) de Tenkodogo, où elle a été hospitalisée pendant près d’une semaine avant de se rétablir. Trois femmes ont été mises en cause dans cette affaire. Considérée comme l’auteure principale, l’exciseuse a été jugée selon la procédure de flagrant délit et reconnue coupable de pratique de MGF. La mère de la victime et une autre femme, poursuivies pour complicité, ont bénéficié d’une procédure de composition pénale. Chacune s’est acquittée d’une amende de cinq cent mille francs CFA. Au-delà du traitement judiciaire, ces audiences foraines, tenues au pied du mont Boulgou, ont été l’occasion de rappeler aux populations les conséquences néfastes des MGF sur la santé et l’intégrité physique des filles. L’hémorragie survenue dans cette affaire, qui a nécessité l’évacuation de la fillette, illustre les risques liés à cette pratique prohibée par la loi. À travers cette audience délocalisée, le TGI de Tenkodogo a ainsi associé la sensibilisation à sa mission de répression des infractions. items.title: Bunkpurugu chieftaincy dispute: Chief Justice orders transfer of case to Tamale over security fears
items.description: The Chief Justice has granted a request by defendants in the Bunkpurugu chieftaincy dispute to transfer their case from the High Court in Nalerigu to Tamale over security concerns. One of the defendants, Elijah Saan, told JoyNews that they feared for their lives if they travelled to Nalerigu to attend court. He said the defendants had received intelligence suggesting they could be killed if they appeared in court in Nalerigu and had instructed their lawyer to apply for the transfer of the case to Tamale. The case was scheduled for hearing on Friday, October 23, 2026. The Registrar of the Nalerigu High Court confirmed to JoyNews on Friday that the Chief Justice had granted the request. The transfer comes amid heightened tensions in Bunkpurugu following the disputed enskinment of Melchizedek Musah Jamung as chief on September 14, 2026. The installation, which took place amid an ongoing chieftaincy dispute, reportedly triggered violence that left a woman dead and four others injured. Police have since been searching for the rival chief and other members of the Jamong royal family in connection with the disputed enskinment. The development has also prompted the Overlord of the Mamprugu Traditional Area, Naa Bohagu Abdulai Mahami Sheriga, to file an application at the High Court in Nalerigu seeking to have four people committed for contempt of court over the installation. In the application filed on October 14, 2026, the Nayiri accused the respondents of defying judicial processes by proceeding with the enskinment despite an ongoing legal dispute over the Bunkpurugu skin. The dispute between the Jamong and Jafouk royal families has contributed to persistent tensions in the area, with reports of farm destruction, arson and residents fleeing their homes amid fears of further violence.

items.title: Over 500 ‘illegal’ Afghans held in three provinces
items.description: ISLAMABAD: Undocumented Afghan nationals continue to be arrested by authorities, and a joint report of IOM and UNHCR says over the past one week, 517 Afghans were arrested from three districts of Balochistan, Sindh and Khyber-Pakhtunkhwa. Out of all arrests and detentions during October 11 to 17, ACC holders and undocumented Afghans from Chagai, Peshawar and Karachi represented 97 per cent of the total arrests and detentions, while Proof of Regis­tration (POR) holders represented 3 per cent. About 56pc of the total reported arrests and detentions took place in Balochistan, 34pc in Pun­jab and 10pc in Khyber-Pakhtunkhwa. The report says prior to 2023, there was no data collected on the arrest and detention of Afghan Citizen Card (ACC) holders or undocumented Afghan nationals. Since January 2023, IOM has started to collect the data. Findings of the report show cumulatively, from Sept 15, 2023 to Oct 17, 2026, about 2,744,068 Afghans have been sent back to their country from Pakistan. Between Oct 11 and 17, UNHCR and IOM estimate 3,883 Afghans returned through the Torkham, Chaman and Bahramcha border crossing points to Afghanistan. Between October 11 and 17, the nu­­mber of returns decreased by 10pc and deportations by 48pc — compared to the previous week of October 4 to 10, 2026 (4,295 returns including 961 deportations). Betw­een Oct 11 and 17, a total of 3,883 returns were reported, including 499 deportations. Compared to the previous week, dep­o­­rtations de­­c­­reased significantly, while returns de­­creased only moderately, report says. Among those who returned bet­we­en Oct 11 and 17, most were un­­documented (83pc) followed by ACC holders (9pc) and PoR holders (8pc). Majority of the PoR returns were processed by UNHCR through the Volu­n­tary Repatriation Centres (VRCs). Among those deported between Oct 11 and 17, most were undocumented (99pc) followed by PoR holders (1pc) and ACC holders (1pc). Since April 1, 2025, 1,890,035 Afghans returned, of which 237,387 (13pc) were deported. During the period, fear of arrest remained the main reason for return among undocumented individuals and ACC holders (95pc) as well as for PoR holders (68pc). Published in Dawn, October 24th, 2026

items.title: Tenkodogo : deux femmes accusées d’avoir traité d’autres personnes de sorcières devant le juge
items.description: Le tribunal de Tenkodogo a libéré deux femmes, A. Y. et B. B, faute de preuves. La justice leur reprochait d’avoir accusé d’autres personnes de sorcellerie. Dans cette affaire, c’est le procureur qui a demandé que les deux femmes soient libérées. Devant les juges, A. Y. a dit qu’elle n’avait rien fait. La personne qui se plaignait a même reconnu qu’A. Y. n’était pas là au moment des faits et qu’elle n’était pas responsable. Son nom avait été cité après une ancienne dispute, mais personne n’a pu dire ce qu’elle avait fait exactement. Le procureur a donc estimé qu’il n’y avait pas de faute et a demandé sa libération. Pour B. B., le tribunal a parlé d’un message audio. Dans ce message, une personne était accusée d’avoir rendu un enfant malade par la sorcellerie. Cette personne soupçonnait B. B., parce qu’elles avaient des problèmes entre elles et parce que des rumeurs circulaient. Mais elle n’avait aucune preuve. B. B. a affirmé qu’elle n’avait ni enregistré ni partagé ce message. La personne qui se plaignait a même dit qu’elle ne reconnaissait pas la voix entendue dans l’audio. Comme personne ne pouvait savoir qui avait enregistré le message, le procureur a demandé que B. B. soit libérée, au bénéfice du doute. Le procureur a tout de même averti sévèrement les deux femmes de ne plus jamais recommencer ce genre de choses. items.title: Bank Al-Maghrib : avis favorable du CEC sur dix textes
items.description: Obligations sécurisées, lutte contre le blanchiment, résilience numérique, accueil de la clientèle : réuni dans sa composition élargie, le Comité des établissements de crédit, présidé par le Wali de Bank Al-Maghrib, a donné son feu vert à dix textes qui viendront enrichir le cadre réglementaire du secteur bancaire du Royaume. Le cadre réglementaire du secteur bancaire du Royaume continue de s’étoffer. Institué par l’article 25 de la loi n° 103-12 relative aux établissements de crédit et organismes assimilés, le Comité des établissements de crédit (CEC), présidé par le Wali de Bank Al-Maghrib, a tenu sa réunion annuelle le 22 octobre 2026, au siège de la Banque centrale, à Rabat. Siégeant dans sa composition élargie, il a rendu un avis favorable sur dix textes qui régissent l’activité bancaire. Ceux-ci portent sur les obligations sécurisées, la lutte contre le blanchiment de capitaux, la résilience numérique et l’accueil de la clientèle. Le Comité s’est aussi prononcé en faveur d’un accord de coopération conclu avec la banque centrale ougandaise. Le CEC a notamment pour mission de donner son avis sur les textes réglementaires encadrant l’activité bancaire. Il réunit autour de son président un large éventail d’acteurs. On y retrouve un deuxième représentant de la Banque centrale et deux représentants du ministère chargé des Finances, parmi lesquels le Directeur du Trésor et des Finances Extérieures. Siègent également deux représentants de l’association professionnelle des banques, dont son président, ainsi que les présidents de l’association professionnelle des sociétés de financement, de l’association professionnelle des établissements de paiement et de la fédération nationale des associations de microcrédit. Sept circulaires pour les obligations sécurisées Le premier volet des textes approuvés concerne la loi n° 94-21 relative aux obligations sécurisées. Sept circulaires d’application ont reçu un avis favorable. Elles visent à parachever le cadre réglementaire pour permettre aux établissements émetteurs de rendre le dispositif opérationnel. Pour rappel, les obligations sécurisées ont pour objet de diversifier les sources de refinancement des établissements de crédit. Le Comité a également validé un amendement de la circulaire n° 5/W/2017 relative à l’obligation de vigilance. L’objectif est de mettre le dispositif de lutte contre le blanchiment de capitaux, le financement du terrorisme et le financement de la prolifération (LBC-FT-FP), applicable aux établissements de crédit et organismes assimilés, en conformité avec les évolutions récentes des standards du Groupe d’action financière (GAFI). Cyberrisques et accueil de la clientèle : deux directives Autre texte approuvé : une directive fixant les règles minimales de résilience opérationnelle numérique applicables aux établissements de crédit et organismes assimilés. Elle entend renforcer le dispositif de gestion des cyberrisques. Le contexte est celui d’une recrudescence des cyberattaques, accentuée par l’accélération de la transformation digitale. Une seconde directive porte sur les exigences minimales en matière d’accueil et de mesure de la satisfaction de la clientèle. Son ambition est d’asseoir une relation de confiance avec les usagers des services financiers. Selon Bank Al-Maghrib, l’adoption de ces textes contribuera à enrichir le corpus réglementaire applicable au secteur bancaire et à soutenir son rôle dans le financement de l’économie. Elle devrait aussi renforcer la qualité de la relation avec la clientèle et améliorer la gestion des risques, notamment en matière de LBC-FT-FP. Cette dernière dimension répond aux préoccupations du GAFI, en convergence avec les standards internationaux. Un accord de coopération avec l’Ouganda Au-delà des textes réglementaires, le Comité a émis un avis favorable sur la convention relative à la coopération en matière de contrôle bancaire, d’échange d’informations et de coopération générale entre Bank Al-Maghrib et la Banque centrale de l’Ouganda. The post Bank Al-Maghrib : avis favorable du CEC sur dix textes appeared first on Hespress Français - Actualités du Maroc .

items.title: Ghana needs 759 million cedis to implement 2025-29 health sector supply chain master plan
items.description: More than 759 million cedis — that is how much Ghana needs to fix critical gaps in the supply of medicines and essential medical supplies across the country’s health facilities over the next four years. But with some foreign aid to the health sector being withdrawn, the government is turning to domestic resources to fund the plan and keep Ghana’s universal health coverage target for 2030 within reach. At the launch of the 2025-2029 health sector supply chain master plan, stakeholder say effective funding, improved financial management and the recovery of outstanding debts owed under the National Health Insurance Scheme will be crucial to ensuring that health facilities, particularly those serving women and children, have the essential commodities they need to save lives. The master plan is a revised version of the 2021 – 2025 plan which was partially implemented due to the COVID-19 outbreaks with 35% of the overall targets achieved. The old plan revealed significant gaps in the planning, governance, workforce and operation sectors for the effective rollout of health The new plan is aimed at ensuring the completion of critical tasks while enhancing supply chain adaptability and responsiveness to emerging challenged. The master plan encompasses forty-seven (47) strategic interventions, each linked to the annual performance targets across the second (II) technical areas. The plan seeks to ensure availability, timely-access, affordability of high-quality health commodities across public and private sectors to successfully deliver universal health coverage ensuring Ghanaians have access to high-quality health care services. Targets by 2029 The masterplan seeks to build an integrated central and regional medical stores distribution on time and in full for all service delivery points while tracking cost components. It will also develop a well-coordinated financial system that supports the public health system. The implementation of the masterplan will include a mapping exercise to understand the flow of money and tracking of expenditures at each level. Speaking at the launch of the masterplan in Kumasi, Director for Procurement and Supply Chain at the Ministry of Health, Dr. Edward Bright Agyekum, noted that the government remains focused on generating revenue locally for the masterplan’s implementation. This comes amidst withdrawal of some foreign aid to the health sector, but Dr. Agyekum says strategies are in place to mobilize resources locally to achieve key priorities set out under the plan. “The supply chain master plan will be implemented with local funds. We are using whatever we have to generate. Whatever we are going to do to ensure it’s a local funding, we are mobilizing the scarce resources, the government is pushing for it. We are doing, we are mindful that come what may, the donors will withdraw. We are raising local funding to support implementation,” he said. Owning the SCMP implementation Technical Director with the Global Health Supply Chain, Daniel Oswald Owusu Afranie says the country make be deliberate in owning the masterplan for a universal health coverage by 2030. “The development partners have supported in putting this together. But its implementation is something government must take over and plan towards that. Resource mobilizing is very key,” he said. He noted that the government must devise ways to recoup all debts incurred under the health insurance scheme to complement revenue mobilization for the implementation. He acknowledged that these huge arrears affect the operations of the medical supply stores in procuring and distributing health commodities to health facilities. “How does the NHIS come in. Because in terms of health financing which the NHIA is already doing. We have to look at what role they will be playing in the implementation of the supply chain masterplan. There must be practical measures to ensure those debts are collected so that the regional medical stores will be able to function as business entities,” he added. Focus on Women and Children Women and children are among the most vulnerable groups in Ghana’s healthcare system, with access to essential medicines, vaccines and other medical supplies playing a critical role in their survival and well-being. Supply and Procurement Manager at UNICEF, Honorine Niyomana, stressed that the plan must deliberately and strategically focus on women and children. Ms. Niyomana says inadequate supplies could hinder mother and children from accessing equitable care. “Ghana has made important progress in improving health for women and children. But progress can be lost quickly when the commodities run out. A stock out of a single essential medicine can send a mother or caregiver home without care or force a family to travel far or pay off out of pocket,” she said.

items.title: Jordan church shooting claims 7 lives
items.description: AMMAN: Gunmen killed at least seven people and wounded dozens at a church in southern Jordan on Friday, authorities said, with the king vowing retaliation for the rare attack on Christians in the majority Muslim kingdom. Assailants stormed the compound of a Greek Orthodox church in the village of Hammoud in Karak governorate and opened fire, authorities said. The gunmen got out of a vehicle and started shooting during a funeral procession, the public security directorate said in a statement, adding that a manhunt was underway for the perpetrators. “The terrorist attack against Karak will be met with the harshest retaliation,” King Abdullah II said in a post on X. “We will strike with an iron fist against those who dare to threaten our nation.” According to images from state broadcaster Al-Mamlaka, the king arrived in Karak on Friday evening. After authorities gave a death toll of six, Director of Public Security Major General Abdullah Al-Maaytah said it had risen to seven with 34 injured, 27 of whom were still receiving treatment. Footage aired by Al-Mamlaka showed two gunmen dressed in casual clothes and brandishing pistols, with a third carrying a long gun as they opened fire on the church. A witness said the gunmen fired continuously for five minutes before fleeing. Between 150 and 200 people were in and around the church at the time, the witness said. Published in Dawn, October 24th, 2026

items.title: White House lifts tariffs on some Canadian goods as midterm elections loom
items.description: The Trump administration is lifting some of its 50% tariffs on Canadian goods two weeks before the midterm elections, after a Republican candidate in a key Senate race said she had lobbied for the change. Starting on 30 October, tariffs will be eased on products including “plywood sheets, some paper products, certain machinery and refrigeration equipment,” the White House said on Friday. Republican Senator Susan Collins, who is in a tight race to keep her seat in Maine, first announced the exemptions, saying they would help her state’s agriculture industry. The US imposed a 50% levy on $20bn (£15bn) of Canadian goods after trade talks between the two countries collapsed in August. Maine Senator Susan Collins is seeking to keep her seat in November’s midterm elections Canada has imposed a series of countermeasures against US tariffs, which Prime Minister Mark Carney said were “necessary to protect our workers”. Last month, Carney matched the US tariffs “dollar for dollar” after the breakdown in talks. Trump had imposed them for what he called “unequal treatment” of US cars, dairy and alcohol. The White House said while tariffs would be lifted from some items, including some packing crates and boxes, they would be introduced on other items such as carpets and “waste products”. It said the action reflected President Trump’s “continued efforts to defend American workers and ensure fair trade”. “President Trump continues to address Canada’s discriminatory treatment of US commerce,” White House spokesman Matthew Middleton said. In a statement to the BBC, Canada’s internal trade minister Dominic LeBlanc said: “While we assess these latest steps, Canada stands ready to work constructively and in good faith towards a more mutually beneficial trading relationship that respects Canada’s interests.” The White House’s announcement comes less than a fortnight before the US midterm elections, which will determine whether Trump’s Republican Party or Democrats will control Congress, impacting the remaining two years of his term. Collins said she had repeatedly asked senior Trump officials for tariff relief and that she would “continue working directly with administration officials to seek additional relief and encourage a broader trade agreement with Canada, our neighbour, ally, and largest trading partner”. She wrote on X that the tariff exemptions were on products that were “crucial to Maine’s agricultural industries, including blueberry, potato, apple, and seaweed producers”. Collins’ Democratic challenger, Troy Jackson, responded: “Trump’s trade wars have made life harder and more expensive for Mainers. Susan Collins enabled this chaos, voted to confirm the people behind it, and now wants credit for bringing a cup of water to put out the fire.” Maine borders the Canadian provinces New Brunswick and Quebec. Its economy, as well as that of other border states, is deeply linked to Canada and they have felt the effects of the months-long trade war. Michigan lawmaker Mike Rogers, also a Republican, has called on Trump to end the standoff after spending months supporting the policy in recent advertisements airing in his trade-reliant state. Also on Friday, President Donald Trump said Canada was “working very hard” on a ⁠trade ​deal with the US. Carney, for his part, said that Canada was open to a mutually beneficial deal, but is willing to wait it out. “We could sign it this afternoon if the US were there. If it has to be months from now or longer than that, or another administration, before a proper deal comes into place, we will do that,” he said on Friday, according to Canadian broadcaster CBC. LeBlanc confirmed on Thursday that a delegation met with members of the Canada-United States Economic Relations Advisory Committee – the ninth meeting since April 2026. The committee members discussed the ongoing impact of US tariffs in Canada.

items.title: Burkina : la coupe du Faso s’ouvre désormais à 11 disciplines
items.description: Longtemps concentrée sur le football, la Coupe du Faso s’est maintenant ouverte à 11 autres disciplines dont les finales se disputeront les 24 et 25 octobre, a annoncé vendredi à Ouagadougou, la Directrice générale des sports et des loisirs Valérie Badolo/Tapsoba au cours d’une conférence de presse. La Directrice générale des sports et des loisirs Valérie Badolo/Tapsoba a donné les détails des modalités d’organisation de ces compétitions, soulignant que cette initiative du ministère des Sports, de la Jeunesse et de l’Emploi marque une nouvelle étape dans la valorisation des disciplines longtemps restées dans l’ombre du football. Pour cette première édition, onze disciplines sont concernées : l’athlétisme, les sports pour personnes handicapées, le volleyball, le handball, le rugby, la lutte, la boxe, la pétanque, le karaté-do, le taekwondo et le cyclisme. À travers ces compétitions, les autorités entendent diversifier l’offre sportive, améliorer la préparation des athlètes et favoriser la détection de nouveaux talents. L’initiative vise également à accroître la visibilité des disciplines concernées, à promouvoir l’équité sportive et à renforcer la cohésion sociale. Selon la directrice générale, cette première phase dont le budget est de 100 millions, pourrait être étendue à d’autres disciplines, en fonction des résultats obtenus, des ressources disponibles et de la capacité des fédérations à répondre aux exigences organisationnelles. Elle a insisté sur la nécessité d’une mobilisation coordonnée des fédérations sportives, des encadreurs, des athlètes et des partenaires pour garantir le bon déroulement des finales. Le respect des règlements, la discipline et le fair-play devront, selon elle, guider les compétitions. Mme Badolo/Tapsoba a, par ailleurs, invité les médias à assurer une couverture professionnelle et responsable de l’événement, afin de mieux faire connaître ces disciplines et de valoriser les performances des sportifs auprès du public. Inscrite dans la dynamique de promotion de la jeunesse et de valorisation des potentialités nationales, cette initiative ambitionne de faire du sport un vecteur de cohésion, de solidarité et de patriotisme. La directrice générale a souhaité que cette première édition ouvre la voie à une dynamique durable au bénéfice de l’ensemble du mouvement sportif burkinabè. items.title: KP governor rules out talks with ‘anti-state elements’
items.description: • Kundi calls for decisive action against terrorists, stronger police capacity • Says Centre ready to provide weapons, financial resources to KP police • Insists peace essential for development, investment in province CHARSADDA / PESHAWAR: Khyber Pakhtunkhwa Governor Faisal Karim Kundi on Friday ruled out negotiations or concessions for elements who do not accept the Constitution, stressing that decisive action against terrorism and strengthening the province’s police was the only way to restoring peace. Speaking to journalists after visiting the families of CTD DSP Imranuddin Khan and Constable Kazim Jan in Charsadda, Mr Kundi said elements working against the state should not be offered concessions. He said the Pakistan Army, police and other security agencies had rendered immense sacrifices for the country’s security and stressed that Khyber Pakhtunkhwa must be freed from terrorism. Referring to a recent meeting of the National Apex Committee , the governor said Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif had made it clear that a policy of zero tolerance would be adopted against terrorism. He said decisive action against terrorists was necessary to restore lasting peace, adding that the public should distance itself from terrorists and refrain from providing them shelter. Mr Kundi said police and other law enforcement agencies required modern weapons and equipment to confront terrorists and that he was prepared to divert funds from his development allocation for the purpose. He added that Interior Minister Mohsin Naqvi had assured him that the federal government was ready to provide the police with the required weapons and financial resources. Mr Kundi said the compensation package for police personnel martyred in the line of duty had been enhanced and that police salaries were also being increased. Asked about the non-functional chief minister Sohail Afridi, Mr Kundi said Mr Afridi was in safe hands, adding that nobody could predict what would happen in the future. The governor’s adviser on information, Samar Haroon Bilour, said the police and Counter-Terrorism Department needed modern weapons, secure vehicles, tracking systems and protective equipment to improve their operational capacity. She said sustained federal support was necessary to strengthen both institutions. Earlier in the day, DSP Imranuddin and Constable Jan, who were martyred during an operation against terrorists in Karak district on Thursday, were laid to rest in their native villages in Charsadda with police honours. Mr Kundi claimed that weapons left behind following the withdrawal of international forces from Afghanistan had fallen into the hands of terrorists. He said Pakistan’s long border with Afghanistan made surveillance difficult in some areas and that terrorists possessed sophisticated weapons. Federal package Separately, addressing a news conference at Governor House in Peshawar, Mr Kundi said demands presented by the provincial advisory council at the Apex Committee meeting on Thursday had been accepted by PM Shehbaz. “Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif announced a package of Rs160 billion for the province. To resolve issues related to gas and wheat, the prime minister directed the secretary of food department to convene a meeting soon,” he said. According to the governor, the meeting, attended by the prime minister and senior military leadership, focused on security, development and public concerns in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa. Mr Kundi said peace was essential for development and investment in the province. “If there is peace in the province, there will be development and investment will also come from abroad,” he said. He added that the provincial advisory council would pursue KP’s rights on the basis of facts and said talks had also been held with representatives of the Awami National Party, Jamaat-i-Islami and Qaumi Watan Party chief Aftab Ahmad Khan Sherpao. Mr Kundi said political parties needed to unite over the province’s rights. He also raised the issue of KP’s water share, insisting that the province was not receiving its due allocation under the 1991 water accord. He said the federal government had heard the province’s position and tenders for packages one and four of the Chashma Lift Canal would be issued next month. Ms Bilour said development priorities discussed with the federal government included road connectivity, educational institutions, information technology hubs and vocational training facilities. She said improving security and providing young people with better educational and employment opportunities were both necessary for the province’s long-term development. Mr Kundi said restoring peace, strengthening the police and securing the province’s constitutional and development rights were essential for KP’s future. Published in Dawn, October 24th, 2026

items.title: WB urges Pakistan to shift from stability to growth
items.description: WORLD Bank official Sandeep Mahajan meets Finance Minister Muhammad Aurangzeb.—X/ @Financegovpk • Calls for stronger investment, private sector activity • Aurangzeb stresses need to strengthen investor confidence ISLAMABAD: In what appears to be a push towards accelerating growth, the World Bank has advised Pakistan to move from stabilisation to sustainable growth, with a focus on strengthening investment and private sector activity. This marks the second such endorsement from the international financial institution, which recently commended Pakistan’s stabilisation programme and urged a shift towards sustainable growth to generate employment opportunities for the youth. The IMF has also offered similar advice to Islamabad at a recent workshop on tax reforms. World Bank Regional Practice Director for the Prosperity Vertical for the Middle East, North Africa, Afghanistan and Pakistan (MENAAP) Sandeep Mahajan met Finance Minister Muhammad Aurangzeb on Friday. He was accompanied by Country Director Bolor­maa Amgaabazar and International Finance Corporation (IFC) Division Director Simon Andrews. An official statement said the meeting discussed Pakistan’s economic reform agenda, the transition from stabilisation to sustainable growth and priorities for strengthening inve­stment and private sector activity. Mr Mahajan congratulated Pakis­tan on restoring macroeconomic stability and commended the government’s management of the recent crisis arising from regional conflict. He noted that buffers built through stabilisation efforts and a timely policy response had helped Pakistan manage external pressures. World Bank representatives emphasised the importance of sustaining these gains through continued reforms and effective implementation. Mr Aurangzeb said the government’s priority was to make macroeconomic stability durable and translate it into sustainable, investment-led and export-driven growth. He said that Pakistan had regained access to international capital markets, including through its recent $3 billion Eurobond issuance with five-year and 10-year maturities. The minister also stressed the need to secure further credit rating upgrades, strengthen investor confidence and improve Pakistan’s sovereign credit profile. Mr Aurangzeb underscored the importance of a credible transition framework that maintained fiscal discipline, addressed external sector vulnerabilities and strengthened the foundations for private sector-led, responsible and sustainable growth. The discussion also covered international experience in strengthening fiscal frameworks and policy credibility to manage external risks and support investor confidence. Policy continuity was highlighted as another key requirement for sustained economic progress. The finance minister noted that investment and productivity depended on a predictable policy environment and consistent implementation. Mr Aurangzeb and the World Bank representatives also exchanged views on the government’s growth and jobs agenda, including opportunities to strengthen private sector investment, improve the regulatory environment and mobilise financing for infrastructure. The discussion covered privatisation, the importance of clear regulatory frameworks and credible post-privatisation arran­gements, as well as the potential to develop infrastructure projects through appropriate financing structures and collaboration with development partners. Both sides reaffirmed the importance of continued cooperation between Pakistan and the World Bank, with a focus on sustaining macroeconomic stability, advancing structural reforms, strengthening policy continuity and translating reform gains into investment, employment and improved economic opportunities. Published in Dawn, October 24th, 2026

items.title: Carrick refuses to rule out dropping Fernandes in emotional address
items.description: Under-pressure Manchester United boss Michael Carrick delivered a passionate and emotional address lasting five minutes and 30 seconds as he battles to save his job. And he refused to rule out dropping skipper Bruno Fernandes for Sunday’s Premier League meeting with Bournemouth at Old Trafford. Instead of taking his seat and answering questions as normal in Friday’s scheduled pre-match media conference at Carrington, Carrick said he wanted to start himself. It was a strategy former boss Sir Alex Ferguson used, although the legendary Scot rarely spoke at such length. After a run of seven games without a win, culminating in Wednesday’s shocking 4-1 Champions League defeat by Como, and attacks on the club’s hierarchy by defender Lisandro Martinez and then Fernandes’ condemnation of his own tactics in Italy, Carrick wanted to reaffirm his view of what United stood for. “Recently we haven’t had a good time, I think that’s pretty obvious,” he said. “Wednesday was a bad night, and it hurt me to see us play like that. It was unacceptable. “My responsibility is to get a team on the pitch that represents this football club, and the supporters, and they can be proud of in the identity we show. We have gone away from that recently. It’s important we all recognise that. “The foundation and values of this football club have been etched for many years. I totally understand and get every single one of them. “There’s a resilience about this football club that runs very deep. I’ve seen it with my own eyes, I’ve felt it, I’m know some of the individuals closely who have been a big part of that history. “Entitlement cannot be at this football club. “It was based on being humble, having humility, and hard work. We can never lose that, and I won’t let us lose that.” Asked about Fernandes and whether he has considered dropping him, a defiant Carrick added: “The most important thing for me is the team, the squad and dynamics in the squad. “It’s about the football club. I’ll always do what is best for the football club.” No guarantees for Fernandes Image caption,Manchester United won 12 of their 17 games under Michael Carrick last season Club sources said on Thursday Fernandes would not have the captaincy taken away or be fined for his post-match observations following the Como defeat. In a further interview on Wednesday night with Sky Italia, the Portugal international referred to Manchester United’s storied history. “At this club, there’s too much focus on what’s been done in the past,” said Fernandes. “But we’re not those people anymore. The club and the players need to understand that. “Unfortunately for us – especially when it comes to the players – those who join expect to win trophies, win games, and reach the highest level, that’s been very difficult at this club in recent years.” Whether Carrick was aware of Fernandes’ comments about United’s history before he spoke was uncertain. When asked again if he would take the captaincy away from the 32-year-old midfielder, Carrick repeated: “I will always do what is best for the football club.” He then refused to say whether he had spoken to Fernandes about his conduct, adding: “I don’t think this is the time to go into too much detail.” Despite the challenge to his authority, Carrick said the United dressing room was not divided. “No, it’s not,” he added. “We just need to get back to doing what we do best.” Carrick also said the club were ‘doing everything’ to support Fernandes and his family, whose Cheshire home was burgled on Wednesday. “Thankfully they weren’t directly affected even though it is an awful situation.” ‘Hurt’ fuels motivation and inspiration Carrick named legendary United figures such as Ryan Giggs, Wayne Rooney and Ferguson as examples of the humility, sacrifice and hard work expected of United players. That was at odds with his post-match criticism on Wednesday, when he said if you don’t run forward or back properly, you will not win games. Asked how he would persuade his current squad to adhere to the values expected and he demanded, Carrick added: “It’s clear as day. “I’m not telling you anything new. I haven’t invented that. That’s the make-up of any good football team. You have to earn the right to be better than your opponent. That never changes. “What we look like as a group is my responsibility. That’s the privileged position I am in. I’ll hold that umbrella for me to get wet and everyone else to stay dry. “[Wednesday] hurts an awful lot, but that doesn’t stop me. That hurt is used as pure motivation and inspiration to want more, expect more and get us going in a different direction.”

items.title: Fuel dealers urge consumers to avoid ‘panic buying’
items.description: • PPDA chairman says pricing remains an issue • JI demands meeting with PM ‘this week’ to resolve levy issue ISLAMABAD: Even as talks between the Jamaat-i-Islami (JI) and the government to reduce the fuel levy remained ‘inconclusive’, petroleum dealers on Friday urged consumers not to resort to panic buying, as excessive purchases could create market distortions. Talking to reporters, Pakistan Petroleum Dealers Association (PPDA) Chairman Malik Khuda Baksh said the delicate balance between supply and demand had been maintained efficiently by all stakeholders, including the government, industry and consumers. At the same time, he said the recent closure of the Iran border had put the liquefied petroleum gas (LPG) market under stress. “As far as petrol supply is concerned, there is a huge responsibility on consumers too, especially petrol consumers. We have seen in the past that when cars and motorcycles line up at petrol pumps, it creates artificial shortages in some areas,” the PPDA chairman said. He said reports were circulating that the country could run dry in the coming days and recalled the situation during the US invasion of Afghanistan in October 2001. “There were such reports and a brief panic in those days too, but petrol and diesel remained available in the country. Similarly, the situation remains under control now as well,” he added. Mr Baksh said refineries were operational, while both crude oil and petroleum products were being imported from Gulf countries, including Saudi Arabia and Oman. “Price remains an issue, but that is a different matter,” he said. According to oil industry estimates, diesel demand during November 2026 is likely to be around 750,000 tonnes, driven by seasonal agricultural requirements. Industry sources said local refineries supplied approximately 70 per cent of the country’s diesel requirements, although the bulk of the crude oil processed by them was imported. Petrol demand for November is estimated at around 630,000 tonnes, while local production accounts for roughly 30pc of national consumption. Petroleum industry sources added that high prices and the off-peak travel season were likely to keep consumption subdued next month. Jamaat-govt talks Meanwhile, the JI called on Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif to announce additional relief for the public in his proposed meeting with Hafiz Naeem, and asked that the meeting be held ‘this week’. Speaking to reporters after holding talks with a government delegation led by Planning Minister Ahsan Iqbal, JI Deputy Emir Liaqat Baloch told reporters that while the party would continue to pursue negotiations, it would not abandon the path of protest. As talks continue a technical committee comprising State Minister for Finance Bilal Azhar Kayani, JI Islamabad Emir Nasrullah Randhawa and Deputy Secretary Syed Farasat Shah has been constituted and the committee would meet within two to three days to examine the outstanding issues. Published in Dawn, October 24th, 2026

items.title: Woman, 65, becomes second patient to die of Ebola in Kenya
items.description: Kenya has recorded its second death from Ebola as it handles its first ever outbreak of the disease. A woman, aged 65, who was a close family member of the first victim, a man who had travelled from the Democratic Republic of Congo, died after being placed in quarantine, the health ministry said. Seven other Ebola patients were receiving treatment at two isolation facilities, it added. All the cases were within “one cluster, with no evidence of community spread”, the ministry said. More than 4,000 people have died in Africa since Ebola was confirmed in DR Congo in May, making it the second most deadly outbreak of the disease. Kenya’s latest victim was a “direct contact and close family member of the first case (deceased) and was under quarantine when she developed symptoms” on 13 October, the health ministry said. The first death, on 5 October, was that of a man who fell ill in September and was treated in several hospitals in DR Congo before arriving in the Kenyan capital, Nairobi, where he died a few days later. Those still being treated are three other relatives of the first victim, three health workers and a hospital cleaner. The US has warned its citizens against travelling to Kenya, while neighbouring countries such as Uganda, Ethiopia and Somalia are also on alert. Ebola is a rare but deadly disease caused by a virus. As the disease progresses, vomiting and diarrhoea develop and it can lead to organ failure. Some, but not all, patients develop internal and external bleeding. The disease spreads from one person to another by contact with infected bodily fluids such as blood or vomit. The Bundibugyo species of Ebola is relatively rare, with no approved vaccine or treatment – though trials are under way. With more than 9,500 cases in DR Congo, Kenya faces a steady risk of new cases arriving across borders, according to the International Rescue Committee, which has been working alongside both governments to contain the spread. Kenya has introduced enhanced screening for travellers arriving from DR Congo and nine other countries it considers to be at high risk: Uganda, Tanzania, Rwanda, Burundi, Angola, Zambia, Ethiopia, South Sudan and the Central African Republic. Travellers arriving from those countries are required to complete a digital surveillance form before boarding their flights, and to present a QR code to port health officials on arrival. Kenya also ordered enhanced public health screening of aircraft arriving from those countries, as authorities seek to prevent further imported cases. Within the country, the government has been sharing public messages to create awareness about Ebola, including encouraging people to promptly report any suspected cases and seek care at a hospital. It has also focused on hygiene and safety measures, such as washing hands and avoiding close contact with sick people.In another development, Nigeria’s health minister has said the country’s single confirmed case of Ebola appears to be genetically related to a strain identified earlier in Kenya. Professor Ali Pate said there was no evidence so far that the Kenyan patient had travelled to Nigeria, but that further testing was under way. He emphasised that Nigeria had so far recorded only one confirmed case of the virus. “We are conducting additional tests. Some of the results are negative, while others are pending,” Pate said. Health officials have been investigating whether Nigeria’s first case crossed paths with Kenya’s first patient. Both are believed to have travelled through Uganda’s Entebbe International Airport earlier this month.

items.title: ECP proposes AI rules for parties, media, election observers
items.description: ISLAMABAD: The Election Commission of Pakistan (ECP) has proposed amendments to the codes of conduct for political parties and contesting candidates, media and election observers to protect the electoral process from the harmful effects of artificial intelligence (AI). The commission has shared the draft amendments with stakeholders and sought their feedback by Nov 20. According to a draft notification issued on Friday, the ECP cited its constitutional duty under Article 218(3) to ensure honest, just and fair elections. “Therefore, it is the core responsibility of the commission to take all necessary steps to guard against corrupt practices, which also include manipulation of the electoral process through misleading content generated using AI,” the notification said. Draft bars digitally manipulated ‘defamatory content’; feedback sought by Nov 20 Under the proposed rules, political parties and contesting candidates would be required to clearly disclose all AI-generated campaign material, including deepfake images, audio, video and synthetic voices. Robocalls and voter outreach messages using cloned voices would have to disclose their AI-generated nature at the outset. The draft prohibits AI-generated content intended to deceive voters or misrepresent individuals. It also bans false, derogatory or defamatory deepfake statements targeting candidates, party leaders, supporters, election officials, the judiciary, state functionaries or the armed forces. Political parties would be barred from using automated bots or acco­unts to artificially inflate likes, comments, shares or followers to create a false impression of public support. They would also be required to retain logs of all AI-assisted campaign content and submit them to the ECP upon request. Print, electronic and digital media outlets, as well as social media influencers, would be required to explicitly label AI-altered election content. Media houses would remain legally responsible for the factual accuracy of content produced using AI tools for translation, anchoring or analysis. The Pakistan Electronic Media Regulatory Authority, the Social Media Protection and Regulatory Authority and the National Cyber Crime Investigation Agency will actively monitor online platforms. They will submit compliance reports to the ECP, which retains the authority to order immediate content takedowns or re-labelling. Election observers would be required to identify and promptly report AI-generated deepfakes and disinformation campaigns directly to the ECP without further spreading the misleading material. They would also be prohibited from using AI to fabricate or embellish election photographs, videos, reports or field observations. Published in Dawn, October 24th, 2026

items.title: Kompany taken to hospital after collapsing at training
items.description: Bayern Munich manager Vincent Kompany was taken to hospital after collapsing as he watched the club’s second team train on Friday. The 40-year-old had been unwell with a virus and missed the pre-match news conference on Tuesday prior to Bayern’s Champions League game against Arsenal. The former Manchester City and Belgium defender was subsequently on the touchline for the match on Wednesday. Reports in Germany say Kompany is in a stable condition in hospital. “Vincent Kompany required medical attention after collapsing during an FC Bayern reserve team training session on Friday,” said a statement from the Bundesliga club., external “The first-team head coach was watching the second string’s session. “Kompany is undergoing thorough examinations in hospital and will remain under medical care. “His coaching staff will oversee training and match activities until further notice.” Bayern’s next game is against Freiburg in the German top flight on Sunday. “Vincent Kompany’s health is our top priority. We at FC Bayern will do everything we can to ensure his speedy recovery,” said Bayern sporting director Max Eberl. “Vinnie is receiving all the necessary medical care and support, and all the time he needs. “His coaching team, in whom we have complete confidence, will take over his duties. All of us at FC Bayern wish Vinnie a speedy recovery.” Aaron Danks, one of Kompany’s assistants, took the pre-match news conference for Bayern before the Arsenal game. German football journalist Taufig Khalil told BBC Radio 5 Live that Kompany had been “suffering with the virus for about a week”. He added: “The thing started last weekend on Saturday against Leipzig, and that’s the first time we saw Vincent Kompany [when] he didn’t look very well. “He didn’t do the press conference after, and Max Eberl told us that he’s suffering with a virus. “Everybody was really surprised that Vincent Kompany was standing there with his black jacket in the pouring rain of Munich on Wednesday night against Arsenal. Everybody expected Aaron Danks to be there. “The problem was that maybe you couldn’t bench Vincent Kompany, the game was too important for him. “Bayern Munich just told us that he’s in stable conditions. There was a helicopter involved in the whole thing, which landed on the training ground at Bayern Munich, but he was not brought into the hospital by helicopter. They brought him with a medical car and he will be now there.” ‘Get well soon, Vinny’ Kompany left his role as Burnley manager to take over at Bayern in May 2024, succeeding current England manager Thomas Tuchel. He had won the Championship with Burnley in 2022-23 and, despite the Clarets being relegated from the Premier League under him the following season, Kompany was appointed by the Bundesliga club. He has led Bayern to the German top-flight title in the past two seasons and reached the 2025-26 Champions League semi-finals before being beaten by eventual winners Paris St-Germain. Kompany spent 11 years at Manchester City as a player, winning four Premier League titles, two FA Cups and four League Cups. “Everyone at Manchester City is wishing a speedy recovery to our former captain and club legend, Vincent Kompany,” said City in a post on social media. “Get well soon, Vinny.” “Everyone here at Burnley FC sends our best wishes to Vincent and we wish him a speedy recovery,” said a Burnley statement.

items.title: A Very Suspicious Indictment of Two Former FBI Officials
items.description: Not too long ago, the Department of Justice could generally be trusted to prosecute cases in which lawyers believed that real wrongdoing had occurred. Now DOJ frequently unveils lawsuits that seem designed mostly for securing likes and reposts on right-wing social media—the actual facts be damned. Any high-profile criminal case brought by the Trump administration arrives with an air of suspicion. Today, Jeanine Pirro, the top federal prosecutor for Washington, D.C., announced an odd set of charges against two former FBI officials for allegedly lying to Congress during testimony in 2023. “When senior FBI agents lie to Congress believing they are above the law, it’s time to bring the hammer of justice down on them,” Pirro posted on X. For all of the fanfare, DOJ provided little evidence to back up its claims. But the timing of the charges—they’ve arrived just more than a week before the midterm elections—and with the puzzling substance of the allegations and the administration’s crowing online, does not inspire confidence in the integrity of the prosecutorial work. The charges concern several statements made by the defendants, Nikki Floris and Bradley Benavides, in the course of a congressional investigation into supposed “weaponization” of the government against President Trump. In brief, the Justice Department is alleging that Floris and Benavides lied to the House Judiciary Committee regarding their level of knowledge about the FBI’s handling of Hunter Biden’s laptop. Lawyers for Floris issued a statement saying that DOJ “has accused her falsely of a crime on the say-so of politicians, not on the facts.” Benavides’s lawyer likewise described the charges as “baseless.” The saga of the Hunter Biden laptop has now spanned four federal elections, and the specifics of the story may, reasonably, no longer be top of mind. Understanding its relevance here requires a deep plunge into far-right mythology. But the quick version is that MAGA became obsessed with the possibly stolen laptop, and the material it contained documenting Biden’s drug addiction, after the New York Post published an article about the laptop in the lead-up to the 2020 election. Social-media companies, burned by their experience of Russian election interference in 2016, worried that the underlying documents might be Russian misinformation. (This suspicion was never confirmed.) They responded aggressively by suppressing links to the Post ’s story—which outraged the right. The laptop would go on to play a starring role in the coming years as the GOP used congressional investigations to tell a story about the victimization of the right, supposedly having been a target of a sprawling network of government-backed online censorship and unfair treatment by the FBI. This was the context in which Floris and Benavides were testifying in 2023. The two had held leadership positions in the FBI’s Foreign Influence Task Force (FITF) during 2020, a section created to respond to foreign interference after Russia’s 2016 election meddling. There they had crossed paths with the laptop. In recent years, congressional Republicans have pointed to various decontextualized snippets of that testimony and internal FBI documents as part of their efforts to suggest that the FBI was working against Trump in the 2020 election. By then, for a certain kind of very online Trump supporter, Floris and Benavides had already become familiar if relatively minor villains in the anticanon of deep-state enemies. The criminal charges today make sense in this larger narrative. In his X post announcing the charges, FBI Director Kash Patel referred to the agency’s past “political weaponization targeting their opponents.” Just because MAGA hates someone does not mean that they are innocent. But Floris and Benavides’s work as described in the affidavit seems unremarkable. And the document is opaque when describing what the two defendants are actually alleged to have lied about. To be prosecutable under the relevant statute, a lie to government authorities must be told “knowingly and willfully,” and it must be “material” in a way that substantively affects the investigation in question. Some of Floris’s and Benavides’s alleged misstatements, as described in the affidavit, don’t initially appear to be misstatements at all. For example, Floris said she was not involved in the criminal investigation into Hunter Biden during which the FBI seized the laptop; in fact, her work at the FITF really was separate from the criminal probe, which was carried out by a different team. Other supposed lies might well be better understood as forgetfulness. The two defendants were high up in the bureau and wouldn’t necessarily recall the minutiae of an incident that took place three years before they testified. In one instance, the affidavit alleges that Floris lied about her involvement in “an assessment to discredit the Hunter Biden investigations,” but contains no further mention of this supposed assessment nor any quotes from the relevant testimony. Perhaps DOJ will be able to provide more evidence for its allegations as the case goes on, but as things now stand, the charges appear less than airtight. How the Justice Department chose to bring this case also invites suspicion. The charges were filed via a criminal complaint, a method the government uses in many investigations that must move quickly, because a complaint does not require the immediate involvement of a grand jury. The need to rush here is hard to see, given that the relevant testimony was three years ago. Conversely, it’s easy to imagine why DOJ would want to push out incendiary allegations without having to convince a potentially skeptical grand jury—an all-but-certainty in D.C., where jurors have delivered a number of high-profile rebuttals to federal prosecutors. In the next 30 days, if the department wishes to move forward with the case, it will have to seek a grand jury’s indictment. By then, though, the Trump administration may have already gotten the propaganda boost it was looking for. At a hearing today, Magistrate Judge Zia Faruqui appeared skeptical of the case, noting the government’s decision to delay seeking an indictment and describing the defendants’ “sparkling backgrounds.” As many judges have commented over the past year, the traditional “presumption of regularity” awarded to the Justice Department’s work has been eroded by the Trump administration’s habitual use of criminal prosecutions as a tool to harass the president’s enemies. With this case, DOJ has provided little material to reassure its critics.

items.title: Football guinéen : « On était tout seuls sur le chemin », le cri du cœur de SOAR Academy
items.description: À quelques jours de l’Assemblée générale élective de la Fédération guinéenne de football, SOAR Academy rappelle les difficultés des centres de formation à trouver des partenaires. Former les footballeurs de demain sans moyens suffisants reste un défi pour les académies guinéennes. Malgré ses performances et sa présence dans les différentes catégories des équipes nationales, SOAR Academy doit, elle aussi, faire face aux difficultés financières et logistiques. Lors d'un point de presse tenu ce vendredi 23 octobre 2026, son fondateur, Almamy Saidou Sylla, n’a pas caché cette réalité. « L’année dernière, par exemple, on était en compétition dans la sous-région (…) mais on était tout seuls sur le chemin », a-t-il confié. Des mots qui résument le combat quotidien de nombreuses structures de formation, souvent confrontées aux dépenses liées aux déplacements, à l’encadrement et à la progression des jeunes joueurs. « L’idée, ce n’est pas seulement le côté financier, mais c’est aussi apprendre à ces jeunes joueurs comment utiliser leur argent », explique Almamy Saidou Sylla. Du côté du partenaire, Madani Fanta Kaba, directeur général adjoint de BNB Guinée, affirme la volonté d’investir dans l’avenir de la jeunesse : « C’est vraiment accompagner la vision de M. Sylla pour investir dans le développement du football en Guinée et surtout dans le développement des jeunes Africains. » Le jeune académicien ivoirien Coulibaly Zana Boubacar espère, lui aussi, que cette initiative profitera aux générations futures. Il rappelle toutefois que le football ne doit pas faire oublier l’école : « N’oublions pas aussi l’école parce que si je suis ici aujourd’hui, c’est grâce à l’école et à mes parents. » À l’heure où le football guinéen s’apprête à renouveler ses instances dirigeantes, cette initiative pose une question essentielle : qui accompagnera durablement les académies qui forment les talents de demain ?
